recent_commits.message: Supersede sd_binary_0_n(), sd_binary_1_n(), and three mapper helpers
recent_commits.body:
* sd_binary_0_n(group_0, n) is sd_binary_groups(group_0, n - group_0),
and likewise for sd_binary_1_n().

* absorb_key_args(), check_mapper_input_colnames(), and
manage_helper_col() are for handwritten mappers, which function_map()
replaces: its mappers rename key columns, check input columns, and
manage helper columns (.cols_helper) themselves.

section on writing mappers manually says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Deprecate is_numeric_like() and the is_seq_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* is_numeric_like() served the string interface that 1.0.0 removed, and
the four sequence predicates are no longer used: the sequence mappers
record how far each value was moved in diff_var. All five are
soft-deprecated, and their messages say that they may be removed in a
future version.

* The body of is_numeric_like() is the internal numeric_like(), which
the sequence internals and the *_df() column selection call without the
warning. is_seq_dispersed() with a missing `from` called itself again,
which would have warned twice; it now calls is_seq_basic() directly,
which the second call reached anyway.

* The devtools vignette drops its section on sequence testing, and the
pkgdown index the five functions, which are keyword internal. Their
tests shadow them with quiet wrappers.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Deprecate restore_zeros(), restore_zeros_df(), and decimal_places_df()
recent_commits.body:
* The tests no longer take strings, so trailing zeros need not be put
back for them: the number of decimal places is `digits_x` or
`digits_sd`. Without a `width`, restore_zeros() guessed it from the
longest value, which is the guessing that `digits_*` replaced. For
display, formatC() does the same.

* decimal_places_df() replaced the values by their counts, while the
tests need both; decimal_places() in mutate() keeps them.

* Soft-deprecated, so only direct calls warn. The body of
restore_zeros() is now the internal pad_zeros(), which
restore_zeros_df() and debit_plot()'s labels call without the warning.

* The tests of the three functions shadow them with quiet wrappers,
since testthat resets lifecycle_verbosity in every test_that(); other
tests that used restore_zeros() as a helper use sprintf().

* The wrangling vignette drops its section on restoring zeros, and the
pkgdown index the three functions, which are keyword internal.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show in the technical notes why the tests compare whole numbers
recent_commits.body:
* A mean of 1.03 from 40 integers is consistent: 41 / 40 = 1.025 rounds
up to 1.03. In floating point, (1.03 - 0.005) * 40 is a little above 41,
so a naive test would call it inconsistent. The section now shows this
and the whole-number comparison GRIM makes instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse a data frame where values are expected, with a hint
recent_commits.body:

grim_plot_line(n = 100)`, failed on whichever check came first: a
missing `digits_x` in the line plots and explanations, and a raw "length
= 12 in coercion to logical(1)" in grim(), grim_values(), and
grim_closest().

* check_not_data_frame() runs in map_value_sets() and
check_args_given(), so it covers the tests, the values and closest
functions, percentage_of(), add_up_to(), and the *_explain() and
*_plot_line() functions. It points to the mapper where there is one,
and to one row's values or explain_print() for the single-case
functions.

recent_commits.message: repo_check: advise on private ResearchBox boxes (#621); version 0.4.3.23
recent_commits.body:
- A box linked without its passcode that ResearchBox does not show ("does not
  exist or is not public", or the web page's captcha) stays a repository that
  could not be checked, and the authors are told that readers cannot open it:
  make the box public, or link its full peer-review link.
- A box read through its peer-review link is named as private unless
  ResearchBox says it is public (without a key the status is unknown, and the
  passcode shows the link is meant for peer review); it is counted in
  repo_view_only, with private OSF projects, and the light is yellow.
- .rbox_box_meta() gives a box's licence and status from the one box_meta
  request repo_check already made for the licence; .rbox_license() uses it.

  "Private repositories checked through a view-only or peer-review link".

* Remove "Writing mappers manually" from the custom-tests vignette: it was
built on the superseded helpers, and every mapper is made by
function_map(). Keep the column order of mapper output in section 3 and
the advice on internal helpers in section 1.
* Fold section 8, on documenting audit() summaries, into sections 6 and 7.
* Drop the iris example from devtools, which repeated the trailing-zeros
point made right below it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Review the vignettes again
recent_commits.body:
* Explain the total-n output columns and the scenarios_total and hit_rate
summary columns in GRIM in depth.
* Show a handwritten vectorized wrapper, which the custom-tests vignette
recommended but never showed, and list .var among the seq factory's
defaults.
* Say what split_by_parens(transform = TRUE) does, and count decimal
places before as.numeric() after row_to_colnames().
* Name DEBIT's sd_incl_* columns, say why debit_plot() suits sequence
output poorly, and break GRIMMER in depth's overlong calls.
* Group the two custom-test vignettes and devtools as "Implementing
tests"; move wrangling, which is for users, to "Other".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Review the vignettes
recent_commits.body:
* Fix examples that showed nothing: the show_rec columns in GRIM in depth
were cut off by select(4:10); the DEBIT, total-n, and wrangling examples
were all inconsistent or had no hits.
* Show audit(.by = ), the settings header, scrutiny_meta(), zoom,
debit_closest(), and the sd_binary_*() functions.
* Point custom tests to the NA rule and to exact rounding bounds; drop a
duplicate citation key and an empty References section.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Supersede sd_binary_0_n(), sd_binary_1_n(), and three mapper helpers
recent_commits.body:
* sd_binary_0_n(group_0, n) is sd_binary_groups(group_0, n - group_0),
and likewise for sd_binary_1_n().

* absorb_key_args(), check_mapper_input_colnames(), and
manage_helper_col() are for handwritten mappers, which function_map()
replaces: its mappers rename key columns, check input columns, and
manage helper columns (.cols_helper) themselves.

* Superseded means a badge and a NEWS entry, no warning. The vignette
section on writing mappers manually says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Deprecate is_numeric_like() and the is_seq_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* is_numeric_like() served the string interface that 1.0.0 removed, and
the four sequence predicates are no longer used: the sequence mappers
record how far each value was moved in diff_var. All five are
soft-deprecated, and their messages say that they may be removed in a
future version.

* The body of is_numeric_like() is the internal numeric_like(), which
the sequence internals and the *_df() column selection call without the
warning. is_seq_dispersed() with a missing `from` called itself again,
which would have warned twice; it now calls is_seq_basic() directly,
which the second call reached anyway.

* The devtools vignette drops its section on sequence testing, and the
pkgdown index the five functions, which are keyword internal. Their
tests shadow them with quiet wrappers.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Deprecate restore_zeros(), restore_zeros_df(), and decimal_places_df()
recent_commits.body:
* The tests no longer take strings, so trailing zeros need not be put
back for them: the number of decimal places is `digits_x` or
`digits_sd`. Without a `width`, restore_zeros() guessed it from the
longest value, which is the guessing that `digits_*` replaced. For
display, formatC() does the same.

* decimal_places_df() replaced the values by their counts, while the
tests need both; decimal_places() in mutate() keeps them.

* Soft-deprecated, so only direct calls warn. The body of
restore_zeros() is now the internal pad_zeros(), which
restore_zeros_df() and debit_plot()'s labels call without the warning.

* The tests of the three functions shadow them with quiet wrappers,
since testthat resets lifecycle_verbosity in every test_that(); other
tests that used restore_zeros() as a helper use sprintf().

* The wrangling vignette drops its section on restoring zeros, and the
pkgdown index the three functions, which are keyword internal.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show in the technical notes why the tests compare whole numbers
recent_commits.body:
* A mean of 1.03 from 40 integers is consistent: 41 / 40 = 1.025 rounds
up to 1.03. In floating point, (1.03 - 0.005) * 40 is a little above 41,
so a naive test would call it inconsistent. The section now shows this
and the whole-number comparison GRIM makes instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse a data frame where values are expected, with a hint
recent_commits.body:
* Mapper output piped into a function for values, as in `out |>
grim_plot_line(n = 100)`, failed on whichever check came first: a
missing `digits_x` in the line plots and explanations, and a raw "length
= 12 in coercion to logical(1)" in grim(), grim_values(), and
grim_closest().

* check_not_data_frame() runs in map_value_sets() and
check_args_given(), so it covers the tests, the values and closest
functions, percentage_of(), add_up_to(), and the *_explain() and
*_plot_line() functions. It points to the mapper where there is one,
and to one row's values or explain_print() for the single-case
functions.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add more links to NEWS.md
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Mention only functions from before 1.0.0 as changed in NEWS.md
recent_commits.body:
* The bug fixes and breaking changes named functions that 1.0.0 adds,
such as percentage_of(), grim_values(), and the *_explain() and
*_plot_line() functions, as if they had changed. That data_type is
required by the values and line-plot functions, and "continuous" an
error there, moves to their entry under "New features".

* The seq and total-n entry gives threshold instead of the new
sd_meaning as an example of a setting once passed through the dots.

* The debit() mean_n example uses the default sample SD, not the new
sd_meaning = "sd_pop".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require R >= 4.3.0
recent_commits.body:
* About 190 test lines use the pipe placeholder in an extraction, as in
`|> _$x`, which R parses only from 4.3.0 on, so R CMD check failed on
the declared minimum of 4.1.0. CI checked no version that old.

* A CI job on R 4.3 keeps the declared minimum checked.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Summarize the changes most users will meet at the top of NEWS.md
recent_commits.body:
* A before/after example of grim_map() and grim() shows the three new
required arguments, followed by the other renames and result changes
that most users will run into. The paragraph that summarized the test
results is folded into it.

* "split a total as odd" now says what went wrong: disperse_total() and
the total-n mappers split 40 - 1e-9 into 19.5 and 20.5.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Format vignettes/technical-notes.Rmd
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reword some notes in NEWS.md
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which strings count as missing in numbers and in any text
recent_commits.body:
* Functions that read numbers from strings follow as.numeric(), which
takes "nan" and "inf" in any letter case; functions that read any text
take only "NaN" as R writes it, since "Nan" is a name. The two rules
were implicit in NON_FINITE_TOKENS and NAN_TOKENS; the comment now states
them and names the functions on each side.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return n and items_averaged as integer from the *_values() and *_closest() functions
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers return these columns as integer, but the values functions
returned doubles. bind_cases() now converts them where they fit, as the
mappers do, casts the other columns to the types of the ptype, so that a
sum from seq() is double like one from sum_range(), and the ptypes for
the zero-case output are integer for these two columns. A sample size
beyond the integer range stays double.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read an all-NA column as NA of the argument's type, and refuse a digits_* column of strings up front
recent_commits.body:
* An all-NA vector of any type, such as a logical NA or an NA_character_
column from a text file, is a missing value like any other, so
na_as_integer() reads it as NA_integer_ for the whole-number arguments,
from round_whole() and as_integer_if_lossless(), and na_as_character()
as NA_character_ for data_type (ARGS_STRING). The columns are then of
their usual type, and a character NA items_averaged column no longer
crashes grim_total() with a non-numeric argument to round().

* A digits_* column or argument of strings failed in every row, so the
per-row error blamed no row and called the column "a single whole
number". check_digits_numeric() in function_map() now refuses it up
front, naming the column or the argument and the type it has.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add the agent instructions to the repository
recent_commits.body:
* AGENTS.md documents the architecture for AI agents, and CLAUDE.md
includes it. Both were untracked although they describe themselves as
checked in.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give explain_map() dots, take out_max = "auto", and name scrutiny_meta(data)
recent_commits.body:
* The explain_map() generic and its methods take `...`, so that methods
for other classes can add arguments; scrutiny's own require them to be
empty. Adding them after the release would break such methods.

* seq_disperse() takes out_max = "auto" as no maximum, like NULL, since
the sequence mappers default to it.

* scrutiny_meta() takes `data`, like audit(), explain_map(), and the
reverse_map_*() functions.

* NEWS.md no longer says that restore_zeros() has a `sep` argument; it
has sep_in and sep_out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add debit_closest(), as grim_closest() and grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* debit_closest() returns the pair of a binary sample's mean and SD whose
SD is closest to sd: of the pairs debit_values() lists if the value set
is consistent, else of those whose mean would be reported as x, else
that of grim_closest()'s mean. Ties go by the mean closer to x, then the
smaller number of ones. The SDs come from the spread k * (n - k), so
that k and n - k tie exactly.

* check_debit_values_args() holds the checks it shares with
debit_values(). A search over every number of ones checks it on 300
random value sets per run.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return items_averaged in the *_values() and *_closest() output of GRIM and GRIMMER
recent_commits.body:
* grim_values(), grim_closest(), grimmer_values(), and grimmer_closest()
have an items_averaged column after n, as the mappers do. With more than
one item, sum is the total over all items, so that sum / n was not x and
the output could not be read on its own.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read digits_* from columns of data, and disperse each case on its own level
recent_commits.body:
* A mapper whose digits_x or digits_sd argument is left out takes it from
a column of data by that name, as it does for arguments with defaults. A
column states the decimal places as explicitly as an argument, and it
works in a pipe, where per-row values used to need `digits_x = df$col`.
The error for a missing digits_* says so.

* Sequence mappers take one digits_* value per row, from the argument or
a column, and disperse each case on its own decimal level. They required
a single value, and the parts of a table with mixed decimal places,
tested in separate calls, could not be combined with bind_rows(). A case
to disperse whose value is NA is an error.

* Total-n mappers take a digits_* column too, one value per row for both
groups, and record it in values_reported.

* reverse_map_seq() reads the step of each case from its own digits_*
value.

* The wrangling vignette counts the decimal places of each value before
converting it, rather than taking the largest count of a column for
both x and sd.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say how to fix a missing or string x, and name missing arguments in order
recent_commits.body:
* error_digits_missing() tells the story of the quotes, with the link to
the changelog, only in the exports of 0.6.1 that took strings
(EXPORTS_STRING_NUMBERS), not in new ones such as grim_values(). Its
example for a missing digits_sd shows an SD, not the mean.

* stop_string_number() says to count the decimal places with
decimal_places() and convert the string with as.numeric(). The lifecycle
message is only for strings: grim(TRUE, ...) now says that x must be
numeric, as other exports do.

* The *_explain() and *_plot_line() functions say "Need to specify `n`."
for a missing argument without a default, as grim() does, and report the
first one missing, not a missing digits_x ahead of n. check_args_given()
is the shared check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take only "NaN" as R writes it as missing in text
recent_commits.body:
* is_value_missing() no longer takes "Nan" or "nan" as missing, so that
duplicate_count() and the other readers of any text keep a name like
"Nan". "NaN", as R writes it, is still missing there, as documented.
decimal_places() and the other number readers still read any case.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check grim_plot_grid() thresholds before drawing, and hint at grouping
recent_commits.body:
* With show_data = FALSE, rounding and threshold are checked by
check_rounding_args() before mirror_rounding() does arithmetic on them,
so threshold = "4" under "up_from" says it must be a finite number
rather than failing in `10 - threshold`.

* grim_plot_grid() and debit_plot() say that dplyr::group_by() removed
the class of grouped mapper output, as audit() and explain_map() do.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give the lifecycle message for string x only in exports that took strings
recent_commits.body:
* stop_string_number() gives lifecycle's "must be numeric as of scrutiny
1.0.0" only in the exports of 0.6.1 that took x and sd as strings,
EXPORTS_STRING_NUMBERS, now including grim_total() and grim_exp_incon(),
which gave a bare type error. Exports new since then, such as
grim_values() and the *_explain() functions, say plainly that x must be
numeric and that its decimal places go in digits_x.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare grim_plot_grid() settings as methods, and require the mapper's record
recent_commits.body:
* A "ties_*" rounding is compared with the recorded one as the method it
stands for, so "ties_even" agrees with "even", and threshold only where
the recorded method reads it.
* Mapper output that has the class but not the record of its call is an
error, as in debit_plot(), rather than plotted under the defaults, which
drew percentages on the raster for means. rounding and threshold are now
only used with show_data = FALSE.
* NEWS.md says that grim_values() and grim_closest() both return a tibble
with a case column.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give the factor hint for n, thresholds, limits, and probabilities too
recent_commits.body:
* check_not_factor() is now also called by grim_plot_grid() for n, by
check_limit_n() for the n_min and n_max of disperse(), disperse2(), and
the total-n mappers, by check_rounding_args() for threshold, and by
grim_binomial() and grim_binomial_power() for alpha, p0, and p1. These
said that factor(5) "is 5".
* NEWS.md mentions the factor hint.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take "NaN" as missing in the string readers, and name a matrix's columns col1 etc.
recent_commits.body:
* is_value_missing() also takes "NaN" in any letter case as missing, as
decimal_places(), restore_zeros(), and is_numeric_like() already did, so
duplicate_*(), the parens extractors, split_by_parens(), and
row_to_colnames() agree with them. It checks each distinct string once,
which makes the duplicate_*() functions about as fast as before
is_value_missing() trimmed every value, and reads a factor by its labels.
* matrix_to_cols() names the columns of a matrix without names col1 etc.,
so that duplicate_tally() of a one-column matrix gives col1 and col1_n
again rather than value and value_n.
* split_by_parens() says "Not every value has the delim elements" under
both settings of check_delim; it said a skipped column "doesn't contain"
them even if most values did.
* The docs of the *_df() functions say that a column with no values never
causes a warning.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say in audit() that cases from other data have no record either, and expect the new messages
recent_commits.body:
* A case joined from another call's output gets the error from
2e5bd29 too, whose hint now names both causes.
* Two tests expected the messages from before 3729a5f and 2e5bd29.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: repo_check: advise on private ResearchBox boxes (#621); version 0.4.3.23
recent_commits.body:
- A box linked without its passcode that ResearchBox does not show ("does not
  exist or is not public", or the web page's captcha) stays a repository that
  could not be checked, and the authors are told that readers cannot open it:
  make the box public, or link its full peer-review link.

  request repo_check already made for the licence; .rbox_license() uses it.

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: four fixes from the BES run (#591, #594, #595, #598)
recent_commits.body:
- #598: install addresses (install_github(), install.packages("http...")) are
  read from the code without its comments: a commented-out address for
  embryogrowth, which no longer answers, was used instead of CRAN. When an
  install from GitHub or a web address fails and the package is on CRAN or
  Bioconductor, it is installed from there, with a note in version_note; a
  failed download says "could not download <address>: ...". Both install
  paths (with and without Docker).
- #594: a lib.loc with an absolute path (a folder on the authors' computer)
  is removed from library(), require(), requireNamespace() and
  loadNamespace(); $modifications records lib_loc_removed. A relative lib.loc
  stays.
- #591: a folder a script's write stopped on is made in the sandbox and the
  script runs once more, in the same loop as files placed from the deposit
  (R and Python). Only messages of a write count, not a missing input.
  $modifications records folder_made; the report says so.
- #595: the help says pip install --prefix in Docker, --target with
  sandbox = "process".

Tests: unit tests from the real cases; a run test with a lib.loc script and a
write into a folder built in a function; the fallback in both install paths
was run on a local computer. The existing test of a failed GitHub install
keeps checking its point, with the package not on CRAN there.
Version 0.4.3.21 (after #618, 0.4.3.20).

New column error_message in the R and the Python table: for a script that
did not run through, its error, at most 300 characters: the error line of the
output as the report shows it (which names a missing package), with the
address asked for when an internet failure's line names none, or the time
limit; else the last line of the output. NA for a script that ran through.
New .repro_error_message(), next to .repro_failure_reason().

The code that reads this table uses its columns by name, so a new column
changes nothing there. Tests: a unit test with 6b437_v1's message and each
kind of failure; the R and Python failing-script module tests (full mode).

recent_commits.message: data_check warns about keys in a repository; module_run() removes keys from every result (#607)
recent_commits.body:
A PsyArXiv preprint's OSF project (6qf9p_v3) held an OpenRouter key in the
survey flow of two Qualtrics surveys, as embedded data, which the export also
wrote into every response. Metacheck did not warn, and copied the key into its
saved result, which GitHub refused to store.

- R/keys.R: betterleaks' rules of high and medium confidence (427, all
  readable by R with perl = TRUE), with their filters: minimum entropy,
  patterns a key must or must not match, texts, the general placeholders, and
  path conditions. Each rule is tried only near its keywords; keywords are
  found in the unique pieces of a text; encoded data (1,000+ base64
  characters) is masked. Keys are numbered, never returned; only their first
  characters are shown.
- data_check: every downloaded file the authors wrote is searched whole (with
  code_check's downloads, and a local folder's hidden files such as .env); of
  a tabular data file the column names and first 3 rows of the table as read.
  A key turns the light red; the report gives files, lines or rows, type and
  beginning, and how to revoke it; summary column key_n, result table keys.
- module_run(): any key in a module's result is replaced by "[key removed]".
- data-raw/key_patterns.R collects the rules (RcppTOML, its literal strings
  unescaped; checked against Python's tomllib for all 474 rules) into
  inst/databases/key_patterns.Rds; betterleaks' MIT notice in inst/COPYRIGHTS.

Tested with random fake keys of 12 types, on 6qf9p_v3 itself (1 key in 4
files), and on 400 repositories of an earlier corpus run (no find from text
that is not a key, after two fixes the run showed).

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: four fixes from the BES run (#591, #594, #595, #598)
recent_commits.body:
- #598: install addresses (install_github(), install.packages("http...")) are
  read from the code without its comments: a commented-out address for
  embryogrowth, which no longer answers, was used instead of CRAN. When an
  install from GitHub or a web address fails and the package is on CRAN or
  Bioconductor, it is installed from there, with a note in version_note; a
  failed download says "could not download <address>: ...". Both install
  paths (with and without Docker).
- #594: a lib.loc with an absolute path (a folder on the authors' computer)
  is removed from library(), require(), requireNamespace() and
  loadNamespace(); $modifications records lib_loc_removed. A relative lib.loc
  stays.
- #591: a folder a script's write stopped on is made in the sandbox and the
  script runs once more, in the same loop as files placed from the deposit
  (R and Python). Only messages of a write count, not a missing input.
  $modifications records folder_made; the report says so.
- #595: the help says pip install --prefix in Docker, --target with
  sandbox = "process".

Tests: unit tests from the real cases; a run test with a lib.loc script and a
write into a folder built in a function; the fallback in both install paths
was run on a local computer. The existing test of a failed GitHub install
keeps checking its point, with the package not on CRAN there.

recent_commits.message: stat_p_exact: table notes, legends and thresholds are not flagged as imprecise (#604)
recent_commits.body:
- New .p_not_test() judges each p-value by the words of its own clause and
  returns "marker", "threshold", "legend" or NA. A p-value that a test
  statistic belongs to is never left out.
- stat_p_exact() leaves these out and keeps the reason in the new table
  column not_a_test. Before, only "*p < .05/.01/.001" was left out, and of a
  note repeated under two tables only one copy.
- Built on 11 collections (5,378 papers) and tested on 6 others (6,543
  papers): 18,377 flagged before, 13,216 now; of 300 random p-values left out
  there, none was an imprecisely reported result.
- Version 0.4.3.10.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Data check: labelled .rds columns and binary tar records no longer stop it; failed modules show the whole error
recent_commits.body:
- data_read_head() loads haven when a column is labelled. readRDS() and load()
  do not load haven, so a labelled text column (PISA country codes, jev3u_v1)
  could not be turned into text and data_check failed for the whole paper.
- .tar_pax() skips extended header records with binary values (extended
  attributes written by tar on a Mac), which gave "embedded nul in string"
  (4z75t_v1).
- A failed module's error message is escaped as HTML in the report and the
  checklist, so a part in angle brackets is no longer left out.
- Version 0.4.3.10.

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.message: Describe when grim_plot_grid() uses rounding, threshold, and an inferred digits_x
recent_commits.body:

  threshold arguments and for inferring digits_x from x, but grim_plot_grid()
  refuses anything other than mapper output, which records its settings and
  has a digits_x column. They now name show_data = FALSE and a removed
  digits_x column instead, and so does NEWS.md.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse grimmer_closest() on too many sums, and break its mean ties exactly
recent_commits.body:
* For a consistent value set, grimmer_closest() checks one sum per remainder
  modulo n against the SD, one at a time: 35 seconds for n = 9e6, where
  grimmer() takes a tenth of one. More than 100,000 such sums is an error
  now, as for grimmer() at a million. It takes an n above about
  10^(digits_x + 5).
* With no mean reported as x, it picked between two equally close sums by the
  noise in the means, so that it could disagree with grim_closest() since
  70a6159 made that one exact. Both compare whole numbers now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Order alpha after alternative in grim_binomial_power(), and keep a tiny SE
recent_commits.body:
* grim_binomial() and binom.test() take alternative before the significance
  level; grim_binomial_power() took them the other way around. Both are new
  in 1.0.0.
* The sd_binary_*() functions took the root of the product of the variance
  and the denominator ratio, which underflows for an SE at an n of about
  1e300. They take the product of the roots.
* A comment in grim_exp_incon() still said its NA cases are exactly those of
  grim().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Find tally columns by name, and name the class and cause in two errors
recent_commits.body:

  suffix as a tally column, such as one that mutate() added as extra_n.
  duplicate_tally() now records the names of its tally columns, and audit()
  reads those.
* Grouped duplicate_tally() output got only "See ?audit" since 51ce062.
  It gets the hint that group_by() removed the class again, without calling
  it mapper output.
* explain_print() on a plain data frame named the tibble class it had turned
  it into, not the class it was given.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Break ties in grim_closest() and grimmer_closest() by a stated rule
recent_commits.body:
* grim_closest() took the tie between two equally close means from round()
  on the sum, which rounds half to even, so 0.5 with n = 17 and n = 19 went
  different ways. It now compares distances as whole numbers and returns
  the smaller mean.
* grimmer_closest() picked between two equally close SDs of one sum by the
  noise in their roots. The smaller SD now wins, with the tolerance the
  comparison across sums already had.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let zoom = "medium" reach a neighbor that a limit leaves room for, or warn
recent_commits.body:
* The search for the nearest attainable values stopped at 9,999 values per
  side, even where a limit cut one side short, so the 0% row of one case
  never reached 100%. It now spends its 20,000 values on the side that has
  room for them.
* Under "medium", a row that still has no neighbor on a side gets a
  warning, as an empty row under "close" did. The docs state the limit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return a row of NA from grimmer_values() where a missing value forces TRUE

recent_commits.message: Fix a crash and the tie-break of grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* For n from 2 to 4, a sum whose remainder fails test 3 passed an NA range
to the search for attainable sums of squares, which stopped with "missing
value where TRUE/FALSE needed". Such sums are now dropped first.

by the mean closer to x, then the smaller sum: deviations are now computed
so that mirror remainders keep them equal, SDs on either side of sd within
a tolerance count as tied, and the distance to x is counted in units of
its last decimal place.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
* It mirrors debit()'s signature now, as sd_meaning does. Like
"sd_sample_or_pop" there, "mean_n" is an error: it takes the mean as
anything that would be reported as x, so there is no finite list of
values. "exact" is the default and the only value allowed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show grimmer_closest(), debit_values(), and debit_plot_line() in the vignettes
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add debit_values() and debit_plot_line()
recent_commits.body:
* debit_values() is the counterpart of grim_values() and
grimmer_values() for DEBIT: every number of ones among n binary values
whose mean and SD would be reported as x and sd, with the mean, the SD,
and the number of ones as sum. It lists actual samples, so it follows
formula = "exact", and like grimmer_values() it takes one SD premise per
call. The ones come from the range and spreads that debit_scalar()
decides by, and a brute-force test checks every number of ones by hand.

* debit_plot_line() draws the comb of SDs that debit() admits for one
value set, like grimmer_plot_line(), from 0 to 1 at its widest. It takes
formula, since it only asks debit() about each SD.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grimmer_closest()
recent_commits.body:
* The counterpart of grim_closest(): the achievable pair whose SD is
closest to sd, among the pairs reported as x and sd if the value set is
consistent, else among those whose mean is reported as x, or has the
mean grim_closest() returns. One row per value set, in the shape of
grimmer_values().

* It lists no pairs: sums with the same remainder modulo n have the same
SDs, so each remainder is tried once, with the sum of squares nearest
the target found directly for n >= 5 (vectorized) and by windowed search
through sum_squares_attainable() for fewer numbers.

* A brute-force test over all samples of 2 to 5 whole numbers checks
the distance to sd under three SD premises.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give manage_helper_col() plain argument names
recent_commits.body: * var_arg is now arg and affix is add_col, which say what they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:

written in full, without a leading space or an exponent, and reads back

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.body:

debit_plot() failed when it recomputed the bound columns. Only rows can
be read under the wrong record, so only rows are refused.

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.body:

the one that says how to convert it.

* The hint showed as.numeric(as.character(x)) with the argument's name,
which is not the column's name if a key argument renamed it, as in

recent_commits.message: Refuse rows of another mapper call that replace rows of the output
recent_commits.body:

call with other settings into rows that audit() and the others read
under this call's settings. tibble's [<- assigns column by column, so
the vctrs methods never saw it; a [<- method is now registered for
each mapper class, and rows_update(), rows_patch(), and vec_assign()
only pass plain data or rows of the same output.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give mapper output without rows the columns it has with rows
recent_commits.body:

grimmer_map() lacked reason, and a total-n mapper whose totals left no
pair of group sizes did, too. function_map() now tests a row of missing
values and takes the columns of its result, or only the key result

cols_renamed before it reads the arguments, so they are reserved names
now, too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Stop grimmer_explain() after three failures when the verdict is FALSE
recent_commits.body:

count of the ones not shown comes from the range, so it took 8 s at
n = 1e6 where grimmer() takes 0.05 s since cd30bc1.

* debit_explain() loses three branches that could not be reached.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return 0 from grim_exp_incon() for continuous data without digits_x
recent_commits.body:

so its result was NA where grim() is TRUE, contrary to ?grim_exp_incon.

* The value section of ?grim-stats said that a missing x always gives
NA, which holds for integer data only.

* NEWS.md named the smallest SD that GRIMMER refuses but not the
smaller SE, and ?grim_plot_line said that n + 1 percentages are
attainable even where fewer can be reported.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop value sets without n or items_averaged from grim_plot_grid() itself
recent_commits.body:

decided, so it reached ggplot2, which dropped it with its own vague
message. Such rows are now dropped with the warning about value sets
that have no place on the grid.

that remain, which later drops made wrong, and its plural agrees.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Find the tally columns by the suffix duplicate_tally() gave them
recent_commits.body:

dplyr error. duplicate_tally() now records colname_end in the
"scrutiny" attribute, and audit() reads it, with "n" as the fallback.

* With no tally column left, as after renaming them, audit() says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Correct the size limits of GRIMMER and two lists of NA cases in the docs
recent_commits.body:

which NEWS.md and ?grimmer left out; the technical notes now say that
the sample SD refused for two values is above about 1.05 million.

under GRIMMER and DEBIT, and ?grim_exp_incon lists a missing digits_x.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the ticks past the values in the line plots, and fix a plural

from its neighbor at each end of the axis.

recent_commits.message: Fix add_up_to_map() positions next to row names, and four mapper details
recent_commits.body:

column that a data frame's character row names become, so it tested
the wrong columns, silently: only `a` instead of `a` and `b`.

defunct string columns, as the rows are split into strings before the
basic mapper sees them. It now gets the factor message, too.

recent_commits.message: Stop grim_closest() from recursing without decimal places to go on

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Accept scrutiny's own explanation column at another console width
recent_commits.body:
* explain_print() and explain_map() compared an earlier explanation
column with a new one character by character, but the lines are wrapped
at the console width, so narrowing the console made them refuse their
own column as the user's. Whitespace is ignored now.

recent_commits.message: Leave a value set open where a missing n or SD can still decide it
recent_commits.body:
* debit() with sd_meaning = "sd_sample_or_pop" and n missing returned
FALSE when no population SD fit, though a sample SD did for some n:
debit(0.5, 0.53, NA, 2, 2, "integer", sd_meaning = "sd_sample_or_pop")
was FALSE, but TRUE with n = 8. combine_sd_sample_or_pop() only kept NA
for an n known to be above 1.

* grimmer() with items_averaged missing asked GRIM about the given n
rather than a single value, so it passed data that are all the same
where none can be: grimmer(5.4, 0, 18, 1, 1, NA, "integer") was TRUE,
but FALSE with items_averaged from 1 to 4. It also passed n = 1 under a
sample SD or SE, which leaves the case open.

* Continuous data with n missing passed any SD under "sd_pop" and
"sd_sample_or_pop", though a single value has an SD of 0; with n = 1, a
missing SD passed. Both are NA now, with explanations that say why.

* The explanation of continuous data no longer builds the one for
integers first, which the test refuses at sizes continuous data can
have, so grimmer_explain() and grim_explain() erred where the test
passed.

* Explanations: plurals with x missing, the inputs line shows a value
whose decimal count is missing as given, an SE is called an SE, and
"No n from 2 to 2" is gone.

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the second run runs only what it changes (#581)
recent_commits.body:
In 10.1111/1365-2656.13449 the second run (corrected order, added
library() lines) ran every script again: the unchanged script that had
timed out used the paper's remaining time a second time, the script that
got library() lines had none left, and the rule 'a script the second run
had no time for keeps its first result' gave it the first run's error,
the failure the added lines were meant to fix.

- The second run runs only the scripts that got library() lines or
  another script to load first, the users of the new order's edges, and
  the scripts that read what those write (not a reader that timed out in
  the first run). An unchanged script keeps its first result.
- A script of a later run (second run, old defaults, fetched file,
  written-later and placed files, Python 2; R and Python) that had no time
  left, or that the time for all scripts together stopped, is
  skipped_time_limit, not its first result: the runners mark such a stop
  with error_type 'deadline' (R, R in Docker, Python, Python in Docker),
  and .repro_later_pass() turns it into skipped_time_limit. In the first
  run such a script stays timed_out.

recent_commits.message: Download a file Dataverse converted as it was uploaded (#582)
recent_commits.body:
Dataverse's file listing gives the checksum of the original upload, while
/api/access/datafile/<id> sends the .tab Dataverse made from it, so every
converted file (an SPSS .sav, Stata .dta or .csv made into a .tab) failed
the checksum and dataverse_file_download() reported it as not downloaded.
Measured on 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND: the default download never matches; with
?format=original both files match exactly.

.dataverse_file_entry() gives the name, size and URL of a listing entry,
used by dataverse_file_download() and by repo_check's Dataverse listing: a
file with originalFileFormat gets ?format=original, originalFileSize (or
an unknown size, never the converted file's), and the listed name with the
original's extension (originalFileName as a fallback). This is the file
the authors' own code reads, and an SPSS file keeps its value labels.

GGDUND now gives Study1_June2017manuscript.sav and Study2_...sav, both
checksum_ok, with no warning, and reads as SPSS data (value labels on 8
columns); repo_check lists the same names, sizes and URLs, and
download_repo_files() fetches them. New test of the entry function;
test-archive-dataverse, test-module-repo_check and test-repo-download pass.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Download a file of unknown size with a limit instead of leaving it out (#583)
recent_commits.body:
Without a file_size column, files$file_size[idx] was NULL, so no size was
looked up and every file was left out with no record and no message; with
the column present, a file whose size the host did not give either was
dropped the same way (the early 'if (!any(cand)) next' also skipped a
repository where no size was known).

download_repo_files() now gives the table an empty file_size column for the
call (removed again at the end), and downloads a still-missing file of
unknown size with a limit: max_file_size, or what the repository's
max_download_size budget has left if that is less. The new
.download_capped() streams the file to '<dest>.part' and stops once the
limit is passed (older libcurl versions cannot stop a transfer of unknown
size, so this does not rely on curl's maximum file size). A file over its
limit is listed in 'oversize_skipped' with the bytes that had arrived, with
a message; with no budget left, 'gated' says so. Such files are fetched one
at a time, not in the parallel path.

Tested on the case from the issue (now downloaded), on another host, and
with the host's size forced unknown: under, over and without budget. The
test that expected unknown-size files to be left out now expects them
downloaded; new test of the three cases. test-repo-download,
test-module-code_check, test-module-repo_check, test-zip-peek,
test-data-checks, test-data-manifest, test-data-read,
test-archive-researchbox, test-archive-dataverse and test-fair-repo pass.

recent_commits.message: Join a streamed answer's pieces once: large files from a zip took hours (#584)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_get(), .http_range_tail() and .http_range_bytes() read their
streamed answers (req_perform_connection()) with httr2::resp_body_raw(),
which adds each 32 KB piece with c() and so copies everything read so far:
reading N MB copied about 16 N^2 MB. A 653 MB member of a zip did not finish
in three hours, and Zenodo broke off transfers of 365 and 449 MB.

.resp_body_stream_raw() reads the stream in 512 KB pieces into a list and
joins them once, and reads an answer whose body is already in memory (such
as a mocked one in the tests) with resp_body_raw() as before. A 30 MB range
of Zenodo 6864177 now arrives in 8 to 11 s, as fast as curl, with the same
bytes (md5). New test of the reader in test-zip-peek.R; test-zip-peek,
test-tar-peek, test-repo-download and test-module-code_check pass.

recent_commits.message: Fix the eight test failures the CRAN changes caused
recent_commits.body:
The full test suite (1,726 tests) gave 8 failures, all from this branch:

- Five tests called functions that are no longer exported with
  metacheck:: (.github_config, .paper_coerce, .xml_find_text,
  .xml_find1_text, .xml_read_grobid); they now use metacheck:::.
- Three checks in test-llm.R and test-module-power.R set
  metacheck.llm.cache = FALSE to get fresh answers. The CRAN changes had
  made FALSE mean "kept for this session only", so answers saved by
  earlier tests were replayed and the error and fallback under test never
  happened. llm_cache(FALSE) turns the cache off again, as before this
  branch: every call asks the model again. The default (option not set)
  still keeps answers for the session only, and llm_cache(TRUE) keeps
  them between sessions; options(metacheck.llm.cache = NULL) returns to
  the default. This corrects the sentence about llm_cache(FALSE) in the
  previous commit message; NEWS.md, the help page and its example say so.

The six affected test files now pass.

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.5: changes for a submission to CRAN
recent_commits.body:
R CMD check --as-cran (R 4.5.3, Windows, with the \donttest examples and
internet) now passes with no errors or warnings. Two notes remain: "New
submission", which CRAN gives every first submission, and one about pandoc
not being installed on the checking computer. Before this work it gave
1 error, 5 warnings and 6 notes.

Most changes follow from one CRAN rule: a package may not write files outside
R's temporary folder (tempdir()) unless the user asks for it, and may not
use the internet when it is loaded. The manual (scienceverse/metacheck_book,
issue #2) needs the changes marked [manual] below.

Where files are saved
- [manual] AI (LLM) answers are kept only for the session by default, in its
  temporary folder. llm_cache(TRUE) keeps them between sessions, in
  .metacheck_llm_cache in the working folder as before (or where
  metacheck.cache.dir or METACHECK_LLM_CACHE_DIR points). llm_cache(FALSE)
  no longer means "ask again every time"; llm_cache_clear() does that.
- [manual] rbox_file_download() and the zip files code_check opens keep their
  files in the session's temporary folder unless cache = TRUE. They always
  used the lasting cache in the working folder, even with cache = FALSE.
- metacheck_cache_info() and the *_cache_clear() functions no longer create
  empty cache folders in the working folder, and repo_cache_clear() no longer
  recreates the folder it emptied. The functions that write a cache entry now
  create the folder themselves.
- [manual] These functions no longer have a default folder, which was the
  working folder; it must now be named:
    download_to: osf_file_download(), zenodo_file_download(),
      dryad_file_download(), dataverse_file_download(),
      figshare_file_download(), reshare_file_download(),
      researchdata4tu_file_download()
    save_path: convert(), convert_bibr(), convert_grobid(), grobid_to_bibr(),
      paper_write()
    path: module_template()
    output_dir: FAIR_repo() (its copy was "<folder>_FAIR" in the working folder)
  Use "." for the working folder. Without the folder, the function stops
  with R's message 'argument "save_path" is missing, with no default'. The
  conversion functions check this before a file is sent to a server.
  convert_grobid() with several files and save_path = NULL stops instead of
  writing to the working folder.
- [manual] Without output_file, report() and report_repository() write the
  report to the session's temporary folder, and a message says where. The
  export functions export_jasp_html(), export_omv_html(), export_spv_html(),
  export_mplus_html() and export_stata_smcl_html() do the same without
  `out`, instead of writing next to their input file. Give a file name to
  keep the result. The report app's "code to repeat this" now shows
  save_path = ".".
- The log that lastlog() reads is kept in the session's temporary folder.
- [manual] The databases (FLoRA, Retraction Watch), installed modules, paper
  collections and the state folder (key problems, ResearchBox and AsPredicted
  "not found" counts) are kept in tools::R_user_dir("metacheck", "data")
  instead of rappdirs::user_data_dir("metacheck", "scienceverse"). Files in
  the old folder are not read: download the databases and install modules
  again. rappdirs is no longer needed. report_app() and osf_app() keep their
  usage counts there too; the three hosted apps are unchanged.
- tests/testthat: test-module-.R, test-fair-repo.R, test-import-grobid.R and
  test-report.R write to temporary folders; the test "null section import"
  rewrote fixtures/problems/203020.json on every run. Two unused LLM cache
  files in tests/testthat/.metacheck_llm_cache are removed, and testthat's
  _problems/ folder is ignored by git.

Internet use when the package loads
- The start-up message no longer reads metacheck's DESCRIPTION from GitHub
  to look for a newer version (it advised remotes::install_github()), and
  links to https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- The OSF token is no longer checked at load, only the first time it is used
  (.key_use() in .osf_headers(), which already did this), so loading the
  package no longer contacts the OSF or clears a refused OSF_PAT.

Converting PDFs
- [manual] convert() always tries the servers in this order, with the methods
  "auto", "bibr" and "grobid" alike: metacheck's server on SURF Research
  Cloud, the TU/e GROBID server, a GROBID on this computer (localhost:8070),
  then the public GROBID servers on Hugging Face. SURF is now also used when
  its bibr is not ready, as it then converts with its own GROBID
  (.surf_isalive() accepts grobid = "local" in /health); before, SURF was
  skipped and its GROBID never used, and with method = "grobid" it was never
  asked. A server, key or backend given to convert() is used as given.
- While bibr does not work, convert() no longer looks for a bibr on this
  computer or in the online list (.bibr_working in R/import-convert.R turns
  this back on). convert_bibr() still works when called directly. Word files
  need bibr, so they cannot be converted until then.
- pkgdown/assets/convert.json no longer lists grobid.metacheck.app, which
  does not answer, or the platform's bibr. The website must be rebuilt for
  this to take effect.
- [manual] convert_grobid() without api_url tries the TU/e server, a GROBID
  on this computer, then the Hugging Face servers, instead of stopping when
  the TU/e server does not answer. SURF is not among them, because
  convert_grobid() returns GROBID's XML and SURF returns the paper JSON.

Optional packages used without checking that they are installed
- llm(), researchdata4tu_file_download() and zenodo_upload() used withr,
  which is only suggested; without it every AI question stopped with an
  error. These calls are now written with options() or setwd() and on.exit().
- paper() used digest for the id of a paper made without one; it now uses
  tools::md5sum() on a temporary file, which gives the same id.
- methods is listed in Imports (methods::slotNames() was used).

Exports and help pages
- 24 internal functions are no longer exported (.aspredicted_info,
  .bibtype_convert, .fsd_info, .github_config, .gitlab_config, .is_paper,
  .is_paper_list, .llm_model_list_groq, .llm_ollama_native, .osf_file_data,
  .osf_headers, .osf_node_data, .osf_parent_project, .osf_preprint_data,
  .osf_reg_data, .osf_user_data, .paper_coerce, .paper_schema,
  .psycharchives_info, .rbox_info, .xml_find_text, .xml_find1_text,
  .xml_read_grobid, .xml2bib). They were marked internal, and nothing in the
  apps, the API servers, the modules or our other repositories (checked:
  surf-research-cloud, metacheck_platform_docker, tue_datamanager_check,
  metacheck_book, papers, metacheck_docker_reproducibility) calls them.
  297 functions remain exported (was 321).
- [manual] Functions the manual presents to users are no longer marked
  internal, so they appear in the help index: data_check_case_issues(),
  data_check_colname(), data_check_constant(), data_check_empty(),
  data_check_numeric_in_text(), data_check_scale_values(),
  data_check_spss_filter(), data_check_demographic(), data_col_facets(),
  data_classify_files(), data_format(), verbose() and pb().
- Every exported function has an example. CRAN asks that examples run, so:
  - examples that loaded a paper collection from GitHub (the *_links()
    functions, module_run(), paperlist(), paper_table(), paper_id(),
    ref_table(), text_expand()) use the demo papers and run offline;
  - about 105 functions without examples got one, most offline (the
    data_check_*() and data_col_*() helpers, from the manual where it had
    one; the statistics readers and writers; the repro_*() helpers);
  - examples that need the internet are wrapped in
    \donttest{ if (online("<host>")) { ... } }, so CRAN runs them only when
    the service answers, and downloads go to tempdir();
  - \dontrun{} is kept only where an example needs an API key or AI service,
    Docker, Python or RegCheck, an SPSS file, a Shiny app, an upload, or
    installs or removes modules or packages (34 pages, was 93).
- Every function's help page says what it returns (CRAN asks for \value).
  llm_max_calls(), llm_model() and osf_delay() said "NULL" but return the
  current setting.
- The print() methods for papers, paper lists, module lists, module help and
  module output return their object invisibly, as R's own print methods do,
  instead of NULL.
- [manual] demopaper("stroop_effect") is a second demo paper (the
  manuscript of Lakens/stroop_effect_paper, converted with GROBID, with its
  title, id and ORCID iD corrected), and demofile("repo") returns its
  repository, bundled in inst/extdata/stroop_effect_paper: a 30 KB copy of
  the GitHub repository (data, code, codebook, README, licence, a renv.lock
  with only the fields renv needs), without the apaquarto extension, the
  rendered PDF and the hidden files. Its analysis.qmd renders to HTML, its
  README no longer mentions the missing .Rproj file, and it says to run
  clean_data.R from the code/ folder. The GitHub repository and the
  manuscript there have William Schneider's ORCID iD (0000-0002-8393-5316,
  from the apaquarto template) instead of 0000-0002-0247-239X.
- inst/extdata also holds sample.jasp and sample.omv (copies of the test
  fixtures) for the examples of import_jasp(), import_omv(),
  read_stat_tables() and the export functions.

Problems the check reported
- Non-ASCII characters in R code are written as \uXXXX (10 files); each
  file was parsed before and after and gives the same R code.
- The Greek letter beta in .tei_table_contents's help page broke the PDF
  manual; it is written as \eqn{\beta}{beta}.
- Help-page links to internal objects without a help page are plain code
  text; repro_run_order() documents extra_edges; setNames is
  stats::setNames; text such as <word> in two help pages is code text.
- Links that the address check could not reach (OpenAlex, ResearchBox,
  osf.io/preprints/discover, localhost) are code text; moved links point to
  https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- An example line over 100 characters is split.

Package description and citation
- [manual] The Description field is a short paragraph, as CRAN asks, with
  no abbreviations and no names that need quotes.
- inst/CITATION takes the version and year from DESCRIPTION (it said
  version 0.4.0), and lists the authors without roles (it named two
  maintainers; CRAN allows one: Lisa DeBruine, as in DESCRIPTION).
- .Rbuildignore leaves out tmp_output/.
- Version 0.4.3.5, Date 2026-11-06.

Not changed, for later
- dataverse_file_download() marks every .tab file of 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND as
  damaged, even without a size limit (probably Dataverse's converted table
  file against the checksum of the original upload).
- download_repo_files() skips a file of unknown size without a message.
- The tests were changed where needed but not run.

  shows 10 values to either side of the reported one, so that the marker and
  the strip behind it stand out. comb_window() widens the window until the
  nearest attainable value on each side is in view. zoom = FALSE shows a
  whole unit, as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pass continuous data only if some data can have them
recent_commits.body:
* Continuous data used to pass before any check, so grimmer() was TRUE for
  a negative SD or a population SD other than 0 at n = 1, and all three
  tests for an n or items_averaged that describes no data.
  verdict_continuous() now decides them, and a data_type of NA gives the
  result for whole numbers only where continuous data agree.

* grimmer() checks sd_meaning before the data_type branch, so continuous
  rows no longer accept an invalid one.

* data_type must have length 1 in the *_explain() functions, and
  grim_total() rejects NULL arguments and a factor data_type.

* The explanations follow the new verdicts, and is_percentage_of()'s docs
  say x_meaning instead of percent.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require data_type in DEBIT and the GRIM statistics
recent_commits.body:
* debit(), its mappers, and debit_explain() take data_type like GRIM and
  GRIMMER; "integer" stands for the binary values 0 and 1. debit_plot()
  leaves out continuous data with a warning, via drop_continuous(),
  which grim_plot_grid() now shares.
* grim_exp_incon() and grim_total() require data_type instead of
  defaulting to "integer", like the tests.
* GRIM's old percent argument is an error that points to x_meaning: a
  deprecated() formal of the exports without dots, and a check in
  check_factory_dots() for the mappers.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require a data_type in GRIM and GRIMMER
recent_commits.body:
* data_type = "integer", "quasi-integer", or "continuous" has no
  default, like items_averaged, since the tests only apply to whole
  numbers. It is a helper column of the mappers and vectorized in grim()
  and grimmer().
* Continuous data pass, with the reason "Continuous data" in
  grimmer_map() and an exp_incon of 0. Quasi-integer data are tested as
  whole numbers with a warning once per session. A missing data_type
  gives NA unless the value set passes as whole numbers.
* grim_explain() and grimmer_explain() say what the data type does;
  grim_plot_grid() leaves out continuous data with a warning.
* Every call in the examples, vignettes, README, and tests gives it. The
  mapper oracle and the explanation sweep cover all three types and NA.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Replace GRIM's percent argument with x_meaning
recent_commits.body:
* x_meaning = c("mean", "percentage") says what x is, like
  sd_meaning in GRIMMER and DEBIT, instead of switching a conversion on.
  It is an enum resolved like sd_meaning and checked against the new
  X_MEANINGS constant.
* Applies to grim(), its three mappers, grim_explain(), grim_values(),
  grim_closest(), grim_exp_incon(), grim_total(), and grim_plot_values().
  grim_plot_grid() reads it from the recorded settings.
* grim()'s Defaults section says why "mean" is the default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain the defaults of the tests
recent_commits.body:
* grim(), grimmer(), and debit() say why rounding = "up_or_down",
  sd_meaning = "sd_sample", and formula = "exact" are the defaults, and
  when to choose another. The basic vignettes say it too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Draw attainable values as squares and leave out the others
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_values() and grimmer_plot_values() draw a square for each
  value that a sample can have instead of a tall tooth, and nothing for the
  others, so that a gap marks an inconsistency. color_incon is gone.
* The panel is a strip whose aspect ratio keeps the squares square on any
  device. The strip of the reported value's range stays within the panel.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show consistent raster cells in grey and inconsistent ones in white
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() draws the consistent cells as the panel background and
  only the inconsistent ones as white tiles; the gradient for three or more
  decimal places runs from white to raster_color accordingly.

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the second run runs only what it changes (#581)
recent_commits.body:
In 10.1111/1365-2656.13449 the second run (corrected order, added
library() lines) ran every script again: the unchanged script that had
timed out used the paper's remaining time a second time, the script that
got library() lines had none left, and the rule 'a script the second run
had no time for keeps its first result' gave it the first run's error,
the failure the added lines were meant to fix.

- The second run runs only the scripts that got library() lines or
  another script to load first, the users of the new order's edges, and
  the scripts that read what those write (not a reader that timed out in
  the first run). An unchanged script keeps its first result.
- A script of a later run (second run, old defaults, fetched file,
  written-later and placed files, Python 2; R and Python) that had no time
  left, or that the time for all scripts together stopped, is
  skipped_time_limit, not its first result: the runners mark such a stop
  with error_type 'deadline' (R, R in Docker, Python, Python in Docker),
  and .repro_later_pass() turns it into skipped_time_limit. In the first
  run such a script stays timed_out.
- The report says 'not started, or stopped early'.

Tested with the case of the issue: a.R runs longer than a script may and
b.R uses %>% only a.R loads. With time for b.R again: b.R ran_ok (the run
took 19 s instead of 39, as a.R is not run again); without: b.R
skipped_time_limit. New test of both. The test that expected the first
result to be kept now expects skipped_time_limit; two report-text tests
updated. All reproducibility_check test files pass (367 tests).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Download a file Dataverse converted as it was uploaded (#582)
recent_commits.body:
Dataverse's file listing gives the checksum of the original upload, while
/api/access/datafile/<id> sends the .tab Dataverse made from it, so every
converted file (an SPSS .sav, Stata .dta or .csv made into a .tab) failed
the checksum and dataverse_file_download() reported it as not downloaded.
Measured on 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND: the default download never matches; with
?format=original both files match exactly.

.dataverse_file_entry() gives the name, size and URL of a listing entry,
used by dataverse_file_download() and by repo_check's Dataverse listing: a
file with originalFileFormat gets ?format=original, originalFileSize (or
an unknown size, never the converted file's), and the listed name with the
original's extension (originalFileName as a fallback). This is the file
the authors' own code reads, and an SPSS file keeps its value labels.

GGDUND now gives Study1_June2017manuscript.sav and Study2_...sav, both
checksum_ok, with no warning, and reads as SPSS data (value labels on 8
columns); repo_check lists the same names, sizes and URLs, and
download_repo_files() fetches them. New test of the entry function;
test-archive-dataverse, test-module-repo_check and test-repo-download pass.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Download a file of unknown size with a limit instead of leaving it out (#583)
recent_commits.body:
Without a file_size column, files$file_size[idx] was NULL, so no size was
looked up and every file was left out with no record and no message; with
the column present, a file whose size the host did not give either was
dropped the same way (the early 'if (!any(cand)) next' also skipped a
repository where no size was known).

download_repo_files() now gives the table an empty file_size column for the
call (removed again at the end), and downloads a still-missing file of
unknown size with a limit: max_file_size, or what the repository's
max_download_size budget has left if that is less. The new
.download_capped() streams the file to '<dest>.part' and stops once the
limit is passed (older libcurl versions cannot stop a transfer of unknown
size, so this does not rely on curl's maximum file size). A file over its
limit is listed in 'oversize_skipped' with the bytes that had arrived, with
a message; with no budget left, 'gated' says so. Such files are fetched one
at a time, not in the parallel path.

Tested on the case from the issue (now downloaded), on another host, and
with the host's size forced unknown: under, over and without budget. The
test that expected unknown-size files to be left out now expects them
downloaded; new test of the three cases. test-repo-download,
test-module-code_check, test-module-repo_check, test-zip-peek,
test-data-checks, test-data-manifest, test-data-read,
test-archive-researchbox, test-archive-dataverse and test-fair-repo pass.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Join a streamed answer's pieces once: large files from a zip took hours (#584)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_get(), .http_range_tail() and .http_range_bytes() read their
streamed answers (req_perform_connection()) with httr2::resp_body_raw(),
which adds each 32 KB piece with c() and so copies everything read so far:
reading N MB copied about 16 N^2 MB. A 653 MB member of a zip did not finish
in three hours, and Zenodo broke off transfers of 365 and 449 MB.

.resp_body_stream_raw() reads the stream in 512 KB pieces into a list and
joins them once, and reads an answer whose body is already in memory (such
as a mocked one in the tests) with resp_body_raw() as before. A 30 MB range
of Zenodo 6864177 now arrives in 8 to 11 s, as fast as curl, with the same
bytes (md5). New test of the reader in test-zip-peek.R; test-zip-peek,
test-tar-peek, test-repo-download and test-module-code_check pass.

recent_commits.message: Fix the eight test failures the CRAN changes caused
recent_commits.body:
The full test suite (1,726 tests) gave 8 failures, all from this branch:

- Five tests called functions that are no longer exported with
  metacheck:: (.github_config, .paper_coerce, .xml_find_text,
  .xml_find1_text, .xml_read_grobid); they now use metacheck:::.
- Three checks in test-llm.R and test-module-power.R set
  metacheck.llm.cache = FALSE to get fresh answers. The CRAN changes had
  made FALSE mean "kept for this session only", so answers saved by
  earlier tests were replayed and the error and fallback under test never
  happened. llm_cache(FALSE) turns the cache off again, as before this
  branch: every call asks the model again. The default (option not set)
  still keeps answers for the session only, and llm_cache(TRUE) keeps
  them between sessions; options(metacheck.llm.cache = NULL) returns to
  the default. This corrects the sentence about llm_cache(FALSE) in the
  previous commit message; NEWS.md, the help page and its example say so.

The six affected test files now pass.
