recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.5: changes for a submission to CRAN
recent_commits.body:
R CMD check --as-cran (R 4.5.3, Windows, with the \donttest examples and
internet) now passes with no errors or warnings. Two notes remain: "New
submission", which CRAN gives every first submission, and one about pandoc
not being installed on the checking computer. Before this work it gave
1 error, 5 warnings and 6 notes.

Most changes follow from one CRAN rule: a package may not write files outside
R's temporary folder (tempdir()) unless the user asks for it, and may not
use the internet when it is loaded. The manual (scienceverse/metacheck_book,
issue #2) needs the changes marked [manual] below.

Where files are saved
- [manual] AI (LLM) answers are kept only for the session by default, in its
  temporary folder. llm_cache(TRUE) keeps them between sessions, in
  .metacheck_llm_cache in the working folder as before (or where
  metacheck.cache.dir or METACHECK_LLM_CACHE_DIR points). llm_cache(FALSE)
  no longer means "ask again every time"; llm_cache_clear() does that.
- [manual] rbox_file_download() and the zip files code_check opens keep their
  files in the session's temporary folder unless cache = TRUE. They always
  used the lasting cache in the working folder, even with cache = FALSE.
- metacheck_cache_info() and the *_cache_clear() functions no longer create
  empty cache folders in the working folder, and repo_cache_clear() no longer
  recreates the folder it emptied. The functions that write a cache entry now
  create the folder themselves.
- [manual] These functions no longer have a default folder, which was the
  working folder; it must now be named:
    download_to: osf_file_download(), zenodo_file_download(),
      dryad_file_download(), dataverse_file_download(),
      figshare_file_download(), reshare_file_download(),
      researchdata4tu_file_download()
    save_path: convert(), convert_bibr(), convert_grobid(), grobid_to_bibr(),
      paper_write()
    path: module_template()
    output_dir: FAIR_repo() (its copy was "<folder>_FAIR" in the working folder)
  Use "." for the working folder. Without the folder, the function stops
  with R's message 'argument "save_path" is missing, with no default'. The
  conversion functions check this before a file is sent to a server.
  convert_grobid() with several files and save_path = NULL stops instead of
  writing to the working folder.
- [manual] Without output_file, report() and report_repository() write the
  report to the session's temporary folder, and a message says where. The
  export functions export_jasp_html(), export_omv_html(), export_spv_html(),
  export_mplus_html() and export_stata_smcl_html() do the same without
  `out`, instead of writing next to their input file. Give a file name to
  keep the result. The report app's "code to repeat this" now shows
  save_path = ".".
- The log that lastlog() reads is kept in the session's temporary folder.
- [manual] The databases (FLoRA, Retraction Watch), installed modules, paper
  collections and the state folder (key problems, ResearchBox and AsPredicted
  "not found" counts) are kept in tools::R_user_dir("metacheck", "data")
  instead of rappdirs::user_data_dir("metacheck", "scienceverse"). Files in
  the old folder are not read: download the databases and install modules
  again. rappdirs is no longer needed. report_app() and osf_app() keep their
  usage counts there too; the three hosted apps are unchanged.
- tests/testthat: test-module-.R, test-fair-repo.R, test-import-grobid.R and
  test-report.R write to temporary folders; the test "null section import"
  rewrote fixtures/problems/203020.json on every run. Two unused LLM cache
  files in tests/testthat/.metacheck_llm_cache are removed, and testthat's
  _problems/ folder is ignored by git.

Internet use when the package loads
- The start-up message no longer reads metacheck's DESCRIPTION from GitHub
  to look for a newer version (it advised remotes::install_github()), and
  links to https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- The OSF token is no longer checked at load, only the first time it is used
  (.key_use() in .osf_headers(), which already did this), so loading the
  package no longer contacts the OSF or clears a refused OSF_PAT.

Converting PDFs
- [manual] convert() always tries the servers in this order, with the methods
  "auto", "bibr" and "grobid" alike: metacheck's server on SURF Research
  Cloud, the TU/e GROBID server, a GROBID on this computer (localhost:8070),
  then the public GROBID servers on Hugging Face. SURF is now also used when
  its bibr is not ready, as it then converts with its own GROBID
  (.surf_isalive() accepts grobid = "local" in /health); before, SURF was
  skipped and its GROBID never used, and with method = "grobid" it was never
  asked. A server, key or backend given to convert() is used as given.
- While bibr does not work, convert() no longer looks for a bibr on this
  computer or in the online list (.bibr_working in R/import-convert.R turns
  this back on). convert_bibr() still works when called directly. Word files
  need bibr, so they cannot be converted until then.
- pkgdown/assets/convert.json no longer lists grobid.metacheck.app, which
  does not answer, or the platform's bibr. The website must be rebuilt for
  this to take effect.
- [manual] convert_grobid() without api_url tries the TU/e server, a GROBID
  on this computer, then the Hugging Face servers, instead of stopping when
  the TU/e server does not answer. SURF is not among them, because
  convert_grobid() returns GROBID's XML and SURF returns the paper JSON.

Optional packages used without checking that they are installed
- llm(), researchdata4tu_file_download() and zenodo_upload() used withr,
  which is only suggested; without it every AI question stopped with an
  error. These calls are now written with options() or setwd() and on.exit().
- paper() used digest for the id of a paper made without one; it now uses
  tools::md5sum() on a temporary file, which gives the same id.
- methods is listed in Imports (methods::slotNames() was used).

Exports and help pages
- 24 internal functions are no longer exported (.aspredicted_info,
  .bibtype_convert, .fsd_info, .github_config, .gitlab_config, .is_paper,
  .is_paper_list, .llm_model_list_groq, .llm_ollama_native, .osf_file_data,
  .osf_headers, .osf_node_data, .osf_parent_project, .osf_preprint_data,
  .osf_reg_data, .osf_user_data, .paper_coerce, .paper_schema,
  .psycharchives_info, .rbox_info, .xml_find_text, .xml_find1_text,
  .xml_read_grobid, .xml2bib). They were marked internal, and nothing in the
  apps, the API servers, the modules or our other repositories (checked:
  surf-research-cloud, metacheck_platform_docker, tue_datamanager_check,
  metacheck_book, papers, metacheck_docker_reproducibility) calls them.
  297 functions remain exported (was 321).
- [manual] Functions the manual presents to users are no longer marked
  internal, so they appear in the help index: data_check_case_issues(),
  data_check_colname(), data_check_constant(), data_check_empty(),
  data_check_numeric_in_text(), data_check_scale_values(),
  data_check_spss_filter(), data_check_demographic(), data_col_facets(),
  data_classify_files(), data_format(), verbose() and pb().
- Every exported function has an example. CRAN asks that examples run, so:
  - examples that loaded a paper collection from GitHub (the *_links()
    functions, module_run(), paperlist(), paper_table(), paper_id(),
    ref_table(), text_expand()) use the demo papers and run offline;
  - about 105 functions without examples got one, most offline (the
    data_check_*() and data_col_*() helpers, from the manual where it had
    one; the statistics readers and writers; the repro_*() helpers);
  - examples that need the internet are wrapped in
    \donttest{ if (online("<host>")) { ... } }, so CRAN runs them only when
    the service answers, and downloads go to tempdir();
  - \dontrun{} is kept only where an example needs an API key or AI service,
    Docker, Python or RegCheck, an SPSS file, a Shiny app, an upload, or
    installs or removes modules or packages (34 pages, was 93).
- Every function's help page says what it returns (CRAN asks for \value).
  llm_max_calls(), llm_model() and osf_delay() said "NULL" but return the
  current setting.
- The print() methods for papers, paper lists, module lists, module help and
  module output return their object invisibly, as R's own print methods do,
  instead of NULL.
- [manual] demopaper("stroop_effect") is a second demo paper (the
  manuscript of Lakens/stroop_effect_paper, converted with GROBID, with its
  title, id and ORCID iD corrected), and demofile("repo") returns its
  repository, bundled in inst/extdata/stroop_effect_paper: a 30 KB copy of
  the GitHub repository (data, code, codebook, README, licence, a renv.lock
  with only the fields renv needs), without the apaquarto extension, the
  rendered PDF and the hidden files. Its analysis.qmd renders to HTML, its
  README no longer mentions the missing .Rproj file, and it says to run
  clean_data.R from the code/ folder. The GitHub repository and the
  manuscript there have William Schneider's ORCID iD (0000-0002-8393-5316,
  from the apaquarto template) instead of 0000-0002-0247-239X.
- inst/extdata also holds sample.jasp and sample.omv (copies of the test
  fixtures) for the examples of import_jasp(), import_omv(),
  read_stat_tables() and the export functions.

Problems the check reported
- Non-ASCII characters in R code are written as \uXXXX (10 files); each
  file was parsed before and after and gives the same R code.
- The Greek letter beta in .tei_table_contents's help page broke the PDF
  manual; it is written as \eqn{\beta}{beta}.
- Help-page links to internal objects without a help page are plain code
  text; repro_run_order() documents extra_edges; setNames is
  stats::setNames; text such as <word> in two help pages is code text.
- Links that the address check could not reach (OpenAlex, ResearchBox,
  osf.io/preprints/discover, localhost) are code text; moved links point to
  https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- An example line over 100 characters is split.

Package description and citation
- [manual] The Description field is a short paragraph, as CRAN asks, with
  no abbreviations and no names that need quotes.
- inst/CITATION takes the version and year from DESCRIPTION (it said
  version 0.4.0), and lists the authors without roles (it named two
  maintainers; CRAN allows one: Lisa DeBruine, as in DESCRIPTION).
- .Rbuildignore leaves out tmp_output/.
- Version 0.4.3.5, Date 2026-11-06.

Not changed, for later
- dataverse_file_download() marks every .tab file of 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND as
  damaged, even without a size limit (probably Dataverse's converted table
  file against the checksum of the original upload).
- download_repo_files() skips a file of unknown size without a message.
- The tests were changed where needed but not run.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.4: reproducibility_check fixes for #575 (work in progress)
recent_commits.body:
Fixes for the scripts that stopped on a missing file in the BES run (#575):
- a path written into a script gets the same changed name as its copy
  (a colon in a folder name)
- a file the deposit holds in another folder is copied to where a script
  looked, and the script runs again (file_placed); sf and terra errors read
- of several files with one name, the copy outside another project's folder
  is chosen; a name still ambiguous is counted, not kept as written
- a script runs again each time it stops on a new file another script wrote,
  up to five times
- an empty file the listing reports is written when the host refuses it;
  empty archive members are kept; folders of uncopied files are made
- a path inside here() counts from where here() starts
- the failure reason comes from the error that stopped the script; a program

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the second run runs only what it changes (#581)
recent_commits.body:
In 10.1111/1365-2656.13449 the second run (corrected order, added
library() lines) ran every script again: the unchanged script that had
timed out used the paper's remaining time a second time, the script that
got library() lines had none left, and the rule 'a script the second run
had no time for keeps its first result' gave it the first run's error,
the failure the added lines were meant to fix.

- The second run runs only the scripts that got library() lines or
  another script to load first, the users of the new order's edges, and
  the scripts that read what those write (not a reader that timed out in
  the first run). An unchanged script keeps its first result.
- A script of a later run (second run, old defaults, fetched file,
  written-later and placed files, Python 2; R and Python) that had no time
  left, or that the time for all scripts together stopped, is
  skipped_time_limit, not its first result: the runners mark such a stop
  with error_type 'deadline' (R, R in Docker, Python, Python in Docker),
  and .repro_later_pass() turns it into skipped_time_limit. In the first
  run such a script stays timed_out.
- The report says 'not started, or stopped early'.

Tested with the case of the issue: a.R runs longer than a script may and
b.R uses %>% only a.R loads. With time for b.R again: b.R ran_ok (the run
took 19 s instead of 39, as a.R is not run again); without: b.R
skipped_time_limit. New test of both. The test that expected the first
result to be kept now expects skipped_time_limit; two report-text tests
updated. All reproducibility_check test files pass (367 tests).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Download a file Dataverse converted as it was uploaded (#582)
recent_commits.body:
Dataverse's file listing gives the checksum of the original upload, while
/api/access/datafile/<id> sends the .tab Dataverse made from it, so every
converted file (an SPSS .sav, Stata .dta or .csv made into a .tab) failed
the checksum and dataverse_file_download() reported it as not downloaded.
Measured on 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND: the default download never matches; with
?format=original both files match exactly.

.dataverse_file_entry() gives the name, size and URL of a listing entry,
used by dataverse_file_download() and by repo_check's Dataverse listing: a
file with originalFileFormat gets ?format=original, originalFileSize (or
an unknown size, never the converted file's), and the listed name with the
original's extension (originalFileName as a fallback). This is the file
the authors' own code reads, and an SPSS file keeps its value labels.

GGDUND now gives Study1_June2017manuscript.sav and Study2_...sav, both
checksum_ok, with no warning, and reads as SPSS data (value labels on 8
columns); repo_check lists the same names, sizes and URLs, and
download_repo_files() fetches them. New test of the entry function;
test-archive-dataverse, test-module-repo_check and test-repo-download pass.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Download a file of unknown size with a limit instead of leaving it out (#583)
recent_commits.body:
Without a file_size column, files$file_size[idx] was NULL, so no size was
looked up and every file was left out with no record and no message; with
the column present, a file whose size the host did not give either was
dropped the same way (the early 'if (!any(cand)) next' also skipped a
repository where no size was known).

download_repo_files() now gives the table an empty file_size column for the
call (removed again at the end), and downloads a still-missing file of
unknown size with a limit: max_file_size, or what the repository's
max_download_size budget has left if that is less. The new
.download_capped() streams the file to '<dest>.part' and stops once the
limit is passed (older libcurl versions cannot stop a transfer of unknown
size, so this does not rely on curl's maximum file size). A file over its
limit is listed in 'oversize_skipped' with the bytes that had arrived, with
a message; with no budget left, 'gated' says so. Such files are fetched one
at a time, not in the parallel path.

Tested on the case from the issue (now downloaded), on another host, and
with the host's size forced unknown: under, over and without budget. The
test that expected unknown-size files to be left out now expects them
downloaded; new test of the three cases. test-repo-download,
test-module-code_check, test-module-repo_check, test-zip-peek,
test-data-checks, test-data-manifest, test-data-read,
test-archive-researchbox, test-archive-dataverse and test-fair-repo pass.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Join a streamed answer's pieces once: large files from a zip took hours (#584)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_get(), .http_range_tail() and .http_range_bytes() read their
streamed answers (req_perform_connection()) with httr2::resp_body_raw(),
which adds each 32 KB piece with c() and so copies everything read so far:
reading N MB copied about 16 N^2 MB. A 653 MB member of a zip did not finish
in three hours, and Zenodo broke off transfers of 365 and 449 MB.

.resp_body_stream_raw() reads the stream in 512 KB pieces into a list and
joins them once, and reads an answer whose body is already in memory (such
as a mocked one in the tests) with resp_body_raw() as before. A 30 MB range
of Zenodo 6864177 now arrives in 8 to 11 s, as fast as curl, with the same
bytes (md5). New test of the reader in test-zip-peek.R; test-zip-peek,
test-tar-peek, test-repo-download and test-module-code_check pass.

recent_commits.message: Fix the eight test failures the CRAN changes caused
recent_commits.body:
The full test suite (1,726 tests) gave 8 failures, all from this branch:

  metacheck:: (.github_config, .paper_coerce, .xml_find_text,

  branch: every call asks the model again. The default (option not set)
  still keeps answers for the session only, and llm_cache(TRUE) keeps
  them between sessions; options(metacheck.llm.cache = NULL) returns to
  the default. This corrects the sentence about llm_cache(FALSE) in the

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.5: changes for a submission to CRAN
recent_commits.body:
R CMD check --as-cran (R 4.5.3, Windows, with the \donttest examples and
internet) now passes with no errors or warnings. Two notes remain: "New
submission", which CRAN gives every first submission, and one about pandoc
not being installed on the checking computer. Before this work it gave
1 error, 5 warnings and 6 notes.

Most changes follow from one CRAN rule: a package may not write files outside
R's temporary folder (tempdir()) unless the user asks for it, and may not
use the internet when it is loaded. The manual (scienceverse/metacheck_book,
issue #2) needs the changes marked [manual] below.

Where files are saved
- [manual] AI (LLM) answers are kept only for the session by default, in its
  temporary folder. llm_cache(TRUE) keeps them between sessions, in
  .metacheck_llm_cache in the working folder as before (or where
  metacheck.cache.dir or METACHECK_LLM_CACHE_DIR points). llm_cache(FALSE)
  no longer means "ask again every time"; llm_cache_clear() does that.
- [manual] rbox_file_download() and the zip files code_check opens keep their
  files in the session's temporary folder unless cache = TRUE. They always
  used the lasting cache in the working folder, even with cache = FALSE.
- metacheck_cache_info() and the *_cache_clear() functions no longer create
  empty cache folders in the working folder, and repo_cache_clear() no longer
  recreates the folder it emptied. The functions that write a cache entry now
  create the folder themselves.
- [manual] These functions no longer have a default folder, which was the
  working folder; it must now be named:
    download_to: osf_file_download(), zenodo_file_download(),
      dryad_file_download(), dataverse_file_download(),
      figshare_file_download(), reshare_file_download(),
      researchdata4tu_file_download()
    save_path: convert(), convert_bibr(), convert_grobid(), grobid_to_bibr(),
      paper_write()
    path: module_template()
    output_dir: FAIR_repo() (its copy was "<folder>_FAIR" in the working folder)
  Use "." for the working folder. Without the folder, the function stops
  with R's message 'argument "save_path" is missing, with no default'. The
  conversion functions check this before a file is sent to a server.
  convert_grobid() with several files and save_path = NULL stops instead of
  writing to the working folder.
- [manual] Without output_file, report() and report_repository() write the
  report to the session's temporary folder, and a message says where. The
  export functions export_jasp_html(), export_omv_html(), export_spv_html(),
  export_mplus_html() and export_stata_smcl_html() do the same without
  `out`, instead of writing next to their input file. Give a file name to
  keep the result. The report app's "code to repeat this" now shows
  save_path = ".".
- The log that lastlog() reads is kept in the session's temporary folder.
- [manual] The databases (FLoRA, Retraction Watch), installed modules, paper
  collections and the state folder (key problems, ResearchBox and AsPredicted
  "not found" counts) are kept in tools::R_user_dir("metacheck", "data")
  instead of rappdirs::user_data_dir("metacheck", "scienceverse"). Files in
  the old folder are not read: download the databases and install modules
  again. rappdirs is no longer needed. report_app() and osf_app() keep their
  usage counts there too; the three hosted apps are unchanged.
- tests/testthat: test-module-.R, test-fair-repo.R, test-import-grobid.R and
  test-report.R write to temporary folders; the test "null section import"
  rewrote fixtures/problems/203020.json on every run. Two unused LLM cache
  files in tests/testthat/.metacheck_llm_cache are removed, and testthat's
  _problems/ folder is ignored by git.

Internet use when the package loads
- The start-up message no longer reads metacheck's DESCRIPTION from GitHub
  to look for a newer version (it advised remotes::install_github()), and
  links to https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- The OSF token is no longer checked at load, only the first time it is used
  (.key_use() in .osf_headers(), which already did this), so loading the
  package no longer contacts the OSF or clears a refused OSF_PAT.

Converting PDFs
- [manual] convert() always tries the servers in this order, with the methods
  "auto", "bibr" and "grobid" alike: metacheck's server on SURF Research
  Cloud, the TU/e GROBID server, a GROBID on this computer (localhost:8070),
  then the public GROBID servers on Hugging Face. SURF is now also used when
  its bibr is not ready, as it then converts with its own GROBID
  (.surf_isalive() accepts grobid = "local" in /health); before, SURF was
  skipped and its GROBID never used, and with method = "grobid" it was never
  asked. A server, key or backend given to convert() is used as given.
- While bibr does not work, convert() no longer looks for a bibr on this
  computer or in the online list (.bibr_working in R/import-convert.R turns
  this back on). convert_bibr() still works when called directly. Word files
  need bibr, so they cannot be converted until then.
- pkgdown/assets/convert.json no longer lists grobid.metacheck.app, which
  does not answer, or the platform's bibr. The website must be rebuilt for
  this to take effect.
- [manual] convert_grobid() without api_url tries the TU/e server, a GROBID
  on this computer, then the Hugging Face servers, instead of stopping when
  the TU/e server does not answer. SURF is not among them, because
  convert_grobid() returns GROBID's XML and SURF returns the paper JSON.

Optional packages used without checking that they are installed
- llm(), researchdata4tu_file_download() and zenodo_upload() used withr,
  which is only suggested; without it every AI question stopped with an
  error. These calls are now written with options() or setwd() and on.exit().
- paper() used digest for the id of a paper made without one; it now uses
  tools::md5sum() on a temporary file, which gives the same id.
- methods is listed in Imports (methods::slotNames() was used).

Exports and help pages
- 24 internal functions are no longer exported (.aspredicted_info,
  .bibtype_convert, .fsd_info, .github_config, .gitlab_config, .is_paper,
  .is_paper_list, .llm_model_list_groq, .llm_ollama_native, .osf_file_data,
  .osf_headers, .osf_node_data, .osf_parent_project, .osf_preprint_data,
  .osf_reg_data, .osf_user_data, .paper_coerce, .paper_schema,
  .psycharchives_info, .rbox_info, .xml_find_text, .xml_find1_text,
  .xml_read_grobid, .xml2bib). They were marked internal, and nothing in the
  apps, the API servers, the modules or our other repositories (checked:
  surf-research-cloud, metacheck_platform_docker, tue_datamanager_check,
  metacheck_book, papers, metacheck_docker_reproducibility) calls them.
  297 functions remain exported (was 321).
- [manual] Functions the manual presents to users are no longer marked
  internal, so they appear in the help index: data_check_case_issues(),
  data_check_colname(), data_check_constant(), data_check_empty(),
  data_check_numeric_in_text(), data_check_scale_values(),
  data_check_spss_filter(), data_check_demographic(), data_col_facets(),
  data_classify_files(), data_format(), verbose() and pb().
- Every exported function has an example. CRAN asks that examples run, so:
  - examples that loaded a paper collection from GitHub (the *_links()
    functions, module_run(), paperlist(), paper_table(), paper_id(),
    ref_table(), text_expand()) use the demo papers and run offline;
  - about 105 functions without examples got one, most offline (the
    data_check_*() and data_col_*() helpers, from the manual where it had
    one; the statistics readers and writers; the repro_*() helpers);
  - examples that need the internet are wrapped in
    \donttest{ if (online("<host>")) { ... } }, so CRAN runs them only when
    the service answers, and downloads go to tempdir();
  - \dontrun{} is kept only where an example needs an API key or AI service,
    Docker, Python or RegCheck, an SPSS file, a Shiny app, an upload, or
    installs or removes modules or packages (34 pages, was 93).
- Every function's help page says what it returns (CRAN asks for \value).
  llm_max_calls(), llm_model() and osf_delay() said "NULL" but return the
  current setting.
- The print() methods for papers, paper lists, module lists, module help and
  module output return their object invisibly, as R's own print methods do,
  instead of NULL.
- [manual] demopaper("stroop_effect") is a second demo paper (the
  manuscript of Lakens/stroop_effect_paper, converted with GROBID, with its
  title, id and ORCID iD corrected), and demofile("repo") returns its
  repository, bundled in inst/extdata/stroop_effect_paper: a 30 KB copy of
  the GitHub repository (data, code, codebook, README, licence, a renv.lock
  with only the fields renv needs), without the apaquarto extension, the
  rendered PDF and the hidden files. Its analysis.qmd renders to HTML, its
  README no longer mentions the missing .Rproj file, and it says to run
  clean_data.R from the code/ folder. The GitHub repository and the
  manuscript there have William Schneider's ORCID iD (0000-0002-8393-5316,
  from the apaquarto template) instead of 0000-0002-0247-239X.
- inst/extdata also holds sample.jasp and sample.omv (copies of the test
  fixtures) for the examples of import_jasp(), import_omv(),
  read_stat_tables() and the export functions.

Problems the check reported
- Non-ASCII characters in R code are written as \uXXXX (10 files); each
  file was parsed before and after and gives the same R code.
- The Greek letter beta in .tei_table_contents's help page broke the PDF
  manual; it is written as \eqn{\beta}{beta}.
- Help-page links to internal objects without a help page are plain code
  text; repro_run_order() documents extra_edges; setNames is
  stats::setNames; text such as <word> in two help pages is code text.
- Links that the address check could not reach (OpenAlex, ResearchBox,
  osf.io/preprints/discover, localhost) are code text; moved links point to
  https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/.
- An example line over 100 characters is split.

Package description and citation
- [manual] The Description field is a short paragraph, as CRAN asks, with
  no abbreviations and no names that need quotes.
- inst/CITATION takes the version and year from DESCRIPTION (it said
  version 0.4.0), and lists the authors without roles (it named two
  maintainers; CRAN allows one: Lisa DeBruine, as in DESCRIPTION).
- .Rbuildignore leaves out tmp_output/.
- Version 0.4.3.5, Date 2026-11-06.

Not changed, for later
- dataverse_file_download() marks every .tab file of 10.7910/DVN/GGDUND as
  damaged, even without a size limit (probably Dataverse's converted table
  file against the checksum of the original upload).
- download_repo_files() skips a file of unknown size without a message.
- The tests were changed where needed but not run.

places), and paper_write() makes a new folder before asking for its
full path.

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the threshold's scale once per value set
recent_commits.body:
* grim_scalar(), grimmer_scalar(), and debit_scalar() called
  rounding_scale() two or three times per row, and grim_scalar() called
  check_sum_range_exact() for every row; together with the flag check, the
  exactness checks of this release made grim() about 40% slower. The scale
  is now computed once, and the sum check is inlined, calling the function
  only for the error. grim() takes 0.25 s for 10,000 value sets, against
  0.30 s before and 0.21 s before the checks.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: State the size limits in the help pages instead of NEWS
recent_commits.body:
* The limits on significant digits and sums were only in NEWS, where the
  "Numeric inputs" bullet quoted their formulas. ?grim now states them,
  ?grimmer and ?debit say what they refuse beyond, and NEWS points there.
  The GRIMMER limit for n from 2 to 4 is the new one, about 3e5; the old
  "4.7e7 to 6.7e7" had only held for sd_sample.

* ?seq_disperse said dispersion "can be any numeric vector"; it takes
  non-negative whole numbers, and drops zeros and repeats.

* A NEWS line described a missing string by the development state before
  it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Abort in big() for a negative or infinite input
recent_commits.body:
* floor(x / 2^24) never reaches 0 for either, so big() would loop forever.
  No caller passes one today; this makes a future one an internal error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let empty data frames bind to mapper output, and reject added rows in the audits
recent_commits.body:
* bind_rows(out, tibble(x = numeric())) was an error, though it adds no
  rows. vec_rbind() passes the vec_ptype2() methods prototypes without
  rows, so a plain data frame is now only rejected when it is cast, which
  skips inputs without rows. Two mapper outputs are still compared in
  vec_ptype2(), where the error names both arguments.

* full_join() and rbind() add rows that the vctrs methods never see, and
  audit_seq() then read them under the first call's verdicts, as NA for a
  case beyond its record. audit_seq() and audit_total_n() now reject any
  case or group with more rows than the call recorded. Basic mapper output
  records no rows, so joins remain uncovered there; NEWS says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write the bounds of the mean and the number of ones in full in debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* The product of n and a bound of the mean was printed as a double rounded
  to 15 digits, so debit_explain(0, 0.3, 899999999999999, 0, 1) said
  "0.5 * 899999999999999 = 450000000000000" next to a range ending at
  449999999999999. The bound itself was rounded to four places, as 0.0222
  for 0.02225. Both are now written out exactly from the numerators.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Prune GRIMMER's remainders with the mean known, and refuse large SDs below n = 5 sooner
recent_commits.body:
* With the mean known, the sums can cover every remainder modulo n, as
  with digits_x = 0, and then GRIMMER tried all of them:
  grimmer(5, 0.0001, 999999, 0, 4, 1) took 19 s. The pruning of remainders
  out of the SD's reach, until now only applied with the mean unknown, now
  applies there too, and the case takes 0.08 s. 211,200 small-n
  brute-force cases and 6,000 random cases with n up to 5000 get the same
  verdicts as before.

* For n from 2 to 4, sums of squares from 2^40 on are refused, rather than
  from 2^52 or 2^53: deciding them took seconds and gigabytes for n = 3,
  13 s and 5.4 GB at an SD of 4.7e7. This rules out SDs of about 3e5 to 1e6,
  depending on n and sd_meaning, which no study reports for so few values.

* The too-large-n error writes n and the count in full, not as 2e+06.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Call .cols_derived functions once per mapper call, not once per row
recent_commits.body:
* grim_map() spent about three quarters of its time calling
  grim_exp_incon() row by row, 1.2 s of 1.6 s for 10,000 rows. The function
  is vectorized, and called once on the columns, it gives the same values;
  grim_map() now takes 0.36 s for those rows.

* .cols_derived is new in 1.0.0, so its contract changes without a
  deprecation: each function is vectorized, and a .reported_variadic
  argument comes as a list of each row's values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Judge logical() like numeric() in is_seq_*() and use a repeated row once
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(logical()) was FALSE where is_seq_linear(numeric()) is
  TRUE; an empty logical vector is how R writes an empty vector of no type.

* row_to_colnames(row = c(1, 1)) pasted the row to itself, as in "x x".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Raise scrutiny's own errors for list-columns, unnamed columns, and a list from
recent_commits.body:
* duplicate_count() failed in sort.int() on a list-column, and
  duplicate_tally() and duplicate_count_colpair() compared its elements as
  deparsed strings such as "1:3". All three now reject list-columns.

* duplicate_count_colpair() names unnamed columns by position, as the other
  duplicate_*() functions do; tibble rejected them.

* seq_disperse(from = list(1)) failed in is.finite().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a name repeated in constant
recent_commits.body:
* disperse(), disperse2(), disperse_total(), and the total-n mappers kept
  only the last of the columns that a repeated name in `constant` gave.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse group sizes and dispersed values from 2^52 on
recent_commits.body:
* disperse2() took the mean of its two n values before any check, and from
  2^52 on that rounded the half away, so c(2^52 + 1, 2^52 + 2) gave wrong
  group sizes. All three disperse*() functions now refuse group sizes from
  2^52 on, one limit in place of 2^52 for halves and 2^53 for whole numbers.

* seq_disperse() checked decimal values against 2^53 units of their last
  place, where a double's spacing has long passed a unit, so
  "80000000000000.01" gave repeated values off the decimal grid. The limit
  is now 2^52 units, and the units are counted without dividing by `by`,
  which reported Inf for a tiny one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave hits unknown in audit_total_n() that an undecided split might add to
recent_commits.body:
* A split whose both_consistent is NA might be a hit, so the hits of its
  direction and the total are NA, as audit_seq() has had it since 6f0f1b5.
  They were counted as misses.

* The audit sections of the sequence and total-n mappers now say that
  removed rows, as by filter(), make a count NA too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Narrow the tolerance floor of is_seq_*() to two units in the last place
recent_commits.body:
* The floor of 8 * eps times the largest value, from 8306180, merged steps
  one unit apart in the 15th significant digit, so that
  is_seq_linear(c(9e14, 9e14 + 1, 9e14 + 3)) was TRUE. Steps and centers are
  off by at most two units in the last place, and such a step is at least
  4.5 of them. 30,000 generated sequences with 10 to 15 significant digits
  are now all judged right, linear and not.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take n as a double in GRIMMER's candidate sums
recent_commits.body:
* With an integer n, as from read.csv(), the shift q * (s + r) overflowed
  once the mean was large, so grimmer_explain(), grimmer_values(), and
  explain_map() failed with a missing value where TRUE/FALSE was needed, and
  grimmer() warned. The verdict was unaffected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Replace stray `ifelse()`s by `dplyr::if_else()`
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let columns be added to mapper output again
recent_commits.body:
* Since a67f24d, bind_cols(), tidyr::nest(), and group_modify() on mapper
  output failed with "Can't combine mapper output with other data":
  vec_cbind() asks the same vec_ptype2() methods for the type of its inputs,
  which it passes without columns. Only rows can be read under the wrong
  record, so the guard now skips inputs without columns, and casts of inputs
  without rows, as in bind_rows(out, tibble()).
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
- PWD is set to the run folder: Hydra/OmegaConf ${oc.env:PWD} stopped
  three scripts of 10.1111/2041-210X.14007.
- A Python script finds the repository's modules that the files it imports
  need (14007: run.py -> run_NNs -> fluxrgnn).
- A script that stopped on a Git LFS pointer with no file in the deposit

recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run again after a later write, keep data files, programs needing arguments, R_LIBS (#568)
recent_commits.body:
- A script that stopped on a file another script wrote later (at a new path)
  runs once more, after the file is copied to where it looked when it was
  written in another folder (10.1111/2041-210X.13814, 13923).
- A file that is not text, such as R data saved as .R, is not_r_content and
  is never written over (13897: load() failed with bad restore file magic
  number).
- A program that stopped for want of its command-line arguments is
  needs_a_person (19 scripts in 5 papers).
- R_LIBS is set in Docker, so R processes a script starts find the run's
  packages (13910: gbm's cross-validation workers).

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: install only for files that run; find named files fast (#568)

installs. .repro_named_files() looked for every listed file in all of the
code; it now looks only for the files still to fetch, among the code's words
(more than 4 minutes without ending in 10.1111/2041-210X.13798).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Prune GRIMMER's remainders with the mean known, and refuse large SDs below n = 5 sooner

  with digits_x = 0, and then GRIMMER tried all of them:
  grimmer(5, 0.0001, 999999, 0, 4, 1) took 19 s. The pruning of remainders
  out of the SD's reach, until now only applied with the mean unknown, now
  applies there too, and the case takes 0.08 s. 211,200 small-n
  brute-force cases and 6,000 random cases with n up to 5000 get the same
  verdicts as before.

  from 2^52 or 2^53: deciding them took seconds and gigabytes for n = 3,
  13 s and 5.4 GB at an SD of 4.7e7. This rules out SDs of about 3e5 to 1e6,
  depending on n and sd_meaning, which no study reports for so few values.

* The too-large-n error writes n and the count in full, not as 2e+06.

  grim_map() now takes 0.36 s for those rows.

  deprecation: each function is vectorized, and a .reported_variadic

recent_commits.body:

  and verdicts element by element for every pair, which took 4 times as long

  identical() recognizes at once.

recent_commits.message: Update the stated limits of GRIMMER

recent_commits.message: Count exactly in grim_total() where the products pass 2^53
recent_commits.body:

  was below 2^53 itself. Those elements now go through

recent_commits.message: Take gcd()'s steps with a large quotient in big numbers
recent_commits.body:

  loss of accuracy, which it can really lose where long doubles are no wider
  than doubles, as on arm64. Such a step is now exact.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show DEBIT's products exactly in debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Past 2^53, n * (n - 1) and the denominators were printed as doubles,
  which show a neighbor of the true number, and the largest or smallest SD
  was picked among spreads that doubles tie, naming the wrong k. The k is
  now picked by its distance from n / 2, and the products are written out
  with the exact whole-number helpers.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
recent_commits.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: file names after the call, Windows paths, R's old defaults, files at the top (#568)
recent_commits.body: A file name on the line after its call is found (code_file_refs, repro_file_io). Quoted Windows paths get / before the run. A script that stops on text not read as factors (R before 4.0) or on Latin-1 data runs again with that default, as do the scripts waiting for its files. A path naming a file at the top as it is there counts from where the script runs. tidyhydat's database counts as needing the internet.

recent_commits.body: A script that stopped on a file the deposit holds but that was not downloaded, mostly one over max_file_size, gets the outcome not_downloaded, is left out of the counted scripts and is counted in summary_table$repro_not_downloaded_n. pip installs inside the container and the result is copied to the library folder, since pip's own move copied permissions an exFAT drive refuses.

recent_commits.body: Found in the corpus run: 10.1111/1365-2664.14541 (name_in_code logical vs character) and 10.1111/2041-210X.13721 (invalid multibyte string in Latin-1 scripts).

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: counts per paper in summary_table; packages found nowhere (#568, item 24; #389)
recent_commits.body:
summary_table gives, for each paper, the scripts with a result of their own
(repro_scripts_n), the software files not run because they are not part of the
analysis (repro_not_analysis_n), and for each reason in the reason column how
many scripts did not run through for it (repro_fail_file, repro_fail_package and
so on). A corpus can now be counted from summary_table alone.

A package the Docker install finds in none of the places it looks (Bioconductor,
the CRAN Archive, the list of known places, R-universe) gets the install category
source_unknown. The report names it, since the code does not say where it comes
from, and the checklist says so for the script that needs it. A failed search of
R-universe is reported as a failed search, and the search now works in a bare
rocker/r-ver image, which lacked jsonlite: there it always failed, which looked
like a package R-universe lacks. Tried in both images: ecodeal is found nowhere,
and weathercan installs from the CRAN Archive.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: link the pipeline behind the paper's results; notebooks are not imported (#568)
recent_commits.body:
A file of software that nothing names, but that the analysis depends on, runs
too: in the same repository, a script that runs reads a file it writes, sources
or imports it; it reads a file such a script writes; or it runs a script linked
to the paper; along the whole chain. A name built from a pattern
("{metric}_per_hour.csv") matches the names it stands for. In the corpus this
links four FluxRGNN scripts that train the models and choose their settings, and
nothing else. The new paper_link column of table says what links each file of
software that runs to the paper's results, in words.

A Jupyter notebook is no longer taken as imported: `import audio` named a
package's module, and a tutorial notebook audio.ipynb got run_by_import and was
never run. Only .py files can be imported.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run software files only when linked to the paper; rgdal again (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Inside software (a package, application or copied tool), a script runs only when
something links it to the paper's results: the paper names it or an appendix it
names, it names the paper's figures or tables or writes a file named after one, a
README names it next to a figure or table, or it reads data deposited with the
paper outside the software. Otherwise it is not_analysis, with the reason. Trinity's
generated scripts that read the paper's data, and a package run by a workflow
(Snakefile, _targets.R, make.R), are the paper's analysis.

rgdal, rgeos and maptools install again from the CRAN Archive when the image has the
GDAL and GEOS header files: sp 2.1-4, the last version with sp.h, is installed first.
A script that crashes R in compiled code gets the reason environment.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run the authors' folders, fetch what the code needs, the internet, software files (#568)
recent_commits.body:
The code always runs in the repository as the authors organised it; the layout
argument is gone. A path that works nowhere is pointed to the one file with that
name in the repository, and the report lists it so the authors can change it. A
path to a file that exists nowhere is a missing input again.

When the code will run, the first module that downloads also fetches what the run
needs, in one request to each host; GitHub, GitLab and Dryad archives are kept
whole. Before the run a file the code names is fetched, and after the run a file
a script could not open is fetched and that script runs again.

A new argument, internet (off by default), lets scripts use the internet within
the download limits, checked every two seconds. A first rule marks files that
belong to software (package code, tests, documentation, generated files, web
applications, copied tools) as not_analysis. The option metacheck.docker_image_py
selects the large Python image with torch. Four functions no longer undo their
own clean-up with a later on.exit() without add = TRUE.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the install's second pass reaches more packages (#568, items 9, 14)
recent_commits.body:
A package on CRAN that needs one from Bioconductor gets it (speaq needs
MassSpecWavelet). Old packages compile: the warning this R treats as an error is
allowed in this pass, and Calloc() and the like, which R has dropped, map to their
current names, so maptools installs. What stopped a package is kept in its message.
rgdal and rgeos, withdrawn from CRAN in 2023, still do not install.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Divide each count by n before multiplying in sd_binary_*()
recent_commits.body:
* n^2 overflowed to Inf from about 1e154, so sd_binary_0_n(3, 1e300)
was 0 rather than the tiny SD it is. The variance is now
(group_0 / n) * (group_1 / n).
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rule out a dispersed sequence with a known infinity
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_dispersed(c(Inf, 1, NA), from = 1, test_linear = FALSE) was NA,
but no number is centered with an infinity on a finite from, nor is an
infinite from the center of any sequence. The same held with a missing
from. With test_linear = TRUE, the linear test already said FALSE.
* is_seq_dispersed(c(1, Inf, 2), from = Inf, test_linear = FALSE) failed
with a base R error: near(Inf, Inf) is NA. This predates the audit fixes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check test_linear and tolerance in the is_seq_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* A missing tolerance made every comparison NA, so every sequence was
not linear, and a missing test_linear failed in if () with a base R
error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject an infinite by in seq_disperse()
recent_commits.body:
* by = Inf passed the check for a positive number and gave a sequence of
NAs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the type of n in the total-n mappers
recent_commits.body:
* A string or factor n column reached is_whole_number() or round() and
failed in base R, where the basic and seq tiers give a type error. The
total-n tier now gives the same one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Handle NULL and string by-row arguments in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* A by-row argument left at a NULL default has no column, but the output
was assembled as if it had one, so it got a column named NA.
* A by-row argument that is both an argument and a column of data was
checked for agreement as numbers, so two different strings both became
NA, agreed, and the column was silently replaced, with two coercion
warnings. Values that are not both numbers are now compared as text, in
the new values_agree().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reserve every name function_map() assigns before reading arguments
recent_commits.body:
* enum_defaults and enum_vals are assigned before the arguments are read,
and cols_tested, col_variadic, arg_given, and vals before the by-row
arguments are checked for missingness, but none was reserved, so an
argument of .fn by one of these names was silently shadowed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record the reported columns for reverse_map_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* It took the columns before n to be the statistics reported for both
groups, so a custom basic mapper with n first rebuilt n1 and n2, and one
with n in the middle lost the columns after it; audit_total_n() inherited
both. Total-n output now records its .reported as the reported element of
the "scrutiny" attribute, which reverse_map_total_n() reads.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the width that restore_zeros() pads to
recent_commits.body:
* A width beyond what strrep() can build, such as 1e10, made it return NA
for the zeros, which was pasted into "1.5NA". width is now capped at
WRITTEN_OUT_MAX, the limit for written-out exponents.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round a tied SD both ways in debit(formula = "mean_n") under "even"
recent_commits.body:
* The bounds of "even" include both ties, so "exact" accepts an SD of 0.3
for a reconstructed SD of exactly 0.25, but "mean_n" rerounded that SD
to 0.2 only and rejected it, against its documented role as the looser
test. A tie is now rounded both ways, as "up_or_down" does. Swept over
every rounding method and sd_meaning: "mean_n" never rejects what
"exact" accepts.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rule out sequences whose missing values would have to pass an infinity
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(c(1, Inf, NA), test_linear = FALSE) was NA, but no
number comes after Inf; the same held for a leading NA before -Inf and
the mirror cases in is_seq_descending(). The known values are now padded
at a missing end with the infinity it would have to pass.
* is_seq_linear(c(Inf, NA, NA)) was NA, but an infinity among more than
two values is never linear, also when it is the only known one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from grim() for a character NA as x
recent_commits.body:
* grim_scalar() divided or multiplied x before its check for an
undecidable case, so a character NA failed in base R in grim(),
grim_explain(), and grim_map(). The check now comes first and takes any
non-finite x as undecidable, as the other tests do.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep integer counts from overflowing in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* group_0 * group_1 was an integer product, so counts from about 46,341
each gave NA, with the overflow warning suppressed along with sqrt()'s.
The counts are now doubles.
* An infinite or NaN count, n, or mean gave NaN rather than the
documented NA: which() skipped the NA that the whole-number test
returned for them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare near-whole n_min and n_max as whole numbers in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* n_max = 100 * 0.29 was compared as 28.999999999999996, so disperse()
and the total-n mappers dropped the group sizes that reach 29. The limits
are now rounded like n and dispersion; disperse2() rounds them before its
half-unit shift.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave out a key argument that a wrapper forwards as NULL
recent_commits.body:
* A variable holding NULL, as from a wrapper with a NULL default, had its
name read as a column name, so every mapper tier failed with "already has
a column". Any key argument that evaluates to NULL now counts as not
specified.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn a number restore_zeros() cannot write out into NA
recent_commits.body:
* An exponent beyond the integer range, as in "0e99999999999", made
write_out_decimal() fail on an NA decimal point, and one inside it, as
in "1e-2147483647", asked R for a string longer than it allows. The
exponent is now read as a double, and a value whose integer or decimal
part would have more than WRITTEN_OUT_MAX digits becomes NA with a
warning, as a non-number does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take a character NA items_averaged as missing in grim_total()
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 933b877 let it through, as grim() does, but the
count then multiplied n by a string and failed in base R. grim() returns
NA there, and so does grim_total() now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a character NA in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 901d5c8 let any all-NA vector through, so a
character NA reached the arithmetic and failed in base R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from is_seq_*() for strings that are all missing
recent_commits.body:
* c("NaN", "NaN", "NaN") errored with "argument of length 0" since
5d6a90c made is_numeric_like() take "NaN" as missing, and all-"NA"
strings always had. Such strings only become NA after coercion, so they
got past the all-NA check and left no known value to index.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take a from of "NA" or "NaN" as missing in is_seq_dispersed()
recent_commits.body:
* is_numeric_like() returns NA for these strings, which reached an if()
and errored. For "NaN", this was a regression from 5d6a90c; it used to
return FALSE.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round near-whole steps in seq_disperse() before dropping zeros
recent_commits.body:
* A step like (0.1 + 0.2) * 10 - 3 passed the whole-number check but not
the zero filter, so the reported value was returned three times and the
sequence mappers tested it repeatedly.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that sequence mappers drop the other columns of data
recent_commits.body:
* The docs said that *_map_seq() output has the columns of the basic
mapper's output, and NEWS that mappers keep row names as a rowname
column. Sequence mappers drop both by design; case joins them back.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the empty "consistency with" line for a single key column
recent_commits.body:
* With only one key column, as in add_up_to_map() without a total, the
missing-column error ended on "tested for consistency with .".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the input of the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* A string failed in base R, mismatched lengths recycled with a base
warning, and a negative n was blamed on the count. Each is now an error
that names the argument.
* A fractional n or count gives NA, as it describes no data set and is
undecidable everywhere else in scrutiny.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check types in grim_total() and take 10^digits mod n exactly
recent_commits.body:
* grim_total() and grim_exp_incon() returned a silent NA for a string n,
and failed in base R for a string items_averaged or a missing percent.
They now check these as grim() does.
* With percent = TRUE and digits_x of 14 or 15, the first step of Euclid's
algorithm took 10^16 or 10^17 modulo n in doubles, which warned about a
complete loss of accuracy. That remainder is now built digit by digit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show a negative zero as zero in explanations
recent_commits.body: * formatC() printed round(-0.04, 1) as "-0.0", next to "rounds to 0.0".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name both roundings of a tie in an inconsistent GRIM explanation
recent_commits.body:
* Under "even" and "ties_even", grim_explain() said that a neighboring

takes such a tie to round either way. It now says "0.02 or 0.03 (a tie)".
grimmer_explain() inherits the fix.

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: counts per paper in summary_table; packages found nowhere (#568, item 24; #389)
recent_commits.body:
summary_table gives, for each paper, the scripts with a result of their own
(repro_scripts_n), the software files not run because they are not part of the
analysis (repro_not_analysis_n), and for each reason in the reason column how
many scripts did not run through for it (repro_fail_file, repro_fail_package and
so on). A corpus can now be counted from summary_table alone.

A package the Docker install finds in none of the places it looks (Bioconductor,
the CRAN Archive, the list of known places, R-universe) gets the install category
source_unknown. The report names it, since the code does not say where it comes
from, and the checklist says so for the script that needs it. A failed search of
R-universe is reported as a failed search, and the search now works in a bare
rocker/r-ver image, which lacked jsonlite: there it always failed, which looked
like a package R-universe lacks. Tried in both images: ecodeal is found nowhere,
and weathercan installs from the CRAN Archive.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: link the pipeline behind the paper's results; notebooks are not imported (#568)
recent_commits.body:
A file of software that nothing names, but that the analysis depends on, runs
too: in the same repository, a script that runs reads a file it writes, sources
or imports it; it reads a file such a script writes; or it runs a script linked
to the paper; along the whole chain. A name built from a pattern
("{metric}_per_hour.csv") matches the names it stands for. In the corpus this
links four FluxRGNN scripts that train the models and choose their settings, and
nothing else. The new paper_link column of table says what links each file of
software that runs to the paper's results, in words.

A Jupyter notebook is no longer taken as imported: `import audio` named a
package's module, and a tutorial notebook audio.ipynb got run_by_import and was
never run. Only .py files can be imported.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run software files only when linked to the paper; rgdal again (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Inside software (a package, application or copied tool), a script runs only when
something links it to the paper's results: the paper names it or an appendix it
names, it names the paper's figures or tables or writes a file named after one, a
README names it next to a figure or table, or it reads data deposited with the
paper outside the software. Otherwise it is not_analysis, with the reason. Trinity's
generated scripts that read the paper's data, and a package run by a workflow
(Snakefile, _targets.R, make.R), are the paper's analysis.

rgdal, rgeos and maptools install again from the CRAN Archive when the image has the
GDAL and GEOS header files: sp 2.1-4, the last version with sp.h, is installed first.
A script that crashes R in compiled code gets the reason environment.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run the authors' folders, fetch what the code needs, the internet, software files (#568)
recent_commits.body:
The code always runs in the repository as the authors organised it; the layout
argument is gone. A path that works nowhere is pointed to the one file with that
name in the repository, and the report lists it so the authors can change it. A
path to a file that exists nowhere is a missing input again.

When the code will run, the first module that downloads also fetches what the run
needs, in one request to each host; GitHub, GitLab and Dryad archives are kept
whole. Before the run a file the code names is fetched, and after the run a file
a script could not open is fetched and that script runs again.

A new argument, internet (off by default), lets scripts use the internet within
the download limits, checked every two seconds. A first rule marks files that
belong to software (package code, tests, documentation, generated files, web
applications, copied tools) as not_analysis. The option metacheck.docker_image_py
selects the large Python image with torch. Four functions no longer undo their
own clean-up with a later on.exit() without add = TRUE.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the install's second pass reaches more packages (#568, items 9, 14)
recent_commits.body:
A package on CRAN that needs one from Bioconductor gets it (speaq needs
MassSpecWavelet). Old packages compile: the warning this R treats as an error is
allowed in this pass, and Calloc() and the like, which R has dropped, map to their
current names, so maptools installs. What stopped a package is kept in its message.
rgdal and rgeos, withdrawn from CRAN in 2023, still do not install.
recent_commits.author: Lakens
