recent_commits.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
recent_commits.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Divide each count by n before multiplying in sd_binary_*()
recent_commits.body:

was 0 rather than the tiny SD it is. The variance is now

recent_commits.message: Rule out a dispersed sequence with a known infinity
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_dispersed(c(Inf, 1, NA), from = 1, test_linear = FALSE) was NA,
but no number is centered with an infinity on a finite from, nor is an
infinite from the center of any sequence. The same held with a missing
from. With test_linear = TRUE, the linear test already said FALSE.
* is_seq_dispersed(c(1, Inf, 2), from = Inf, test_linear = FALSE) failed
with a base R error: near(Inf, Inf) is NA. This predates the audit fixes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check test_linear and tolerance in the is_seq_*() functions
recent_commits.body:

not linear, and a missing test_linear failed in if () with a base R
error.

recent_commits.message: Reject an infinite by in seq_disperse()
recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the type of n in the total-n mappers
recent_commits.body:
* A string or factor n column reached is_whole_number() or round() and
failed in base R, where the basic and seq tiers give a type error. The
total-n tier now gives the same one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Handle NULL and string by-row arguments in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* A by-row argument left at a NULL default has no column, but the output
was assembled as if it had one, so it got a column named NA.
* A by-row argument that is both an argument and a column of data was
checked for agreement as numbers, so two different strings both became
NA, agreed, and the column was silently replaced, with two coercion
warnings. Values that are not both numbers are now compared as text, in
the new values_agree().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reserve every name function_map() assigns before reading arguments
recent_commits.body:
* enum_defaults and enum_vals are assigned before the arguments are read,
and cols_tested, col_variadic, arg_given, and vals before the by-row
arguments are checked for missingness, but none was reserved, so an
argument of .fn by one of these names was silently shadowed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record the reported columns for reverse_map_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* It took the columns before n to be the statistics reported for both
groups, so a custom basic mapper with n first rebuilt n1 and n2, and one
with n in the middle lost the columns after it; audit_total_n() inherited
both. Total-n output now records its .reported as the reported element of
the "scrutiny" attribute, which reverse_map_total_n() reads.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the width that restore_zeros() pads to
recent_commits.body:
* A width beyond what strrep() can build, such as 1e10, made it return NA
for the zeros, which was pasted into "1.5NA". width is now capped at
WRITTEN_OUT_MAX, the limit for written-out exponents.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round a tied SD both ways in debit(formula = "mean_n") under "even"
recent_commits.body:
* The bounds of "even" include both ties, so "exact" accepts an SD of 0.3
for a reconstructed SD of exactly 0.25, but "mean_n" rerounded that SD
to 0.2 only and rejected it, against its documented role as the looser
test. A tie is now rounded both ways, as "up_or_down" does. Swept over
every rounding method and sd_meaning: "mean_n" never rejects what
"exact" accepts.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rule out sequences whose missing values would have to pass an infinity
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(c(1, Inf, NA), test_linear = FALSE) was NA, but no
number comes after Inf; the same held for a leading NA before -Inf and
the mirror cases in is_seq_descending(). The known values are now padded
at a missing end with the infinity it would have to pass.
* is_seq_linear(c(Inf, NA, NA)) was NA, but an infinity among more than
two values is never linear, also when it is the only known one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from grim() for a character NA as x
recent_commits.body:
* grim_scalar() divided or multiplied x before its check for an
undecidable case, so a character NA failed in base R in grim(),
grim_explain(), and grim_map(). The check now comes first and takes any
non-finite x as undecidable, as the other tests do.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep integer counts from overflowing in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* group_0 * group_1 was an integer product, so counts from about 46,341
each gave NA, with the overflow warning suppressed along with sqrt()'s.
The counts are now doubles.
* An infinite or NaN count, n, or mean gave NaN rather than the
documented NA: which() skipped the NA that the whole-number test
returned for them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare near-whole n_min and n_max as whole numbers in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* n_max = 100 * 0.29 was compared as 28.999999999999996, so disperse()
and the total-n mappers dropped the group sizes that reach 29. The limits
are now rounded like n and dispersion; disperse2() rounds them before its
half-unit shift.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave out a key argument that a wrapper forwards as NULL
recent_commits.body:
* A variable holding NULL, as from a wrapper with a NULL default, had its
name read as a column name, so every mapper tier failed with "already has
a column". Any key argument that evaluates to NULL now counts as not
specified.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn a number restore_zeros() cannot write out into NA
recent_commits.body:
* An exponent beyond the integer range, as in "0e99999999999", made
write_out_decimal() fail on an NA decimal point, and one inside it, as
in "1e-2147483647", asked R for a string longer than it allows. The
exponent is now read as a double, and a value whose integer or decimal
part would have more than WRITTEN_OUT_MAX digits becomes NA with a
warning, as a non-number does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take a character NA items_averaged as missing in grim_total()
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 933b877 let it through, as grim() does, but the
count then multiplied n by a string and failed in base R. grim() returns
NA there, and so does grim_total() now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a character NA in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 901d5c8 let any all-NA vector through, so a
character NA reached the arithmetic and failed in base R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from is_seq_*() for strings that are all missing
recent_commits.body:
* c("NaN", "NaN", "NaN") errored with "argument of length 0" since
5d6a90c made is_numeric_like() take "NaN" as missing, and all-"NA"
strings always had. Such strings only become NA after coercion, so they

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: counts per paper in summary_table; packages found nowhere (#568, item 24; #389)
recent_commits.body:
summary_table gives, for each paper, the scripts with a result of their own
(repro_scripts_n), the software files not run because they are not part of the
analysis (repro_not_analysis_n), and for each reason in the reason column how
many scripts did not run through for it (repro_fail_file, repro_fail_package and
so on). A corpus can now be counted from summary_table alone.

A package the Docker install finds in none of the places it looks (Bioconductor,
the CRAN Archive, the list of known places, R-universe) gets the install category
source_unknown. The report names it, since the code does not say where it comes
from, and the checklist says so for the script that needs it. A failed search of
R-universe is reported as a failed search, and the search now works in a bare
rocker/r-ver image, which lacked jsonlite: there it always failed, which looked
like a package R-universe lacks. Tried in both images: ecodeal is found nowhere,
and weathercan installs from the CRAN Archive.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: link the pipeline behind the paper's results; notebooks are not imported (#568)
recent_commits.body:
A file of software that nothing names, but that the analysis depends on, runs
too: in the same repository, a script that runs reads a file it writes, sources
or imports it; it reads a file such a script writes; or it runs a script linked
to the paper; along the whole chain. A name built from a pattern
("{metric}_per_hour.csv") matches the names it stands for. In the corpus this
links four FluxRGNN scripts that train the models and choose their settings, and
nothing else. The new paper_link column of table says what links each file of
software that runs to the paper's results, in words.

A Jupyter notebook is no longer taken as imported: `import audio` named a
package's module, and a tutorial notebook audio.ipynb got run_by_import and was
never run. Only .py files can be imported.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run software files only when linked to the paper; rgdal again (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Inside software (a package, application or copied tool), a script runs only when
something links it to the paper's results: the paper names it or an appendix it
names, it names the paper's figures or tables or writes a file named after one, a
README names it next to a figure or table, or it reads data deposited with the
paper outside the software. Otherwise it is not_analysis, with the reason. Trinity's
generated scripts that read the paper's data, and a package run by a workflow
(Snakefile, _targets.R, make.R), are the paper's analysis.

rgdal, rgeos and maptools install again from the CRAN Archive when the image has the
GDAL and GEOS header files: sp 2.1-4, the last version with sp.h, is installed first.
A script that crashes R in compiled code gets the reason environment.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run the authors' folders, fetch what the code needs, the internet, software files (#568)
recent_commits.body:
The code always runs in the repository as the authors organised it; the layout
argument is gone. A path that works nowhere is pointed to the one file with that
name in the repository, and the report lists it so the authors can change it. A
path to a file that exists nowhere is a missing input again.

When the code will run, the first module that downloads also fetches what the run
needs, in one request to each host; GitHub, GitLab and Dryad archives are kept
whole. Before the run a file the code names is fetched, and after the run a file
a script could not open is fetched and that script runs again.

A new argument, internet (off by default), lets scripts use the internet within
the download limits, checked every two seconds. A first rule marks files that
belong to software (package code, tests, documentation, generated files, web
applications, copied tools) as not_analysis. The option metacheck.docker_image_py
selects the large Python image with torch. Four functions no longer undo their
own clean-up with a later on.exit() without add = TRUE.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
recent_commits.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Handle NULL and string by-row arguments in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* A by-row argument left at a NULL default has no column, but the output
was assembled as if it had one, so it got a column named NA.
* A by-row argument that is both an argument and a column of data was
checked for agreement as numbers, so two different strings both became
NA, agreed, and the column was silently replaced, with two coercion
warnings. Values that are not both numbers are now compared as text, in
the new values_agree().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reserve every name function_map() assigns before reading arguments
recent_commits.body:
* enum_defaults and enum_vals are assigned before the arguments are read,
and cols_tested, col_variadic, arg_given, and vals before the by-row
arguments are checked for missingness, but none was reserved, so an
argument of .fn by one of these names was silently shadowed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record the reported columns for reverse_map_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* It took the columns before n to be the statistics reported for both
groups, so a custom basic mapper with n first rebuilt n1 and n2, and one
with n in the middle lost the columns after it; audit_total_n() inherited
both. Total-n output now records its .reported as the reported element of
the "scrutiny" attribute, which reverse_map_total_n() reads.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the width that restore_zeros() pads to
recent_commits.body:
* A width beyond what strrep() can build, such as 1e10, made it return NA
for the zeros, which was pasted into "1.5NA". width is now capped at
WRITTEN_OUT_MAX, the limit for written-out exponents.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round a tied SD both ways in debit(formula = "mean_n") under "even"
recent_commits.body:
* The bounds of "even" include both ties, so "exact" accepts an SD of 0.3
for a reconstructed SD of exactly 0.25, but "mean_n" rerounded that SD
to 0.2 only and rejected it, against its documented role as the looser
test. A tie is now rounded both ways, as "up_or_down" does. Swept over
every rounding method and sd_meaning: "mean_n" never rejects what
"exact" accepts.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rule out sequences whose missing values would have to pass an infinity
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(c(1, Inf, NA), test_linear = FALSE) was NA, but no
number comes after Inf; the same held for a leading NA before -Inf and
the mirror cases in is_seq_descending(). The known values are now padded
at a missing end with the infinity it would have to pass.
* is_seq_linear(c(Inf, NA, NA)) was NA, but an infinity among more than
two values is never linear, also when it is the only known one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from grim() for a character NA as x
recent_commits.body:
* grim_scalar() divided or multiplied x before its check for an
undecidable case, so a character NA failed in base R in grim(),
grim_explain(), and grim_map(). The check now comes first and takes any
non-finite x as undecidable, as the other tests do.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep integer counts from overflowing in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* group_0 * group_1 was an integer product, so counts from about 46,341
each gave NA, with the overflow warning suppressed along with sqrt()'s.
The counts are now doubles.
* An infinite or NaN count, n, or mean gave NaN rather than the
documented NA: which() skipped the NA that the whole-number test
returned for them.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare near-whole n_min and n_max as whole numbers in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* n_max = 100 * 0.29 was compared as 28.999999999999996, so disperse()
and the total-n mappers dropped the group sizes that reach 29. The limits
are now rounded like n and dispersion; disperse2() rounds them before its
half-unit shift.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave out a key argument that a wrapper forwards as NULL
recent_commits.body:
* A variable holding NULL, as from a wrapper with a NULL default, had its
name read as a column name, so every mapper tier failed with "already has
a column". Any key argument that evaluates to NULL now counts as not
specified.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn a number restore_zeros() cannot write out into NA
recent_commits.body:
* An exponent beyond the integer range, as in "0e99999999999", made
write_out_decimal() fail on an NA decimal point, and one inside it, as
in "1e-2147483647", asked R for a string longer than it allows. The
exponent is now read as a double, and a value whose integer or decimal
part would have more than WRITTEN_OUT_MAX digits becomes NA with a
warning, as a non-number does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take a character NA items_averaged as missing in grim_total()
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 933b877 let it through, as grim() does, but the
count then multiplied n by a string and failed in base R. grim() returns
NA there, and so does grim_total() now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a character NA in the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* The type check from 901d5c8 let any all-NA vector through, so a
character NA reached the arithmetic and failed in base R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return NA from is_seq_*() for strings that are all missing
recent_commits.body:
* c("NaN", "NaN", "NaN") errored with "argument of length 0" since
5d6a90c made is_numeric_like() take "NaN" as missing, and all-"NA"
strings always had. Such strings only become NA after coercion, so they
got past the all-NA check and left no known value to index.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take a from of "NA" or "NaN" as missing in is_seq_dispersed()
recent_commits.body:
* is_numeric_like() returns NA for these strings, which reached an if()
and errored. For "NaN", this was a regression from 5d6a90c; it used to
return FALSE.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round near-whole steps in seq_disperse() before dropping zeros
recent_commits.body:
* A step like (0.1 + 0.2) * 10 - 3 passed the whole-number check but not
the zero filter, so the reported value was returned three times and the
sequence mappers tested it repeatedly.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that sequence mappers drop the other columns of data
recent_commits.body:
* The docs said that *_map_seq() output has the columns of the basic
mapper's output, and NEWS that mappers keep row names as a rowname
column. Sequence mappers drop both by design; case joins them back.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the empty "consistency with" line for a single key column
recent_commits.body:
* With only one key column, as in add_up_to_map() without a total, the
missing-column error ended on "tested for consistency with .".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the input of the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* A string failed in base R, mismatched lengths recycled with a base
warning, and a negative n was blamed on the count. Each is now an error
that names the argument.
* A fractional n or count gives NA, as it describes no data set and is
undecidable everywhere else in scrutiny.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check types in grim_total() and take 10^digits mod n exactly
recent_commits.body:
* grim_total() and grim_exp_incon() returned a silent NA for a string n,
and failed in base R for a string items_averaged or a missing percent.
They now check these as grim() does.
* With percent = TRUE and digits_x of 14 or 15, the first step of Euclid's
algorithm took 10^16 or 10^17 modulo n in doubles, which warned about a
complete loss of accuracy. That remainder is now built digit by digit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show a negative zero as zero in explanations
recent_commits.body: * formatC() printed round(-0.04, 1) as "-0.0", next to "rounds to 0.0".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name both roundings of a tie in an inconsistent GRIM explanation
recent_commits.body:
* Under "even" and "ties_even", grim_explain() said that a neighboring
mean like 0.025 rounds to 0.03, from its binary value, although the test
takes such a tie to round either way. It now says "0.02 or 0.03 (a tie)".
grimmer_explain() inherits the fix.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject an empty decimal separator
recent_commits.body:
* sep = "" matched at the start of every string, so decimal_places()
counted all digits as decimals and restore_zeros() failed in base R.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take the string "NaN" as missing in is_numeric_like(), quiet is_seq_*()
recent_commits.body:
* is_numeric_like(c("1", "NaN")) was FALSE, so restore_zeros_df() and
decimal_places_df() skipped such a column although the vector functions
handle it.
* The is_seq_*() functions leaked a coercion warning for the string "NA",
which is_numeric_like() had already accepted as missing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rule out a dispersed sequence by the center its known values imply
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_dispersed(c(1, 2, NA, NA, NA), from = 10) was NA although the
known values fix the step, and so the center, at 3. Only fully known
mirrored pairs were compared to from.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: the install's second pass reaches more packages (#568, items 9, 14)
recent_commits.body:
A package on CRAN that needs one from Bioconductor gets it (speaq needs
MassSpecWavelet). Old packages compile: the warning this R treats as an error is
allowed in this pass, and Calloc() and the like, which R has dropped, map to their
current names, so maptools installs. What stopped a package is kept in its message.
rgdal and rgeos, withdrawn from CRAN in 2023, still do not install.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: a line per repository; an option for the image (#568, item 8)
recent_commits.body:
When a paper links several repositories, the report has a line per repository, and
table has a repo_name column, so a reader can see when failures lie in software by
others. Nothing is left out automatically: of 92 links whose owner matches no author
name, 61 are the authors' own, so skipping would hide 575 real failures.

The option metacheck.docker_image names another R image, to try one before it is
published.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: Python finds the repository's modules; servers; more packages (#568, items 10, 17, 22)
recent_commits.body:
Item 10: the folder holding each of the repository's own modules a script imports goes
on its search path, nearest to the script first, unless it would hide a standard
module the script uses. Python only looked beside the script.

Item 22: a Python script that serves others waits for a connection until the time
limit, so it is not run and has the outcome needs_a_person.

Item 17: a missing function is also looked up in more common packages, to add the
missing library() call, and snakemake counts as an environment problem.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: reasons, the internet, absent files, packages elsewhere (#568, items 12, 21, 23, 24)
recent_commits.body:
Item 24: run_results and table have a reason column, and a script that stops without
a message gets one.

Item 21: a script that stops because the network is off in a Docker run has the
outcome needs_internet, which keeps the light from green but does not make it red.
The network stays off; a setting to turn it on is left for a decision.

Item 23: the report lists the files that scripts which did not run through read or
run and the deposit does not hold, with data files apart from scripts.

Item 12: the Docker install looks in a table of known places, then through
R-universe's search for that exact name, and names where a package came from.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: load the script that defines what a script uses (#568, item 16)
recent_commits.body:
Each script has a session of its own, so moving the defining script earlier in the
order could not give the next script its objects. When a script stops on a name that
exactly one other script defines, or exactly one in its own folder, the second run
loads that script first, from its own run folder. Two scripts that need each other
do not load each other. The report and modifications (loaded_first) note this,
because the script does not run on its own and should source() the other itself.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: find packages that are not on CRAN (#568, items 9, 11, 13)
recent_commits.body:
Docker route: after the other packages, a second pass looks on Bioconductor and then
for the latest version in the CRAN Archive, in two rounds because an archived package
can need another. Tried in the real image: waffle, hier.part, rain and decontam now
install. Biostrings, phyloseq and others still fail on zlib.h, which the image lacks.

Python: more import names map to their install name, Python 2's standard library is
not looked for on PyPI and gives the outcome python2, pip prefers a wheel, each
package has its own time limit, and a pinned version that does not install is
replaced by the current one, which the install results note.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: what only a person's computer has (#568, items 15, 18, 19, 20)
recent_commits.body:
Item 15: install.packages(), install_github(), BiocManager::install() and the like
are replaced during a Docker run or with recorded versions, and p_load() becomes
library(); the module has installed what the scripts load before the run.

Item 18: file.choose() is replaced by a data file when a comment beside it names
one or the deposit holds only one, and this is noted. A script that still asks a
person, or starts an app with runApp() and the like, has the outcome needs_a_person,
which keeps the light from green but does not make it red. On Windows file.choose()
opened a window and waited; it now stops at once.

Item 19: Numba's and Matplotlib's caches go to /tmp in the Python container, and
plots do not ask for a screen.

Item 20 and part of 17: a figure missing from a document no longer stops the code,
View() does nothing, windowsFonts() no longer stops a script on Linux, here() finds
a mark for the top of the project, and the folder of a written file is made.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run from where paths work; Docker failures; empty arguments (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Fix: the scan for names held in variables, added for item 4, stopped the module
with "argument is missing" on any script with an empty argument, such as x[1, ].

Item 4: in the package layout, each script runs from the folder at or above its own
from which the most of the files and folders it names exist; on a tie from the
nearest .Rproj folder, else its own. A sourced script takes the folder of the script
that sources it, and rewritten paths count from the folder in use. The default
layout does not change here; the two layouts are compared on real papers first.

Item 27: a script whose Docker container never started has the outcome
docker_failed, which keeps the light from green but does not make it red, instead of
errored with a red light.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: function files and package tests are not scripts (#568, item 7)
recent_commits.body:
A file that only defines functions has the new outcome defines_functions: a
function should be used, not run, and 1570 of 1874 such files in the corpus had
counted as ran_ok. The new used_by column and the report name the scripts that use
its functions. A package's tests and its setup.py have the new outcome
not_analysis. Neither is run or counted as a script, so the share of scripts that
ran can go down. A function file a running script sources stays run_by_source.
Plain text saved as R stays a failure, as it cannot be told from a broken analysis.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: Python 2 outcome and more notebook commands (#568, item 6)
recent_commits.body:
Python 2 code gets the outcome python2 in place of not_parsed, from Python's
parser or from the run's error. It is not run, since only Python 3 is available,
and not converted, since that can change results. A file that does not parse is
no longer reported as run by the file that imports it.

code_extract_py() leaves out a whole %%bash cell, makes an indented command pass,
and removes "cd folder" and "name?"; an R-kernel notebook keeps these lines, since
they are code there. A stand-in for get_ipython() is added, and what was left out
or added is noted in modifications, the report, the checklist and table.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: follow more paths to files in the listing (#568, item 4)
recent_commits.body:
A listed file's name held in a variable, as in f <- c(NetworkFunction.R)
followed by source(f), is now rewritten, only when it fits exactly one file. Among
files with one name, the file a reference means is also found counted from a
folder above the script, or by the folders in its own path, also in an absolute
path from the author's computer. If that leaves several files or none, nothing is
guessed.

This is the first part of item 4: 155 of the 271 failures on a listed file would
find it with every file at its original path, which is compared separately.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: give model files an outcome of their own (#568, item 5)
recent_commits.body:
A JAGS or BUGS model saved with an R extension, or a file that is not R at all,
was recognised but still got the outcome not_parsed after a run. It now has the
outcome jags_model or not_r_content, which the counts of scripts in the report
and the checklist, and the to-do list of the report, leave out. A script and such
a file are no longer two scripts whose order is unknown, which made the light
yellow. A model is also recognised with its brace on the next line, or after a
data block.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: find files spelled otherwise, and tell the authors (#568, item 3)
recent_commits.body:
A reference with no exact match now matches the one plan file with the same
extension and the same name apart from case, spaces and punctuation, which
repositories such as Dryad can cause on deposit. A separator between two digits
still counts, and a piece of a name, a placeholder, a name built from a variable
and a file the script writes itself are not compared. The package layout
rewrites these names too.

Each correction is noted so authors can change their script: a name_corrected
row in modifications, a names_corrected column in table, a table in the report
and a line in the checklist. A name that differs only in case gets the same note.

A file with the same name in another format is not converted, and is reported
only when both are data formats; near matches only compare files of the same
extension.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: give same-named scripts their own results (#568, item 26)
recent_commits.body:
Every step knew a script by file_name, which holds no folder, so scripts that
share a name shared one result, and outside the package layout they overwrote
each other in the sandbox. After identical copies are removed, a name that
repeats within a paper becomes the script's path, with the repository in front
when the path repeats too; a name that occurs once stays as it is, so results
stay comparable. table gets a file_path column.

Same-named scripts are written to their own row of the plan or their own path.
Among same-named files, source() and file references mean the file in the
script's own folder or the one their path names, and nothing is guessed
otherwise. Of several Python modules with one name, only one the importer can
reach counts as imported.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: correct the checkable-inputs changes (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Move the helpers above the repro_missing_inputs documentation block, so the
documentation stays on that function. Count a Windows path as checkable. Do
not predict a name built at run time as missing (paste(), paste0(), a Python
name joined with +). After a run, a predicted missing file no longer colours
the light of a script that ran without an error.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: run every script that parses, and do not predict built names as missing (#568)
recent_commits.body:
Scripts with a predicted missing file are no longer skipped. The prediction was
partly wrong and the skip hid how far a script gets. Names that cannot be checked
before the code runs (paste() and sprintf() calls, placeholders, pieces of names)
are no longer predicted as missing. After a run, the report lists only inputs in
the deposit that are not usable as named. Tests added but not yet run.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #567 from scienceverse/recorded_versions
recent_commits.body: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and R 3.6 fixes
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and declared-version fixes
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check gets recorded_versions (default FALSE): with TRUE, the R
packages the scripts load are installed at the versions in renv.lock, a
sessionInfo() or session_info() record, or a groundhog or checkpoint date. The R
version is not changed. On 16 repositories this took about 2.7 times as long and
no failing script started working, so it is not the default. When scripts fail
and a repository records versions, the report, summary and checklist recommend a
run with the setting; on a shared server they say it is not available there.

After installing recorded versions, a load check replaces a recorded version that
keeps a package from loading, or crashes R, with the current one.

code_check reads sessionInfo() records pasted into scripts, and no longer counts a
README in a revdep folder as a record.

Fixes found by running real repositories:
- Docker runs no longer write a crash file of about 2.5 GB per R crash on Windows
- installs on R 3.6 work: closed MRAN addresses go to the Posit copy of that date,
  remotes is installed when the image lacks it, results keep working without
  data.frame's newer defaults
- packages that keep the current version install before recorded ones
- a package gone from CRAN that is in the image or main library counts as present
- batch runs pass layout on
- a package that does not load is reported with R's own reason

The live ResearchBox test in test-module-repo_check.R skips when ResearchBox asks
for a captcha.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Check the types in grim_values(), name a bad constant element, rebuild README
recent_commits.body:
* grim_values() and grim_closest() run the same input checks as grim():
a string n or items_averaged is an error, not an undecidable value set
with a row of NA, and a percent that is not TRUE or FALSE is an error
in them and in grim_plot_values(), through a shared check_percent().

* A constant list element of the wrong length is reported under the
user's name for it, such as `constant$z`, instead of the internal
variable, and without the purrr "In index" contexts, which made an
error about the argument look like one about a row.

* README.md is rebuilt from the unchanged README.Rmd: the whole-number
key and digits columns have been integer since 9d9af5b.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the groups in order when reverse_map_total_n() starts from a back pair
recent_commits.body:
* reverse_map_total_n() took the first two rows of each case as the first
and the second group. A "back" pair holds the second group's values in
its first row, since the mapper swaps the groups for that direction, so
after filter(dir == "back") or a sort by direction the reconstructed x1
and x2 (and sd1 and sd2) changed places, and audit_total_n() reported
the hits under the swapped groups. The two rows of a back pair now
change places first.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add up near-whole counts as whole numbers and reject bad n in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* add_up_to() accepted a near-whole value like 100 * 0.29 as whole but
compared it exactly, so add_up_to(c(10, 19), total = 100 * 0.29) was
FALSE. The values are rounded before the comparison, as every other
whole-number argument is.

* disperse(), disperse2(), and disperse_total() check that n is numeric
and finite before any arithmetic. A string, a logical, a missing value
in disperse2(), or an infinity used to fail with a raw R error from the
arithmetic, or in disperse_total(TRUE) to return no rows at all.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the findings of the grim_grid() audit
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() has a threshold argument for data without a recorded
one, so a plot without data can show any up_from raster. A test checks
that a recorded or given threshold reaches the raster.

* DESCRIPTION requires dplyr >= 1.1.0, which .by needs, as in
grim_plot_rates() and the grim_grid() example.

* grim_grid() says when digits is missing and gives one message for any
value other than 1, 2, or 3, without the digits_x wording about scaling
x. Length checks on rounding and threshold come before roundwork's
message, which names symmetric.

* The docs say three decimal places take about 20 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Point to grim_grid() in the GRIM vignette and keep R 4.1 support
recent_commits.body:
* The vignette no longer says the up_from family has no raster, and shows
grim_grid() with the share of means ruled out per sample size.

* grim_grid() docs say which digits to use for percentages.

* purrr::pluck() keeps the pipe in grim_grid_inconsistent() without the
_$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return every cell of the grid from grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* grim_grid() now has a consistency column and a row for every cell, so
rates such as the share of means ruled out per n are one summarise()
away. The cells are marked by position from the cached inconsistent
ones, which takes about half a millisecond for 2 decimal places.

* The cache is unchanged. grim_plot_grid() reads it through the new
internal grim_grid_inconsistent() and does no extra work.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename grim_raster() to grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* The function returns data, the grid's inconsistent cells, so it is
named after the grid that grim_plot_grid() draws, like grim_values() and
grim_plot_values(). "Raster" is left to the plot's drawing.

* GRIM_RASTERS and generate_grim_raster() follow suit; R/sysdata.rda
was regenerated and holds identical data under the new name.

recent_commits.message: Match target studies whose labels carry a title
recent_commits.body:
A real gpt-5.5 run on Yu et al. (2024) labelled studies as
'Study 4: Feeling Gratitude Toward Close Versus Distant Others'; the
trailing-token match found no number, so 'Study 4' resolved to nothing
and isolation fell back to the generative method. The study number is
now taken from 'Study/Experiment N' anywhere in the label first.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Price gpt-6.1-terra in the cost table
recent_commits.body:
Standard-tier OpenAI pricing for <=272K-token context ($1.00 input,
$5.00 output per 1M tokens), so llm_usd is estimated instead of 0.0.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a
supplement the run lacks, the judge is told to say so for unlocated
registered elements. The CLI's repeatable --supplement PATH (and a
'supplement' batch-manifest column) appends parsed supplements to the
paper under labelled separators, after isolation so they are never
trimmed; supplying them suppresses the judge note.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.

recent_commits.message: Install recorded package versions on request; Docker and declared-version fixes
recent_commits.body:
reproducibility_check gets recorded_versions (default FALSE): with TRUE, the R
packages the scripts load are installed at the versions in renv.lock, a
sessionInfo() or session_info() record, or a groundhog or checkpoint date. The R
version is not changed. On 16 repositories this took about 2.7 times as long and
no failing script started working, so it is not the default. When scripts fail
and a repository records versions, the report, summary and checklist recommend a
run with the setting; on a shared server they say it is not available there.

After installing recorded versions, a load check replaces a recorded version that
keeps a package from loading, or crashes R, with the current one.

code_check reads sessionInfo() records pasted into scripts, and no longer counts a
README in a revdep folder as a record.

Fixes found by running real repositories:
- Docker runs no longer write a crash file of about 2.5 GB per R crash on Windows
- installs on R 3.6 work: closed MRAN addresses go to the Posit copy of that date,
  remotes is installed when the image lacks it, results keep working without
  data.frame's newer defaults
- packages that keep the current version install before recorded ones
- a package gone from CRAN that is in the image or main library counts as present
- batch runs pass layout on
- a package that does not load is reported with R's own reason

The live ResearchBox test in test-module-repo_check.R skips when ResearchBox asks
for a captcha.

recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.message: Keep the groups in order when reverse_map_total_n() starts from a back pair
recent_commits.body:
* reverse_map_total_n() took the first two rows of each case as the first
and the second group. A "back" pair holds the second group's values in
its first row, since the mapper swaps the groups for that direction, so
after filter(dir == "back") or a sort by direction the reconstructed x1
and x2 (and sd1 and sd2) changed places, and audit_total_n() reported
the hits under the swapped groups. The two rows of a back pair now
change places first.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add up near-whole counts as whole numbers and reject bad n in disperse*()
recent_commits.body:
* add_up_to() accepted a near-whole value like 100 * 0.29 as whole but
compared it exactly, so add_up_to(c(10, 19), total = 100 * 0.29) was
FALSE. The values are rounded before the comparison, as every other
whole-number argument is.

* disperse(), disperse2(), and disperse_total() check that n is numeric
and finite before any arithmetic. A string, a logical, a missing value
in disperse2(), or an infinity used to fail with a raw R error from the
arithmetic, or in disperse_total(TRUE) to return no rows at all.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the findings of the grim_grid() audit
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() has a threshold argument for data without a recorded
one, so a plot without data can show any up_from raster. A test checks
that a recorded or given threshold reaches the raster.

* DESCRIPTION requires dplyr >= 1.1.0, which .by needs, as in
grim_plot_rates() and the grim_grid() example.

* grim_grid() says when digits is missing and gives one message for any
value other than 1, 2, or 3, without the digits_x wording about scaling
x. Length checks on rounding and threshold come before roundwork's
message, which names symmetric.

* The docs say three decimal places take about 20 seconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Point to grim_grid() in the GRIM vignette and keep R 4.1 support
recent_commits.body:
* The vignette no longer says the up_from family has no raster, and shows
grim_grid() with the share of means ruled out per sample size.

* grim_grid() docs say which digits to use for percentages.

* purrr::pluck() keeps the pipe in grim_grid_inconsistent() without the
_$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return every cell of the grid from grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* grim_grid() now has a consistency column and a row for every cell, so
rates such as the share of means ruled out per n are one summarise()
away. The cells are marked by position from the cached inconsistent
ones, which takes about half a millisecond for 2 decimal places.

* The cache is unchanged. grim_plot_grid() reads it through the new
internal grim_grid_inconsistent() and does no extra work.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename grim_raster() to grim_grid()
recent_commits.body:
* The function returns data, the grid's inconsistent cells, so it is
named after the grid that grim_plot_grid() draws, like grim_values() and
grim_plot_values(). "Raster" is left to the plot's drawing.

* GRIM_RASTERS and generate_grim_raster() follow suit; R/sysdata.rda
was regenerated and holds identical data under the new name.

* Back to $rounding instead of the _$ extractor, which needs R 4.3.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Draw grim_plot_grid()'s raster through grim_raster()
recent_commits.body:
* The plot passes the recorded rounding and threshold to grim_raster(),
so the up_from family gets a raster instead of an error, and the lookup
and ties_* resolution live in one place.

* Includes the user's edits to grim_raster(): blank lines between steps
and "fractional parts" in the symmetric comment and docs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grim_raster() for the GRIM-inconsistent grid
recent_commits.body:
* Cached rasters for 1 or 2 decimal places are looked up by name; other
rounding methods, the up_from family with its threshold, and 3 decimal
places are computed on demand. More than 3 is an error.

* generate_grim_raster() moves from data-raw/data-gen.R into the package,
so the cache and the on-demand path share one generator.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix: caption-only table extent, W0p page-bound superscripts, grid-copy suppression, styled headings, stacked header labels, canary fixes
recent_commits.body:
Tables - A caption-only region takes its width and depth from its own rules; a whitespace region is extended to the table's closing rule; worded rows in a rule-bounded region are not trimmed as prose. - Side-by-side text lines in one Camelot cell keep page order and a space; a row label that runs on past the stub column returns to it. Both run only after the table gates (convert, then re-convert with telemetry discarded, kept only with an unchanged shape). - Stacked column-label lines fold into one header row (joined with
, as the super-header fold); not onto a data row, an unclosed parenthesis or a lost-glyph line. A single long line over the stub (panel label, stray caption line) is no longer folded into the stub label. - A fourth header row only under stacked label lines. Text and render - W0p superscript marking bound to its page and token; raised-sign exponents. - S8m: a significance mark printed on its own line rejoins its p-value legend. - Lines the render copies from a structured table are suppressed in the body; title rescue folds caret markers; RULE 0g / caption tail lines. - Lines set in the paper's heading face become headings (two- and three-line headings joined, run-in headings refused); a smaller size of a face whose larger size is a ### heading is emitted ####. Every change carries a regression test watched failing first; two-arm render diffs over a 128-paper sample were read against page images by a second model.

recent_commits.message: Test a near-whole n as the whole number it is shown as
recent_commits.body:
* `is_whole_number()` accepts a value within 1.5e-8 of a whole number,
such as `100 * 0.29`, but the arithmetic used it as is. 5288581 rounded
the `n` column of mapper output, yet only after the test, so `grim_map(x
= 1.5, n = 2 - 1e-9, rounding = "ceiling")` was FALSE next to `n = 2`,
where it is TRUE; GRIMMER and DEBIT compared the raw value to their
minimum `n` of 2 and left the verdict NA; `disperse_total()` and the
total-n mappers split `40 - 1e-9` as odd, into 19.5 and 20.5.

rest, which the tests reject as before. It runs at the export boundaries,
on the `ARGS_WHOLE` arguments: `function_map()`'s tested columns, which
the output now takes its key and helper columns from, `map_value_sets()`,
