recent_commits.message: Test a near-whole n as the whole number it is shown as
recent_commits.body:
* `is_whole_number()` accepts a value within 1.5e-8 of a whole number,
such as `100 * 0.29`, but the arithmetic used it as is. 5288581 rounded
the `n` column of mapper output, yet only after the test, so `grim_map(x
= 1.5, n = 2 - 1e-9, rounding = "ceiling")` was FALSE next to `n = 2`,
where it is TRUE; GRIMMER and DEBIT compared the raw value to their
minimum `n` of 2 and left the verdict NA; `disperse_total()` and the
total-n mappers split `40 - 1e-9` as odd, into 19.5 and 20.5.

* `round_whole()` rounds the values the tolerance accepts and leaves the
rest, which the tests reject as before. It runs at the export boundaries,
on the `ARGS_WHOLE` arguments: `function_map()`'s tested columns, which
the output now takes its key and helper columns from, `map_value_sets()`,
the `*_explain()` functions, `disperse_total()`, and the totals of the
total-n body. The `*_scalar()` functions see whole numbers only.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the stable core of 1.0.0 in NEWS and the factory help pages
recent_commits.body:
* The release summary now says that the tests, the mapper tiers, and
audit() are stable, and that everything new in 1.0.0 and the developer
tools may change in a minor release. The bullet under "New features"
that said half of this is folded into it.

* The help pages of function_map(), function_map_seq(), and
function_map_total_n() carry the same note; until now only the pkgdown
reference index did.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Round, not truncate, n and digits_* to integer
recent_commits.body:
* `as_integer_if_lossless()` admits values within tolerance of a whole number
but truncated them, so `n = 100 * 0.29` (28.999999999999996) was shown as 28
next to the verdict for 29. b8536d3 extended this to `digits_*`: a
`digits_x` just below 2 was shown as 1, and `grim_map_seq()` then failed.
* `function_map()` and `function_map_seq()` turn `digits_*` into integers
before testing or dispersing, so the column is the value used. Non-numeric
input passes through unchanged, for `fn()`'s own error.
* Two long lines in `R/utils.R` and `R/function-map.R` formatted with air.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check only single-value defaults for length in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 required every setting to be length 1, so a mapper made from a
`.fn` with a setting such as `bounds = NULL` or `scale = c(1, 7)` failed on
every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the length error for length-2 settings in two stale tests
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 checks every setting's length before its value, so
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` and `percent = c(TRUE, FALSE)` now fail with
"must be length 1, not 2". Two expectations still had the old wording.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the digits_* columns as integers in all mapper tiers
recent_commits.body:
* `n` was already integer when lossless, but `digits_x` and `digits_sd` were
double although they are always whole numbers. `function_map()` and
`function_map_seq()` now pass them through `as_integer_if_lossless()`; the
total-n tier inherits the basic mapper's columns.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut NEWS items that describe changes since 0.6.1 only within the branch
recent_commits.body:
* Each item was checked against scrutiny 0.6.1, installed from main. Dropped:
the integer `digits_*` columns, the `items = 2` partial match, the error for
two key arguments naming one column, the `grim_binomial()` and
`grim_plot_rates()` clause, GRIMMER running indefinitely, the integer
`diff_var`, `1e-300` having 315 decimal places, and mappers failing under
`lapply()`.
* Reworded items that 0.6.1 handled differently from the stated earlier
state: a seq mapper with nothing to disperse already warned, and a total-n
case without group pairs failed rather than vanishing.
* `grim_map(percent = TRUE)` now says that `x` stays a percentage, which is
the actual change from 0.6.1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require every setting to be length 1 in the mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers checked the settings with `check_lengths_congruent()`,
which allowed one of them to be longer than 1. An enum such as
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` then reached `rlang::arg_match()`,
whose error says it is 'not "se"', though "se" is valid; `percent =
c(TRUE, FALSE)` reached the test. The vectorized functions had their
own length-1 check with a better message.

* `check_setting_length()` is that check, shared by `map_value_sets()`,
`function_map()`, and the total-n factory, which reads an enum before
`fn()` does. In the mappers it runs after `check_rounding_args()`, which
keeps its own message for the rounding arguments.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` had no caller left and is deleted with its
tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
recent_commits.body:

default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.

recent_commits.body:

size and reused, so they are not fetched or unpacked again on every run.

control characters, a final dot or space, reserved names) are now changed
in the same way on every system, wherever metacheck saves a file. A script
that cannot be written no longer stops reproducibility_check for the paper.

recent_commits.message: data_check reads every sheet of a spreadsheet that holds a table (#555)
recent_commits.body: Each table of a file with several has its columns under source_file = "file.xlsx [sheet]", and a new column sheet names the sheet; a file with one table keeps its own name. Sheets of notes and codebooks are documentation when the file has another table. FAIR_repo() names each variable's CSV by its sheet, writes a CSV per sheet of an .ods file, and writes dataset_description.json also when the first sheet's CSV went to documentation/.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
recent_commits.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
recent_commits.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() works on a temporary copy and keeps recovered code; data_check is faster on large files (#554); code_check no longer writes into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() runs its checks on a temporary copy, so the folder is only read. It keeps code recovered from output files as scripts, changes the paths scripts write to, replaces setwd() only for a written-out folder, no folder or the script's own folder, changes links in the folder's README to the files' new places, names each variable's file as it is in the copy, and has an execute argument for the library() calls reproducibility_check adds.

data_check's column checks work on each distinct value once and skip text work for plain number columns; 498 columns compared gave identical results. codebook_check no longer converts columns without documented codes. Pages made by pkgdown are not taken for rendered analyses.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() keeps folders, the authors' README and results apart; requirements.txt lists only installable Python packages; output readers keep backslashes
recent_commits.body:
From converting 20 real repositories:
- psychds_file_plan() keeps a file's folders inside data/, materials/ and
  documentation/ as well as analysis/, ignores a top folder that holds
  every file (GitHub downloads), and drops a first folder that only names
  the kind of file. Data in one folder per condition lost which condition
  it was, and the authors' README was moved out of the top.
- FAIR_repo() puts a file a script writes and no script reads, and a
  fitted model, in outputs/, and points scripts there; converts an R data
  file only when it holds a table and no CSV of that name is next to it;
  writes requirements.txt with Python packages only, without the standard
  library and under their pip names; takes the title from the folder's own
  README; marks missing authors "unknown"; shows variable tables only when
  there are labels; writes no dataset_description.json without data.
- The R, Mplus and Stata output readers pad lines in characters instead of
  with formatC(), which dropped a backslash and split columns wrongly.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Scripts keep their folders inside analysis/
recent_commits.body:
psychds_file_plan() put every script flat in analysis/, so two scripts
with one name collided and code that finds its own modules by folder
stopped working. A script now keeps its folders below the folder all
scripts of its study share.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() converts a local folder and never goes online; identical files are left out; READMEs in subfolders keep their folder; archives of your own are not unpacked into your folder
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo(path, output_dir, paper) now converts a folder on the
researcher's own computer, running the checks as report_repository()
does, with local_only for every check. Nothing is downloaded, no link is
followed, and the folder is not changed. The paper is optional and gives
the title, authors, CRediT roles and funding. Online sources, result
reuse and the download arguments are removed.

A file from an archive that is identical to a file next to it, and a
README identical to another, are left out and listed in CHANGES.md. A data
file that holds no table is kept as it is instead of reported as failed,
and two different originals with one name no longer overwrite each other.
Paths of the folder are removed from the saved check results.

psychds_file_plan() puts a README in a subfolder in documentation/, named
after its folder; every README went to the top and they replaced each
other. .archive_dest() unpacks next to itself only an archive metacheck
downloaded; any archive in the temporary folder counted, so an uploaded
folder got a "<zip>.contents" folder written into it.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: FAIR_repo() writes a reorganised, documented copy of a paper's repository; reproducibility_check copies same-named files from their own place and changes only quoted paths
recent_commits.body:
FAIR_repo() places every file where the Psych-DS layout puts it, writes
non-CSV data as CSV next to the original, changes the paths and setwd()
lines of R and Python scripts, and writes dataset_description.json,
ro-crate-metadata.json, a README (only where the repository has none),
requirements.txt, CHANGES.md and logs/. It reuses the checks in a captured
result and runs only the missing ones.

reproducibility_check looked up a file's copy by name and took the first,
so same-named files from different folders got one file's content, and it
replaced a path wherever its text appeared, so x.csv also changed
"old_x.csv".
recent_commits.author: Lakens

but truncated them, so `n = 100 * 0.29` (28.999999999999996) was shown as 28

every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.

recent_commits.message: Round, not truncate, n and digits_* to integer
recent_commits.body:
* `as_integer_if_lossless()` admits values within tolerance of a whole number
but truncated them, so `n = 100 * 0.29` (28.999999999999996) was shown as 28
next to the verdict for 29. b8536d3 extended this to `digits_*`: a
`digits_x` just below 2 was shown as 1, and `grim_map_seq()` then failed.
* `function_map()` and `function_map_seq()` turn `digits_*` into integers
before testing or dispersing, so the column is the value used. Non-numeric
input passes through unchanged, for `fn()`'s own error.
* Two long lines in `R/utils.R` and `R/function-map.R` formatted with air.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check only single-value defaults for length in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 required every setting to be length 1, so a mapper made from a
`.fn` with a setting such as `bounds = NULL` or `scale = c(1, 7)` failed on
every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the length error for length-2 settings in two stale tests
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 checks every setting's length before its value, so
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` and `percent = c(TRUE, FALSE)` now fail with
"must be length 1, not 2". Two expectations still had the old wording.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the digits_* columns as integers in all mapper tiers
recent_commits.body:
* `n` was already integer when lossless, but `digits_x` and `digits_sd` were
double although they are always whole numbers. `function_map()` and
`function_map_seq()` now pass them through `as_integer_if_lossless()`; the
total-n tier inherits the basic mapper's columns.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut NEWS items that describe changes since 0.6.1 only within the branch
recent_commits.body:
* Each item was checked against scrutiny 0.6.1, installed from main. Dropped:
the integer `digits_*` columns, the `items = 2` partial match, the error for
two key arguments naming one column, the `grim_binomial()` and
`grim_plot_rates()` clause, GRIMMER running indefinitely, the integer
`diff_var`, `1e-300` having 315 decimal places, and mappers failing under
`lapply()`.
* Reworded items that 0.6.1 handled differently from the stated earlier
state: a seq mapper with nothing to disperse already warned, and a total-n
case without group pairs failed rather than vanishing.
* `grim_map(percent = TRUE)` now says that `x` stays a percentage, which is
the actual change from 0.6.1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require every setting to be length 1 in the mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers checked the settings with `check_lengths_congruent()`,
which allowed one of them to be longer than 1. An enum such as
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` then reached `rlang::arg_match()`,
whose error says it is 'not "se"', though "se" is valid; `percent =
c(TRUE, FALSE)` reached the test. The vectorized functions had their
own length-1 check with a better message.

* `check_setting_length()` is that check, shared by `map_value_sets()`,
`function_map()`, and the total-n factory, which reads an enum before
`fn()` does. In the mappers it runs after `check_rounding_args()`, which
keeps its own message for the rounding arguments.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` had no caller left and is deleted with its
tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
recent_commits.body:
* `check_values_size()` formatted the value set with `format()`'s
default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.body:
- R/api-keys.R: each key is read from an option first and an environment
  variable second, checked once per R session, and left out with a warning
  when the service refuses it. A refused key or a reached limit is recorded in
  a state folder all R sessions share (METACHECK_STATE_DIR), and
  api_key_status() gives the message for the visitor. api_keys_use() sets a
  visitor's own keys for one job. New github_pat() and openalex_key().
- GitHub, GitLab, OSF, Dataverse, Dryad, ResearchBox and OpenAlex use this;
  keys go only to their own host; a GitHub or GitLab limit now reports the
  repository as not listed instead of empty; ResearchBox's count of "unfound"
  answers moved to the state folder, where it is no longer lost after each job.
- osf_app(): a wrong typed token no longer clears OSF_PAT.
- The three apps: a folded box "Your own API keys (optional)" and a notice
  when a key of the server was refused or used up; the keys go to the
  visitor's own job only. The plumber API takes key_<service> fields.
- Tests: setup.R's resets now run when all tests have run (teardown_env());
  before, they ran at once, so tests wrote to the package source and the
  user's own state folder. test-app-repocheck.R puts metacheck.repo_cache.dir
  back after the app's job.

recent_commits.body:
Batch of fixes from a two-model check of 10 never-processed psychology papers and
from defects reported by downstream consumers. See CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Normalization
- extract_pdf runs one pdftotext -bbox pass (restore_line_end_hyphens=True) so
  plain-text callers get the layout-gated hyphen restores; a failed pass is
  recorded as line_end_hyphen_words_unavailable.
- W0v restores a hyphen inside a DOI broken at a line end; W0t handles compounds
  of three or more parts; W0u adjacency fix.
- S6u rejoins a URL or DOI broken across a line; capital-initials and list
  numbers keep the break. A list number is no longer glued onto the previous DOI.
- S0h keeps hyphens in documents whose font encodes the printed hyphen as U+00AD
  (document-level gate).
- P0t strips running titles repeated on later pages, publisher watermark
  sentences and "Downloaded from" stamps; ORCID URLs and supplementary-material
  body lines are kept.

Tables
- fields_raw on every flattened record (printed tokens).
- Typed descriptive pairs (M (SD), b (SE), n (%), est [CI]) with fields["group"]
  per arm column; new keys SE, count, pct.
- Nested spanning headers are not read as arm groups.
- Caption, label and running-head rows leave the grid for the caption; text-only
  tables keep their data rows out of the header.
- A captionless page directly continuing the previous table is linked
  (continuation_of, caption_status "continuation").

Sections and references
- Reference numbers separated from their entries are paired back via layout.
- Group, bare-surname and full-first-name authors start their own entry.
- A wrapped "Supplemental Materials." no longer opens a false section; an
  unheaded abstract of 1200-1500 characters is kept.

Tests: 4309 passed. Snapshot checksums re-pinned for 11 fixtures after verifying
every changed line is a hyphen insertion. 125-paper render diff reviewed: no
statistic lost.

recent_commits.message: Round, not truncate, n and digits_* to integer
recent_commits.body:
* `as_integer_if_lossless()` admits values within tolerance of a whole number
but truncated them, so `n = 100 * 0.29` (28.999999999999996) was shown as 28
next to the verdict for 29. b8536d3 extended this to `digits_*`: a
`digits_x` just below 2 was shown as 1, and `grim_map_seq()` then failed.
* `function_map()` and `function_map_seq()` turn `digits_*` into integers
before testing or dispersing, so the column is the value used. Non-numeric
input passes through unchanged, for `fn()`'s own error.
* Two long lines in `R/utils.R` and `R/function-map.R` formatted with air.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check only single-value defaults for length in function_map()
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 required every setting to be length 1, so a mapper made from a
`.fn` with a setting such as `bounds = NULL` or `scale = c(1, 7)` failed on
every call, even at its default. Only settings whose default is a single
value are checked now; enums count, since their default resolves to one
string.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Expect the length error for length-2 settings in two stale tests
recent_commits.body:
* d540b95 checks every setting's length before its value, so
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` and `percent = c(TRUE, FALSE)` now fail with
"must be length 1, not 2". Two expectations still had the old wording.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the digits_* columns as integers in all mapper tiers
recent_commits.body:
* `n` was already integer when lossless, but `digits_x` and `digits_sd` were
double although they are always whole numbers. `function_map()` and
`function_map_seq()` now pass them through `as_integer_if_lossless()`; the
total-n tier inherits the basic mapper's columns.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut NEWS items that describe changes since 0.6.1 only within the branch
recent_commits.body:
* Each item was checked against scrutiny 0.6.1, installed from main. Dropped:
the integer `digits_*` columns, the `items = 2` partial match, the error for
two key arguments naming one column, the `grim_binomial()` and
`grim_plot_rates()` clause, GRIMMER running indefinitely, the integer
`diff_var`, `1e-300` having 315 decimal places, and mappers failing under
`lapply()`.
* Reworded items that 0.6.1 handled differently from the stated earlier
state: a seq mapper with nothing to disperse already warned, and a total-n
case without group pairs failed rather than vanishing.
* `grim_map(percent = TRUE)` now says that `x` stays a percentage, which is
the actual change from 0.6.1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Require every setting to be length 1 in the mappers
recent_commits.body:
* The mappers checked the settings with `check_lengths_congruent()`,
which allowed one of them to be longer than 1. An enum such as
`sd_meaning = c("se", "sd_pop")` then reached `rlang::arg_match()`,
whose error says it is 'not "se"', though "se" is valid; `percent =
c(TRUE, FALSE)` reached the test. The vectorized functions had their
own length-1 check with a better message.

* `check_setting_length()` is that check, shared by `map_value_sets()`,
`function_map()`, and the total-n factory, which reads an enum before
`fn()` does. In the mappers it runs after `check_rounding_args()`, which
keeps its own message for the rounding arguments.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` had no caller left and is deleted with its
tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare x to a power of 10 in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `abs(x) >= 10^(15 - digits)` is the same condition as the one on
`floor(log10(abs(x)))`, but exact for every power of ten, so it needs
no correction for `log10()` rounding up just below one. The count in
the message comes from the integer part written out.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the reported values in full in the size error
recent_commits.body:
* `check_values_size()` formatted the value set with `format()`'s
default 7 significant digits, so a reported `x = 0.123456789` was
named as `x = 0.1234568`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name items_averaged in the size error of the values functions
recent_commits.body:
* Two value sets that differ only in `items_averaged` read the same in
the message otherwise.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave one or two missing strings undecided in is_seq_linear()
recent_commits.body:
* A logical or numeric `NA` is some number, and any two numbers are
linear, but a missing string could be no number at all, so
`is_seq_linear(c(NA_character_, NA_character_))` is `NA` again.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check an enum in the total-n mappers before n_min_fn() reads it
recent_commits.body:
* `n_min_fn()` ran on the raw settings, so a two-value or `NULL`
`sd_meaning` failed in `sd_min_n()` with a plain R error instead of
the mapper's own. Each enum given is now validated with
`arg_match_in_export()` right after `resolve_enums()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count the integer digits of x exactly in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `floor(log10(abs(x)))` rounds up to the next whole number just below a
power of 10, so 999999999999999 and 99999.9999999999 were rejected as
having 16 significant digits. The exponent is now corrected downward
when `10^exponent` exceeds `abs(x)`, as in `next_square_root()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a value with more than 15 significant digits
recent_commits.body:
* check_newly_numeric() capped digits_x at 15 but not the integer
digits of x, so 33.33333333333333 with digits_x = 14 passed although a
double does not hold 16 significant digits and the tests are not exact
there. The sum of the two is now capped at 15.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for two values with an infinity among them
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(c(1, Inf)) was FALSE: the step Inf - 1 is Inf, which
dplyr::near() cannot compare to itself. Any two values are linear, so
the step check only runs for three or more.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve a NULL n_min to the default in every total-n mapper
recent_commits.body:
* Only the function-valued .n_min branch replaced a NULL, so
grim_map_total_n(n_min = NULL) passed it on to disperse_total(), which
dispersed down to a group of 0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Report a missing required argument on a 0-row data frame, too
recent_commits.body:
* A mapper tests its first row on its own so that a missing digits_x or
items_averaged is reported by the test function. With no row to test,
the check was skipped and the mapper returned an empty tibble. It now
tests a row of missing values if a required argument is missing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole set in every tier
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS) failed in sd_min_n(),
since the total-n factory reads the settings for n_min before fn()
runs, from the values as given. grimmer(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS)
failed the length check for the same reason, while grimmer_map()
accepted the set.

* The resolution to the first string, as rlang::arg_match() would do
it, is one helper now, resolve_enums(), with eval_enum_defaults() for
the sets, used by function_map(), function_map_total_n(), and
map_value_sets().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for a linear sequence that no missing value could break
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(NA) and is_seq_linear(c(NA, NA)) were NA, although any
one or two values are linear, so the missing values could not change
the answer. NA is only for a question that they could decide either
way, as the too-short case returning FALSE already assumed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give a seq mapper's zero-row output the columns of its usual output
recent_commits.body:
* With no case to disperse from, the fallback kept every column of the
basic mapper's output, while the re-tests drop the columns of data that
play no role in the test. The fallback now keeps what is left of the
key result column plus the columns fn() added.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return FALSE for an all-NA vector too short for the sequence
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(NA) was NA while is_seq_ascending(5) was FALSE: the
all-NA rule ran before the length check, although no values could make
a single one ascending. The length check comes first now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let the total-n mappers' n_min follow sd_meaning
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n() and debit_map_total_n() had n_min = 2 whatever
the sd_meaning, so under "sd_pop" or "sd_sample_or_pop", where a group
of 1 has an SD, such pairs were silently left out. The seq tier already
adapted its out_min through sd_min_n().

* function_map_total_n() takes a function of the settings as .n_min, as
function_map_seq() does for .var_bounds. The manufactured function's
n_min then defaults to NULL, which the body resolves, and the resolved
value is what the recorded setting counts as the default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Document that "ties_even" shares the bounds of "even"
recent_commits.body:
* roundwork gives both methods inclusive bounds on both sides, since
base::round() decides a tie on the binary double, so grim(5.3, 4, 1, 1,
rounding = "ties_even") is TRUE although 21 / 4 rounds to 5.2 in
decimal. The docs mentioned the exception for "even" only.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep grim_explain()'s example means apart from the bounds of x
recent_commits.body:
* divide() formatted a sum divided by n without the bounds to avoid, so
with n above 10^digits_x the shown mean landed on a stated bound:
499 / 999 printed as 0.4995, the bound it falls short of, and the text
contradicted itself. It passes the bounds now, as debit_explain() does
for its SDs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole default set
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() resolved an enum setting such as sd_meaning to its
first string only when it was missing. One given as the whole set, as a
wrapper forwarding its own default does, passed arg_match_in_export()
but was recorded as the set in the "scrutiny" attribute, so
grimmer_map_seq() and debit_map_seq() then failed in sd_min_n().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test grouped data in the total-n mappers, reserve the constant column
recent_commits.body:
* The total-n factory picked the reported columns with dplyr::select(),
which adds the grouping columns of a grouped tibble back in, so the
column count no longer matched the pairs and the proto function failed
with a conversion error. The basic and seq tiers were fine with grouped
input. It subsets with `[` now.

* A `constant` column of `data` silently overwrote the values of the
`constant` argument. It is an error now, like the other result columns,
but only if the argument is given.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: API keys work the same way for every repository, and visitors can use their own when the server's run out
recent_commits.body:
- R/api-keys.R: each key is read from an option first and an environment
  variable second, checked once per R session, and left out with a warning
  when the service refuses it. A refused key or a reached limit is recorded in
  a state folder all R sessions share (METACHECK_STATE_DIR), and
  api_key_status() gives the message for the visitor. api_keys_use() sets a
  visitor's own keys for one job. New github_pat() and openalex_key().
- GitHub, GitLab, OSF, Dataverse, Dryad, ResearchBox and OpenAlex use this;
  keys go only to their own host; a GitHub or GitLab limit now reports the
  repository as not listed instead of empty; ResearchBox's count of "unfound"
  answers moved to the state folder, where it is no longer lost after each job.
- osf_app(): a wrong typed token no longer clears OSF_PAT.
- The three apps: a folded box "Your own API keys (optional)" and a notice
  when a key of the server was refused or used up; the keys go to the
  visitor's own job only. The plumber API takes key_<service> fields.
- Tests: setup.R's resets now run when all tests have run (teardown_env());
  before, they ran at once, so tests wrote to the package source and the
  user's own state folder. test-app-repocheck.R puts metacheck.repo_cache.dir
  back after the app's job.

recent_commits.message: test: pin that an unavailable Camelot patch is recorded; use a placeholder id in the hygiene-guard probe
recent_commits.body:
The two Camelot patch installers (cell join, row-boundary tie) return False
when Camelot is absent or has changed shape; their scopes record an
unavailable event. Nothing asserted that, so the capability could vanish with
every table test green. Three tests now pin the event on both scopes and its
absence on a healthy install.

The hygiene guard's positive probe quoted a real-looking private ledger id.
It now uses a placeholder with the same shape.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): the non-statistic scan folds a soft hyphen to nothing, not to a dash
recent_commits.body:
S6 deletes U+00AD, so a URL with soft hyphens correctly becomes the clean URL.
The scan folded U+00AD to '-' and reported that strip as a rewritten URL on two
corpus papers, exiting 1 on a healthy tree. Adds a regression test with a
red control.

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): separated values still read as data; a merged cell's sentinel is not a word
recent_commits.body:
A cell of space-separated values ('52.96 36.06', which Camelot used to glue
into one pattern-matching string) counts as data, so a study row is not taken
for the header and its df is not copied onto every record. A thousands-grouped
count ('177 709') keeps its previous reading. The worded-interval check ignores
the continuation-merge sentinel, so a merged '0.79 [0.68, 0.89]' still gives d.

recent_commits.message: Leave one or two missing strings undecided in is_seq_linear()
recent_commits.body:

linear, but a missing string could be no number at all, so
`is_seq_linear(c(NA_character_, NA_character_))` is `NA` again.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check an enum in the total-n mappers before n_min_fn() reads it
recent_commits.body:
* `n_min_fn()` ran on the raw settings, so a two-value or `NULL`
`sd_meaning` failed in `sd_min_n()` with a plain R error instead of
the mapper's own. Each enum given is now validated with
`arg_match_in_export()` right after `resolve_enums()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count the integer digits of x exactly in the 15-digit check
recent_commits.body:
* `floor(log10(abs(x)))` rounds up to the next whole number just below a
power of 10, so 999999999999999 and 99999.9999999999 were rejected as
having 16 significant digits. The exponent is now corrected downward
when `10^exponent` exceeds `abs(x)`, as in `next_square_root()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a value with more than 15 significant digits
recent_commits.body:
* check_newly_numeric() capped digits_x at 15 but not the integer
digits of x, so 33.33333333333333 with digits_x = 14 passed although a
double does not hold 16 significant digits and the tests are not exact
there. The sum of the two is now capped at 15.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for two values with an infinity among them
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(c(1, Inf)) was FALSE: the step Inf - 1 is Inf, which
dplyr::near() cannot compare to itself. Any two values are linear, so
the step check only runs for three or more.

recent_commits.message: Report a missing required argument on a 0-row data frame, too
recent_commits.body:
* A mapper tests its first row on its own so that a missing digits_x or
items_averaged is reported by the test function. With no row to test,
the check was skipped and the mapper returned an empty tibble. It now
tests a row of missing values if a required argument is missing.

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole set in every tier
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS) failed in sd_min_n(),
since the total-n factory reads the settings for n_min before fn()
runs, from the values as given. grimmer(sd_meaning = SD_MEANINGS)
failed the length check for the same reason, while grimmer_map()
accepted the set.

* The resolution to the first string, as rlang::arg_match() would do
it, is one helper now, resolve_enums(), with eval_enum_defaults() for
the sets, used by function_map(), function_map_total_n(), and
map_value_sets().

recent_commits.message: Return TRUE for a linear sequence that no missing value could break
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(NA) and is_seq_linear(c(NA, NA)) were NA, although any
one or two values are linear, so the missing values could not change
the answer. NA is only for a question that they could decide either
way, as the too-short case returning FALSE already assumed.

recent_commits.message: Give a seq mapper's zero-row output the columns of its usual output
recent_commits.body:
* With no case to disperse from, the fallback kept every column of the
basic mapper's output, while the re-tests drop the columns of data that
play no role in the test. The fallback now keeps what is left of the
key result column plus the columns fn() added.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return FALSE for an all-NA vector too short for the sequence
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_ascending(NA) was NA while is_seq_ascending(5) was FALSE: the
all-NA rule ran before the length check, although no values could make
a single one ascending. The length check comes first now.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let the total-n mappers' n_min follow sd_meaning
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_total_n() and debit_map_total_n() had n_min = 2 whatever
the sd_meaning, so under "sd_pop" or "sd_sample_or_pop", where a group
of 1 has an SD, such pairs were silently left out. The seq tier already
adapted its out_min through sd_min_n().

* function_map_total_n() takes a function of the settings as .n_min, as
function_map_seq() does for .var_bounds. The manufactured function's
n_min then defaults to NULL, which the body resolves, and the resolved
value is what the recorded setting counts as the default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Document that "ties_even" shares the bounds of "even"
recent_commits.body:
* roundwork gives both methods inclusive bounds on both sides, since
base::round() decides a tie on the binary double, so grim(5.3, 4, 1, 1,
rounding = "ties_even") is TRUE although 21 / 4 rounds to 5.2 in
decimal. The docs mentioned the exception for "even" only.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep grim_explain()'s example means apart from the bounds of x
recent_commits.body:
* divide() formatted a sum divided by n without the bounds to avoid, so
with n above 10^digits_x the shown mean landed on a stated bound:
499 / 999 printed as 0.4995, the bound it falls short of, and the text
contradicted itself. It passes the bounds now, as debit_explain() does
for its SDs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve an enum given as its whole default set
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() resolved an enum setting such as sd_meaning to its
first string only when it was missing. One given as the whole set, as a
wrapper forwarding its own default does, passed arg_match_in_export()
but was recorded as the set in the "scrutiny" attribute, so
grimmer_map_seq() and debit_map_seq() then failed in sd_min_n().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test grouped data in the total-n mappers, reserve the constant column
recent_commits.body:
* The total-n factory picked the reported columns with dplyr::select(),
which adds the grouping columns of a grouped tibble back in, so the
column count no longer matched the pairs and the proto function failed
with a conversion error. The basic and seq tiers were fine with grouped
input. It subsets with `[` now.

* A `constant` column of `data` silently overwrote the values of the
`constant` argument. It is an error now, like the other result columns,
but only if the argument is given.

recent_commits.body:
The two Camelot patch installers (cell join, row-boundary tie) return False
when Camelot is absent or has changed shape; their scopes record an
unavailable event. Nothing asserted that, so the capability could vanish with
every table test green. Three tests now pin the event on both scopes and its
absence on a healthy install.

The hygiene guard's positive probe quoted a real-looking private ledger id.
It now uses a placeholder with the same shape.

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.

recent_commits.message: Name the value set in the size error, test the limit at its boundary
recent_commits.body:
* check_values_size() now names x, sd, and n of the value set that is
too large; in a vectorized call, nothing said which one it was.

* A test sets VALUES_MAX to the exact number of rows for n = 30, 4, 3,
and 2 and for grim_values(): each passes at the limit and errors one
below it.

* The n = 100 cap case is compared pair by pair with its independent
enumeration, not only by count.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the rules for three and four numbers in one place
recent_commits.body:
* sum_squares_attainable() scanned for its first sum of squares with
the rules for n = 3 and 4 written out a second time. It now takes the
first window of sum_squares_attainable_all(), which no longer assumes
that `first` is attainable itself, and whose windows start at 8 and
double up to the chunk size, so that the usual early hit stays cheap.
is_loeschian() moves to the test helpers, its only remaining user.

* loeschian_between() clamps by subassignment instead of pmax() and
tabulates instead of sort(), which cost some 20 and 20 microseconds on
the few numbers of a window: 45 microseconds per call before, 10 now.
grimmer() at n = 3 and 4 is still about 10% slower than with the
dedicated scan, on 40,000 value sets taken from samples.

* The test of sum_squares_attainable_all() was circular now that one
calls the other, so it is checked against every sample of up to four
numbers from -6 to 6 instead, from every start. An empty range returned
NULL rather than numeric(0).
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Check the grimmer_values() cap cases against independent counts
recent_commits.body:
* The 199,990 pairs at x = 50, sd = 20, n = 100 were only the
implementation's own count. The test now derives them in whole numbers
from the rounding bounds alone, sharing no code with the package.

* The n = 2 case only had to stay below 1e5 rows. It is now compared pair
by pair with an enumeration of two totals by their sum and difference:
14,271 pairs, each with the sum of squares (s^2 + d^2) / 2.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the number of means that grim_values() returns
recent_commits.body:
* grim_values() had no limit: n = 1e8 with digits_x = 0 built 2 GB, and
a typo of one more digit would end the session. Like grimmer_values(),
it now errors above a million values per value set, before allocating
them. grim_closest() needs no cap and has none.

* The GRIM vignette shows how to join the output back onto the data by
case, now that the list-column example is gone.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count grimmer_values() pairs exactly, in linear time for n < 5
recent_commits.body:
* For n < 5, each sum's sums of squares were appended with c(), the
quadratic pattern ff3c9d8 removed one level up: 18.6 s for 752k rows at
n = 4, items_averaged = 15. sum_squares_attainable_all() now finds them
in chunks, with a vectorized is_sum_three_squares() for n = 4 and
loeschian_between() for n = 3, which generates the numbers as
x^2 + xy + y^2 rather than testing each with a scan of sqrt(m). That
call takes 0.2 s now, and 286k rows at n = 3 take 0.15 s instead of 19 s.

* The cap of 2694a56 counted every second sum of squares, an upper
bound that is far too high for n = 2, whose sums of squares are sparse:
x = 50, sd = 20, n = 2, items_averaged = 100 was refused as "up to
40,200,101 pairs" and has 14,271. The pairs are now counted as they are
found, and enumeration for n < 5 stops one past the limit.

* check_values_size() and VALUES_MAX hold the limit for both *_values()
functions. The message names items_averaged and sd along with n, which
drive the count as much, and ?grimmer_values states the limit.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cap the number of pairs that grimmer_values() enumerates
recent_commits.body:
* check_enumeration_size() caps the candidate sums at 1e6, but the pairs
grow with n^2 for SDs with few decimal places: x = 50, sd = 20, n = 5000,
both with no decimals, admit 5e8 pairs, some 20 GB over five columns, so
the call died instead of erroring. The count is known before anything is
allocated, from the first and last sum of squares each candidate sum
admits, and above 1e6 it is now the same kind of error as for the sums.
For n < 5 it is an upper bound, since fewer numbers skip some sums of
squares.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return one tibble from grim_values() and grimmer_values()
recent_commits.body:
* Instead of a list with one tibble per value set, both return a single
tibble with a case column, the index of the value set, as *_map_seq()
output has. Nearly every call has one value set, which no longer needs
to be unwrapped; many value sets give one table keyed by case.

* An inconsistent value set has no rows, as in *_map_seq() output, and
an undecidable one keeps its row of NA, so it stays visible.
bind_cases() does the stacking for both wrappers, with the zero-row
tibbles from aaa.R for a call with no value sets.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give grim_values() and grimmer_values() the same shape
recent_commits.body:
* Both return one tibble per value set now. grim_values() gains a sum
column next to x, as grimmer_values() has sum and sum_squares, so the
whole number behind a mean is exact rather than multiplied back from
the mean. An undecidable value set is one row of NA in both, so the
element is a tibble either way: a bare NA next to tibbles broke
purrr::list_rbind(), tidyr::unnest(), and purrr::map_int(nrow).

* grimmer_values() collected its pairs by appending to a vector per
candidate sum, which copied the vector each time: 40 s at n = 20000 and
263 s at n = 40000. One list element per sum, joined once at the end,
takes 0.3 s at n = 20000.

* Drop show_reason = TRUE from the grimmer_scalar() call, whose reason
was discarded. Note the "even" ties for grimmer_values() as for
grim_values(), add the issue reference to NEWS, and give the GRIMMER
vignette the section the GRIM vignette has.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add grimmer_values()
recent_commits.body:
* The sibling of grim_values() for GRIMMER: every pair of a mean and an
SD that n whole numbers can have and that would be reported as x and
sd, with the whole-number sum and sum of squares behind each. Through
the integers, a statistic computed from several groups can be compared
exactly, which is what GRIMMEST needs (#59).

* The verdict and the argument checks come from grimmer_scalar(); the
enumeration goes through grimmer_candidate() and, for n < 5,
sum_squares_attainable(). Nothing in the existing code changed.

* sd_meaning = "sd_sample_or_pop" is an error: the same sum of squares
gives a different SD under each premise.

* grimmer_reachable_pairs() moves to helper.R so that the new tests can
check the pairs against the brute force in both directions.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Correct the verdict changes described in NEWS.md
recent_commits.body:
* A comparison with scrutiny 0.6.1 on a sample of 40,000 GRIMMER value
  sets showed that #80 is no rare edge case: wherever several sums round
  to the mean, a fifth of 0.6.1's inconsistencies were false positives
  for means with one decimal place, and 3% for two. The fix moves to
  "Test results", covers test 1 as well as test 3, and credits the
  reporters. The introduction no longer calls the GRIMMER changes rare.
* The #85 conjunction bug did not need three candidates; it is its own
  bullet now, with a runnable example.
* A mean of 0.00 under "anti_trunc" used to be FALSE, not NA.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename fun and .fun to fn and .fn
recent_commits.body:
* The factories' `.fun` argument is now `.fn`, and every internal `fun`,

  `name_fun` thereby becomes the `name_fn` already used elsewhere.
* `ggplot2::geom_function(fun)` keeps its name.
* The locals that a scalar function's arguments must not shadow now

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

the continuation-merge sentinel, so a merged '0.79 [0.68, 0.89]' still gives d.

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.

recent_commits.message: Replace sd_type with sd_meaning and add an SE premise
recent_commits.body:
* sd_type = c("sample", "population", "either") becomes sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se") in grimmer(), debit(), and all their mappers, explanations, and plots. Each value is one premise about what a value reported as an SD really is: an SD of some kind, or a misreported SE.
* "se" is the standard error of the mean, the sample SD divided by sqrt(n). Its rounding bounds are transformed, not the reported value: sd_denominator() gives n * (n - 1) for it, and every path from the reported value to a sum of squares or a binary spread goes through that function.
* One argument rather than a second, combinable one, because few combinations of statistic and denominator occur in practice; a new premise of the same form is one row in sd_denominator().
* Brute-force tests check GRIMMER and DEBIT under "se" against every reachable sample.
* The docs warn that the test is weak under "se": from about n = 20 on, nearly every GRIM-consistent value set passes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.

recent_commits.message: Update README
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Replace sd_type with sd_meaning and add an SE premise
recent_commits.body:
* sd_type = c("sample", "population", "either") becomes sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se") in grimmer(), debit(), and all their mappers, explanations, and plots. Each value is one premise about what a value reported as an SD really is: an SD of some kind, or a misreported SE.
* "se" is the standard error of the mean, the sample SD divided by sqrt(n). Its rounding bounds are transformed, not the reported value: sd_denominator() gives n * (n - 1) for it, and every path from the reported value to a sum of squares or a binary spread goes through that function.
* One argument rather than a second, combinable one, because few combinations of statistic and denominator occur in practice; a new premise of the same form is one row in sd_denominator().
* Brute-force tests check GRIMMER and DEBIT under "se" against every reachable sample.
* The docs warn that the test is weak under "se": from about n = 20 on, nearly every GRIM-consistent value set passes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Tell basic settings from tier settings by name in scrutiny_args()
recent_commits.body:
* scrutiny_args() took the rows added by the same mapper as the first row. If a basic mapper recorded no settings, the first row was the sequence or total-n mapper's, whose settings were then read as the basic ones.
* The function_map() comment on missing values says where such a value can still come from: a .fun written elsewhere with a lifecycle::deprecated() default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name row 1 in a mapper error that is about that row
recent_commits.body:
* The first row is tested on its own before the others, outside the handler that names the row, so only errors in later rows said where they came from.
* An error there now names row 1 if row 2 passes the test. An error about the arguments, such as a missing `digits_x`, fails on every row and still names none.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep only character row names of a data frame passed to a mapper
recent_commits.body:
* Integer row names, as left by `data[rows, ]`, counted as non-automatic, so a common base R subset gained a `rowname` column of row numbers.
* A data frame with row names and a `rowname` column failed with dplyr's "duplicate names" error; it now says what clashes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add dots to the example audit() methods
recent_commits.body: * The example `audit()` methods in `?audit_cols_minimal` and the simple extension vignette take the dots, as the generic now requires; a package copying `function(data)` got an S3 consistency warning from R CMD check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the dispersed variables from the settings in audit_seq()
recent_commits.body:
* e9af559 moved `var` from the "scrutiny" attribute into its settings tibble, but the branch for output with rows still read `meta$var`. It fell back to the `var` column, so a variable whose dispersion `out_min` or `out_max` clipped away in every case lost its `hits_*` and `diff_*` columns.
* Both branches now read it from the settings, once.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add audit(.by) and explain a class lost to group_by()
recent_commits.body:
* audit() is now audit(data, ..., .by = NULL). With .by, it splits data with [, which keeps class and attribute, summarizes each group, and binds the results behind the grouping columns, in order of appearance.
* group_by() drops the mapper class but keeps the attribute, so audit.default() and explain_map.default() recognize such data and point to the output from before grouping. Other data get a plain no-method error instead of R's.
* Every audit() method takes the dots now, as R CMD check requires; the extension vignette shows the new signature.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the recorded settings as a tibble from scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records a settings tibble: setting, value, default, and added_by. Sequence and total-n mappers append their own settings, such as dispersion, which were not recorded before.
* scrutiny_meta() shows each value as R code in single quotes, which pillar prints without escaping. Package code reads typed values with the internal scrutiny_args().
* default compares each value to the defaults evaluated when the factory made the mapper, so the print header no longer needs the mapper passed in. The bookkeeping for audit_seq() stays in the attribute but out of the tibble; var is now a settings row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Print the settings header with a single space after the name
recent_commits.body: * pillar pads header names to the widest, "A tibble", unless none is named, so the methods write the names into the lines themselves.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name non-default settings in the print header of mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* pillar::tbl_sum() methods for the four basic mapper classes compare the recorded args with the mapper's own defaults, so the attribute needs no new element. Sequence and total-n output gets the line through the basic class.
* scrutiny_meta()'s docs say which elements every mapper records and which only sequence mappers add, and that items_averaged and the digits are columns, not args.
* Unlink the write_doc_audit*() topics, which are no longer documented.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Update two tests for debit_map(show_rec)
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain multi-item percentages under items_averaged
recent_commits.body: * Percent correct on a k-item test and pooled proportions over k trials need items_averaged = k, so 1 is not right for every percentage.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add an article on interpreting results
recent_commits.body:
* Lists the benign causes of an inconsistency (rounding, sample size, scale items, SD convention, other totals, non-integer data, typos), with the scrutiny call that checks each.
* Lays out the workflow from mapper to audit, seq, explanations, and scrutiny_meta(), and says how to weigh and report the evidence.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Mark new functions experimental, state a stability policy, and unexport write_doc_audit*()
recent_commits.body:
* Every export new since 0.6.1 carries the experimental badge; functions released before keep their status.
* The pkgdown reference index says developer tools may change in minor releases.
* write_doc_audit(), write_doc_audit_seq(), and write_doc_audit_total_n() generate roxygen text and serve no analysis, so they are internal now. The extension vignette points to the help pages for the conventions instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the row of data in per-row mapper errors
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() re-signals the test's error in place of purrr's indexed one, adding the row. Total-n mappers translate the scenario row into the row of data.
* Document that percent applies per call, with a split-and-bind example, and that total-n digits apply to every row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Hide debit_map()'s reconstructed values by default
recent_commits.body:
* show_rec now defaults to FALSE, as in grim_map(), so the eight bound and sum columns are only returned on request.
* debit_plot() recomputes them under the recorded settings when they are missing, so plotting default output still works.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make seq_disperse() return numbers and drop string_output
recent_commits.body:
* The strings were a holdover from when the mappers took x as a string. The mappers already passed string_output = "auto" with a numeric x, so their output is unchanged.
* A string from still sets the step size, trailing zeros included; the docs point to by for a number like 5.30.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the global variables of function_duplicate_cols()
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove duplicate_detect()
recent_commits.body:
* Superseded since 0.3.0 by duplicate_tally(), which counts duplicates instead of only flagging them.
* With one product left, function_duplicate_cols() is inlined into duplicate_tally(), whose file is renamed to match it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove the deprecated tolerance argument
recent_commits.body: * grim(), grimmer(), and their mappers compare exact integers, so the argument never had an effect. Removing it at 1.0.0 saves carrying the deprecation to 2.0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Export scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records the settings of the call that produced
a mapper's output, but nothing exported read it, so a report could not
state the rounding method or SD convention behind a verdict. The internal
accessor moves to its own file with documentation of the list's elements.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record reported verdicts for audit_seq() instead of re-testing
recent_commits.body:
* The sequence mapper stores the verdict of every input row from its
initial test as `results_reported` in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
`audit_seq()` indexes it by `case`.

* `audit_seq()` used to recover the mapper's name from a class string,
look the function up in the caller's environment, and replay the
call's arguments from a `fun_args` element, so a dropped argument could
flip the verdict and the mapper had to be findable from wherever
`audit_seq()` ran. `find_fun_by_name()` and `fun_args` are gone; output
that has lost the attribute errors, as `explain_map()` does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Accept any data frame as mapper input
recent_commits.body:
* `check_tibble()` rejected a `data.frame` with a conversion hint, so
tables from `read.csv()` or a PDF extractor failed on the first call.
It is now `as_tibble_input()`, which coerces any data frame to a
tibble and keeps non-automatic row names as a `rowname` column, since
a tibble has none and study labels would otherwise be lost in silence.
Anything that is not a data frame is still an error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make audit() reach every tier and guard study-level GRIM statistics
recent_commits.body:
* Sequence and total-n output carries the basic mapper's class after
its tier classes, so `audit()` dispatched to the basic method, which
counted the dispersed rows as reported cases and only printed a hint.
`audit.scrutiny_map_seq()` and `audit.scrutiny_map_total_n()` now call
`audit_seq()` and `audit_total_n()`.

* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_plot_rates()` reject sequence and total-n
output through `check_grim_map_basic()`: their rows are hypothetical
value sets, inconsistent by construction, so a p-value or rate over
them said nothing about the study, and was returned without a word.

* `check_audit_special()` is removed and `audit_cols_minimal()` loses
`name_test`; both only served the hint that `audit()` no longer needs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the review items of Oct 25
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() marked its error about a .fun whose arguments shadow
its internals as internal, which asked the user to report a bug. A user's
.fun with an argument named `data` triggers it, so it now goes through
abort_in_export() like the other checks at creation.

* map_value_sets() returns an empty vector for a wrapper with no formals
instead of failing on an empty cache key.

* .gitignore: `special-scripts/` made the three entries after it
redundant.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename vectorize_test() to map_value_sets()
recent_commits.body:
* It returns values, not a function, so it is no kind of Vectorize(); and
it serves grim_values(), grim_closest(), add_up_to(), and
is_percentage_of() too, which are no consistency tests.
* Drop the `frame` argument: it is always the caller's frame.
* Cache the missing() calls by the formals' names rather than the name the
wrapper was called under, which needed an identity check and an
empty-name branch. This makes fn_name_from_call() unused, so remove it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: test: pin that an unavailable Camelot patch is recorded; use a placeholder id in the hygiene-guard probe
recent_commits.body:
The two Camelot patch installers (cell join, row-boundary tie) return False
when Camelot is absent or has changed shape; their scopes record an
unavailable event. Nothing asserted that, so the capability could vanish with
every table test green. Three tests now pin the event on both scopes and its
absence on a healthy install.

The hygiene guard's positive probe quoted a real-looking private ledger id.
It now uses a placeholder with the same shape.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): the non-statistic scan folds a soft hyphen to nothing, not to a dash
recent_commits.body:

The scan folded U+00AD to '-' and reported that strip as a rewritten URL on two
corpus papers, exiting 1 on a healthy tree. Adds a regression test with a

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman
