recent_commits.message: Update README
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Replace sd_type with sd_meaning and add an SE premise
recent_commits.body:
* sd_type = c("sample", "population", "either") becomes sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se") in grimmer(), debit(), and all their mappers, explanations, and plots. Each value is one premise about what a value reported as an SD really is: an SD of some kind, or a misreported SE.
* "se" is the standard error of the mean, the sample SD divided by sqrt(n). Its rounding bounds are transformed, not the reported value: sd_denominator() gives n * (n - 1) for it, and every path from the reported value to a sum of squares or a binary spread goes through that function.
* One argument rather than a second, combinable one, because few combinations of statistic and denominator occur in practice; a new premise of the same form is one row in sd_denominator().
* Brute-force tests check GRIMMER and DEBIT under "se" against every reachable sample.
* The docs warn that the test is weak under "se": from about n = 20 on, nearly every GRIM-consistent value set passes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Tell basic settings from tier settings by name in scrutiny_args()
recent_commits.body:
* scrutiny_args() took the rows added by the same mapper as the first row. If a basic mapper recorded no settings, the first row was the sequence or total-n mapper's, whose settings were then read as the basic ones.
* The function_map() comment on missing values says where such a value can still come from: a .fun written elsewhere with a lifecycle::deprecated() default.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name row 1 in a mapper error that is about that row
recent_commits.body:
* The first row is tested on its own before the others, outside the handler that names the row, so only errors in later rows said where they came from.
* An error there now names row 1 if row 2 passes the test. An error about the arguments, such as a missing `digits_x`, fails on every row and still names none.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep only character row names of a data frame passed to a mapper
recent_commits.body:
* Integer row names, as left by `data[rows, ]`, counted as non-automatic, so a common base R subset gained a `rowname` column of row numbers.
* A data frame with row names and a `rowname` column failed with dplyr's "duplicate names" error; it now says what clashes.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add dots to the example audit() methods
recent_commits.body: * The example `audit()` methods in `?audit_cols_minimal` and the simple extension vignette take the dots, as the generic now requires; a package copying `function(data)` got an S3 consistency warning from R CMD check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the dispersed variables from the settings in audit_seq()
recent_commits.body:
* e9af559 moved `var` from the "scrutiny" attribute into its settings tibble, but the branch for output with rows still read `meta$var`. It fell back to the `var` column, so a variable whose dispersion `out_min` or `out_max` clipped away in every case lost its `hits_*` and `diff_*` columns.
* Both branches now read it from the settings, once.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add audit(.by) and explain a class lost to group_by()
recent_commits.body:
* audit() is now audit(data, ..., .by = NULL). With .by, it splits data with [, which keeps class and attribute, summarizes each group, and binds the results behind the grouping columns, in order of appearance.
* group_by() drops the mapper class but keeps the attribute, so audit.default() and explain_map.default() recognize such data and point to the output from before grouping. Other data get a plain no-method error instead of R's.
* Every audit() method takes the dots now, as R CMD check requires; the extension vignette shows the new signature.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Return the recorded settings as a tibble from scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records a settings tibble: setting, value, default, and added_by. Sequence and total-n mappers append their own settings, such as dispersion, which were not recorded before.
* scrutiny_meta() shows each value as R code in single quotes, which pillar prints without escaping. Package code reads typed values with the internal scrutiny_args().
* default compares each value to the defaults evaluated when the factory made the mapper, so the print header no longer needs the mapper passed in. The bookkeeping for audit_seq() stays in the attribute but out of the tibble; var is now a settings row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Print the settings header with a single space after the name
recent_commits.body: * pillar pads header names to the widest, "A tibble", unless none is named, so the methods write the names into the lines themselves.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name non-default settings in the print header of mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* pillar::tbl_sum() methods for the four basic mapper classes compare the recorded args with the mapper's own defaults, so the attribute needs no new element. Sequence and total-n output gets the line through the basic class.
* scrutiny_meta()'s docs say which elements every mapper records and which only sequence mappers add, and that items_averaged and the digits are columns, not args.
* Unlink the write_doc_audit*() topics, which are no longer documented.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Update two tests for debit_map(show_rec)
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain multi-item percentages under items_averaged
recent_commits.body: * Percent correct on a k-item test and pooled proportions over k trials need items_averaged = k, so 1 is not right for every percentage.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add an article on interpreting results
recent_commits.body:
* Lists the benign causes of an inconsistency (rounding, sample size, scale items, SD convention, other totals, non-integer data, typos), with the scrutiny call that checks each.
* Lays out the workflow from mapper to audit, seq, explanations, and scrutiny_meta(), and says how to weigh and report the evidence.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Mark new functions experimental, state a stability policy, and unexport write_doc_audit*()
recent_commits.body:
* Every export new since 0.6.1 carries the experimental badge; functions released before keep their status.
* The pkgdown reference index says developer tools may change in minor releases.
* write_doc_audit(), write_doc_audit_seq(), and write_doc_audit_total_n() generate roxygen text and serve no analysis, so they are internal now. The extension vignette points to the help pages for the conventions instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the row of data in per-row mapper errors
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() re-signals the test's error in place of purrr's indexed one, adding the row. Total-n mappers translate the scenario row into the row of data.
* Document that percent applies per call, with a split-and-bind example, and that total-n digits apply to every row.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Hide debit_map()'s reconstructed values by default
recent_commits.body:
* show_rec now defaults to FALSE, as in grim_map(), so the eight bound and sum columns are only returned on request.
* debit_plot() recomputes them under the recorded settings when they are missing, so plotting default output still works.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make seq_disperse() return numbers and drop string_output
recent_commits.body:
* The strings were a holdover from when the mappers took x as a string. The mappers already passed string_output = "auto" with a numeric x, so their output is unchanged.
* A string from still sets the step size, trailing zeros included; the docs point to by for a number like 5.30.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop the global variables of function_duplicate_cols()
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove duplicate_detect()
recent_commits.body:
* Superseded since 0.3.0 by duplicate_tally(), which counts duplicates instead of only flagging them.
* With one product left, function_duplicate_cols() is inlined into duplicate_tally(), whose file is renamed to match it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove the deprecated tolerance argument
recent_commits.body: * grim(), grimmer(), and their mappers compare exact integers, so the argument never had an effect. Removing it at 1.0.0 saves carrying the deprecation to 2.0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Export scrutiny_meta()
recent_commits.body:
* The "scrutiny" attribute records the settings of the call that produced
a mapper's output, but nothing exported read it, so a report could not
state the rounding method or SD convention behind a verdict. The internal
accessor moves to its own file with documentation of the list's elements.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record reported verdicts for audit_seq() instead of re-testing
recent_commits.body:
* The sequence mapper stores the verdict of every input row from its
initial test as `results_reported` in the "scrutiny" attribute, and
`audit_seq()` indexes it by `case`.

* `audit_seq()` used to recover the mapper's name from a class string,
look the function up in the caller's environment, and replay the
call's arguments from a `fun_args` element, so a dropped argument could
flip the verdict and the mapper had to be findable from wherever
`audit_seq()` ran. `find_fun_by_name()` and `fun_args` are gone; output
that has lost the attribute errors, as `explain_map()` does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Accept any data frame as mapper input
recent_commits.body:
* `check_tibble()` rejected a `data.frame` with a conversion hint, so
tables from `read.csv()` or a PDF extractor failed on the first call.
It is now `as_tibble_input()`, which coerces any data frame to a
tibble and keeps non-automatic row names as a `rowname` column, since
a tibble has none and study labels would otherwise be lost in silence.
Anything that is not a data frame is still an error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Make audit() reach every tier and guard study-level GRIM statistics
recent_commits.body:
* Sequence and total-n output carries the basic mapper's class after
its tier classes, so `audit()` dispatched to the basic method, which
counted the dispersed rows as reported cases and only printed a hint.
`audit.scrutiny_map_seq()` and `audit.scrutiny_map_total_n()` now call
`audit_seq()` and `audit_total_n()`.

* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_plot_rates()` reject sequence and total-n
output through `check_grim_map_basic()`: their rows are hypothetical
value sets, inconsistent by construction, so a p-value or rate over
them said nothing about the study, and was returned without a word.

* `check_audit_special()` is removed and `audit_cols_minimal()` loses
`name_test`; both only served the hint that `audit()` no longer needs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix the review items of Oct 25
recent_commits.body:
* function_map() marked its error about a .fun whose arguments shadow
its internals as internal, which asked the user to report a bug. A user's
.fun with an argument named `data` triggers it, so it now goes through
abort_in_export() like the other checks at creation.

* map_value_sets() returns an empty vector for a wrapper with no formals
instead of failing on an empty cache key.

* .gitignore: `special-scripts/` made the three entries after it
redundant.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename vectorize_test() to map_value_sets()
recent_commits.body:
* It returns values, not a function, so it is no kind of Vectorize(); and
it serves grim_values(), grim_closest(), add_up_to(), and
is_percentage_of() too, which are no consistency tests.
* Drop the `frame` argument: it is always the caller's frame.
* Cache the missing() calls by the formals' names rather than the name the
wrapper was called under, which needed an identity check and an
empty-name branch. This makes fn_name_from_call() unused, so remove it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: test: pin that an unavailable Camelot patch is recorded; use a placeholder id in the hygiene-guard probe
recent_commits.body:
The two Camelot patch installers (cell join, row-boundary tie) return False
when Camelot is absent or has changed shape; their scopes record an
unavailable event. Nothing asserted that, so the capability could vanish with
every table test green. Three tests now pin the event on both scopes and its
absence on a healthy install.

The hygiene guard's positive probe quoted a real-looking private ledger id.
It now uses a placeholder with the same shape.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): the non-statistic scan folds a soft hyphen to nothing, not to a dash
recent_commits.body:
S6 deletes U+00AD, so a URL with soft hyphens correctly becomes the clean URL.
The scan folded U+00AD to '-' and reported that strip as a rewritten URL on two
corpus papers, exiting 1 on a healthy tree. Adds a regression test with a
red control.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

change, all at that heading. Canary audited in-session (6 papers; this was

recent_commits.message: test(perf): measure the interpreter itself, not a Windows venv launcher, in the CPU budget
recent_commits.body: Under a Windows virtual environment sys.executable is a launcher that starts the base interpreter as its child, so the measured process burned no CPU (0.016 s after 1.5 s of spinning) and no budget could fire. The base interpreter is now started directly with __PYVENV_LAUNCHER__, which runs it as the same venv in one process. test_cpu_budget: 3 failed -> 8 passed under the venv; 8 passed under the system interpreter before and after.

recent_commits.message: Read two-column pages by region, and turn the general column reorder on by default
recent_commits.body:
The left-then-right reorder of interleaved pages now runs behind a region
plan. The page body is cut at full-width blank bands; a table across the
gutter, or two two-column blocks stacked apart or in different type, leaves
the page in pdftotext's order, and a full-width table above or below the
columns is read in place. Bands with text on one side only join the column
flow. The column crops also give a rotated margin watermark its own crop when
a figure in the body has a rotated axis title.

Measured over the 125-paper corpus manifest against base: 190 pages in 55
papers change, every one a pure reorder (same words and characters), each
adjudicated by reading the page. DOCPLUCK_COLUMN_CORRECT_GENERAL=0 turns the
general path off. The banded path stays off.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Count the sample SD's reason in GRIMMER's audit() under "either"
recent_commits.body:
* When both SDs fail for different reasons, either could count. The
population SD's did, on the grounds that it decides the verdict, but
that only holds at n = 1, where the reason names it alone. The sample
SD's counts now, as under the default sd_type.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix edge cases in utility functions
recent_commits.body:
* row_to_colnames() made a tibble with duplicate names from a header
that repeats, as in "M, SD, M, SD", which only failed further down. It
is now an error that suggests a second header row.
* duplicate_tally() and duplicate_detect() counted NaN as a value, while
duplicate_count() dropped it. value_to_string() now keeps NaN missing.
* duplicate_tally() and duplicate_detect() gave the output a column name
twice if data had a column like x_n next to x. That is now an error.
* audit() of an empty duplicate_count() had an na_rate of NaN; it is NA
like the other statistics.
* decimal_places("1e400") was 0, and restore_zeros() padded the string.
A number too large for a double is an infinity, so it has NA decimal
places and is left as it is.
* add_up_to() gave verdicts on counts beyond 2^53, where a sum is no
longer exact: add_up_to(c(1e20, 1), 1e20) was TRUE. Such cases are NA.
* An empty string in sep of the parentheses functions is an error
rather than NA with a stringi warning.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count each "either" case once in GRIMMER's audit()
recent_commits.body:
* Under sd_type = "either", a reason can name the sample SD's failure
and the population SD's, and audit() counted the case under both, so
fail_grim, fail_test1, and fail_test3 added up to more than the
inconsistent cases. Only the population SD's reason counts now: it is
the one that decides the verdict.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the Poisson binomial tails exactly
recent_commits.body:
* grim_binomial() took the upper tail as 1 - poibin::ppoibin(), which
cancels to 0 below about 1e-16: 60 consistent rows at a null probability
of 0.5 gave p = 0 rather than 0.5^60, and 100 rows gave a larger p-value
than 60. ppoibin() itself bottoms out there as well, so both functions
now build the distribution by adding one trial at a time and sum each
tail from its far end. poibin is no longer suggested.
* grim_binomial_power() compares p-values to alpha with the tolerance of
stats::binom.test(), so an outcome whose p-value equals alpha rejects.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Vectorize grim_values() and grim_closest() like grim()
recent_commits.body:
* Both were Vectorize() wrappers, so a rounding of length 2 silently
returned two values, mismatched lengths were recycled with only a
warning, and zero-length input gave list() from grim_closest(). They now
share vectorize_test() with the tests, which gains a type argument for
their list and double returns.
* grim_closest() keeps a consistent x to the means that would be
reported as x, even where a closer one rounds to something else, as
under rounding = "floor". The docs said "whether or not x is
consistent"; they now say what the function does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Infer the dispersion step from diff_var in reverse_map_seq()
recent_commits.body:
* For a variable without a digits_* column, the step was taken to be the
smallest gap between two dispersed values. That gap is two steps wide
when the reported value is left out, as with dispersion = 1, and more
with dispersion = c(2, 4, 6), so reverse_map_seq() and audit_seq()
failed when such a variable was dispersed alone. The step is now the
distance between two values divided by their difference in diff_var.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave undecidable splits out of audit_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* A split whose both_consistent is NA was counted in scenarios_total but
never as a hit, so a case that could not be tested at all had a hit_rate
of 0, just like an inconsistent one. It now counts as neither, as in
audit_seq(), and a case with no decidable split has a hit_rate of NA.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Disperse n down to 1 for population SDs in sequence mappers
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_seq() and debit_map_seq() kept n at 2 or above, which a
sample SD needs but a population SD does not (#95). A .var_bounds element
of function_map_seq() may now be a function of the args that .fun
recorded, so the floor follows sd_type.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named argument for every setting
recent_commits.body:
* `function_map_seq()` and `function_map_total_n()` now copy the settings
of `.fun`, i.e. its formals after the dots, such as `rounding`,
`formula`, or `sd_type`, with `.fun`'s defaults, as `function_map()`
does for the basic mappers. They used to go through the dots, hidden
from `formals()`, tab completion, and the help page. Only the settings
given are forwarded, so `fun_args` still records what the caller gave.

* `sd_type` and DEBIT's `formula` list their values in the signature,
e.g. `formula = c("exact", "mean_n")`, and are checked with
`arg_match_in_export()` against `SD_TYPES` and `DEBIT_FORMULAS`. A test
requires every default to equal its constant.

* `function_map()` resolves such a default to its first value before the
length check, so the test function and the "scrutiny" attribute see a
single string.

* The dots of every mapper take nothing now, and their docs say so
instead of claiming to pass arguments on.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give the population SD's verdict under "either" at n = 1
recent_commits.body:
* A single value has no sample SD, only a population SD of 0, so
`sd_type = "either"` is now `TRUE` if the sample SD passes and otherwise
the population SD's verdict. That equals `|` everywhere else, but at
`n = 1` it gave `NA` instead of `FALSE` for an SD that no single value
can have.

* `grimmer_plot_values()` no longer needs to switch to `"population"`
at `n = 1` to avoid teeth without a verdict.

* The explanations say that a single value has no sample SD, state the
population SD's requirement when neither SD can be tested, and use the
singular for one value.

* `explain_either()` and `grimmer_either()` are now `explain_sd_either()`
and `grimmer_sd_either()`, since "either" alone could also mean a
rounding direction.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let DEBIT test population SDs (#95)
recent_commits.body:
* `debit()`, its mappers, and `debit_explain()` take `sd_type` as
GRIMMER does. The population SD of binary data has `n * n` in place of
`n * (n - 1)`, under both `formula = "exact"` and `"mean_n"`.

* `debit_plot()` reads `sd_type` from the "scrutiny" attribute and draws
the line and the attainable means of that SD, or of both under
`"either"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let GRIMMER test population SDs (#95)
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer()`, its mappers, `grimmer_explain()`, and
`grimmer_plot_values()` have a new `sd_type` argument: `"sample"` (the
default), `"population"`, or `"either"`. A population SD divides by `n`
rather than `n - 1`, which is a single integer factor in
`sd_square_term()`, so the test stays exact. The minimum and parity tests
don't depend on the convention.

* `"either"` runs the test under both conventions and combines the
verdicts with `|`. The `reason` column names the convention that passed.

* `sd_type` is checked with `arg_match_in_export()`, whose fast path
costs a tenth of a bare `rlang::arg_match()` on every row.

* A population SD makes `n = 1` testable, so the explanation now reads
correctly for a single value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): guard the new running-head and furniture-number rules against real content
recent_commits.body:
Independent review of normalization 1.9.75 / table extraction 2.4.25 found inputs on which each rule
took content for furniture; each is now a test (tests/test_running_head_and_furniture_guards.py).

- Running heads: page numbers folded off a head must be distinct and rise with the page ("Study 1" /
  "Study 2" are headings); a line carrying a statistic or comparison is never taken; the alternating
  rule needs three pages after page 1 and reads parity from the pages present; nothing is stripped
  on page 1, where a line equal to the head is the title.
- Furniture numbers: only the grid's single bare ASCII page number in its first or last row; an axis
  column needs most ticks alone in their row, so years or a Likert key beside labels stay data.
- Public repo: cite consumer requests by date, not by correspondence message id; the hygiene test
  now detects that id shape.

Census on the final rules: 225 papers, 117 changed, every removed line a running head/footer or
download stamp; 125 papers, 66 uncaptioned candidates set aside in 11, all furniture.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Count the sample SD's reason in GRIMMER's audit() under "either"
recent_commits.body:
* When both SDs fail for different reasons, either could count. The
population SD's did, on the grounds that it decides the verdict, but
that only holds at n = 1, where the reason names it alone. The sample
SD's counts now, as under the default sd_type.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix edge cases in utility functions
recent_commits.body:
* row_to_colnames() made a tibble with duplicate names from a header
that repeats, as in "M, SD, M, SD", which only failed further down. It
is now an error that suggests a second header row.
* duplicate_tally() and duplicate_detect() counted NaN as a value, while
duplicate_count() dropped it. value_to_string() now keeps NaN missing.
* duplicate_tally() and duplicate_detect() gave the output a column name
twice if data had a column like x_n next to x. That is now an error.
* audit() of an empty duplicate_count() had an na_rate of NaN; it is NA
like the other statistics.
* decimal_places("1e400") was 0, and restore_zeros() padded the string.
A number too large for a double is an infinity, so it has NA decimal
places and is left as it is.
* add_up_to() gave verdicts on counts beyond 2^53, where a sum is no
longer exact: add_up_to(c(1e20, 1), 1e20) was TRUE. Such cases are NA.
* An empty string in sep of the parentheses functions is an error
rather than NA with a stringi warning.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count each "either" case once in GRIMMER's audit()
recent_commits.body:
* Under sd_type = "either", a reason can name the sample SD's failure
and the population SD's, and audit() counted the case under both, so
fail_grim, fail_test1, and fail_test3 added up to more than the
inconsistent cases. Only the population SD's reason counts now: it is
the one that decides the verdict.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the Poisson binomial tails exactly
recent_commits.body:
* grim_binomial() took the upper tail as 1 - poibin::ppoibin(), which
cancels to 0 below about 1e-16: 60 consistent rows at a null probability
of 0.5 gave p = 0 rather than 0.5^60, and 100 rows gave a larger p-value
than 60. ppoibin() itself bottoms out there as well, so both functions
now build the distribution by adding one trial at a time and sum each
tail from its far end. poibin is no longer suggested.
* grim_binomial_power() compares p-values to alpha with the tolerance of
stats::binom.test(), so an outcome whose p-value equals alpha rejects.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Vectorize grim_values() and grim_closest() like grim()
recent_commits.body:
* Both were Vectorize() wrappers, so a rounding of length 2 silently
returned two values, mismatched lengths were recycled with only a
warning, and zero-length input gave list() from grim_closest(). They now
share vectorize_test() with the tests, which gains a type argument for
their list and double returns.
* grim_closest() keeps a consistent x to the means that would be
reported as x, even where a closer one rounds to something else, as
under rounding = "floor". The docs said "whether or not x is
consistent"; they now say what the function does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Infer the dispersion step from diff_var in reverse_map_seq()
recent_commits.body:
* For a variable without a digits_* column, the step was taken to be the
smallest gap between two dispersed values. That gap is two steps wide
when the reported value is left out, as with dispersion = 1, and more
with dispersion = c(2, 4, 6), so reverse_map_seq() and audit_seq()
failed when such a variable was dispersed alone. The step is now the
distance between two values divided by their difference in diff_var.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave undecidable splits out of audit_total_n()
recent_commits.body:
* A split whose both_consistent is NA was counted in scenarios_total but
never as a hit, so a case that could not be tested at all had a hit_rate
of 0, just like an inconsistent one. It now counts as neither, as in
audit_seq(), and a case with no decidable split has a hit_rate of NA.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Disperse n down to 1 for population SDs in sequence mappers
recent_commits.body:
* grimmer_map_seq() and debit_map_seq() kept n at 2 or above, which a
sample SD needs but a population SD does not (#95). A .var_bounds element
of function_map_seq() may now be a function of the args that .fun
recorded, so the floor follows sd_type.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named argument for every setting
recent_commits.body:
* `function_map_seq()` and `function_map_total_n()` now copy the settings
of `.fun`, i.e. its formals after the dots, such as `rounding`,
`formula`, or `sd_type`, with `.fun`'s defaults, as `function_map()`
does for the basic mappers. They used to go through the dots, hidden
from `formals()`, tab completion, and the help page. Only the settings
given are forwarded, so `fun_args` still records what the caller gave.

* `sd_type` and DEBIT's `formula` list their values in the signature,
e.g. `formula = c("exact", "mean_n")`, and are checked with
`arg_match_in_export()` against `SD_TYPES` and `DEBIT_FORMULAS`. A test
requires every default to equal its constant.

* `function_map()` resolves such a default to its first value before the
length check, so the test function and the "scrutiny" attribute see a
single string.

* The dots of every mapper take nothing now, and their docs say so
instead of claiming to pass arguments on.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give the population SD's verdict under "either" at n = 1
recent_commits.body:
* A single value has no sample SD, only a population SD of 0, so
`sd_type = "either"` is now `TRUE` if the sample SD passes and otherwise
the population SD's verdict. That equals `|` everywhere else, but at
`n = 1` it gave `NA` instead of `FALSE` for an SD that no single value
can have.

* `grimmer_plot_values()` no longer needs to switch to `"population"`
at `n = 1` to avoid teeth without a verdict.

* The explanations say that a single value has no sample SD, state the
population SD's requirement when neither SD can be tested, and use the
singular for one value.

* `explain_either()` and `grimmer_either()` are now `explain_sd_either()`
and `grimmer_sd_either()`, since "either" alone could also mean a
rounding direction.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let DEBIT test population SDs (#95)
recent_commits.body:
* `debit()`, its mappers, and `debit_explain()` take `sd_type` as
GRIMMER does. The population SD of binary data has `n * n` in place of
`n * (n - 1)`, under both `formula = "exact"` and `"mean_n"`.

* `debit_plot()` reads `sd_type` from the "scrutiny" attribute and draws
the line and the attainable means of that SD, or of both under
`"either"`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let GRIMMER test population SDs (#95)
recent_commits.body:
* `grimmer()`, its mappers, `grimmer_explain()`, and
`grimmer_plot_values()` have a new `sd_type` argument: `"sample"` (the
default), `"population"`, or `"either"`. A population SD divides by `n`
rather than `n - 1`, which is a single integer factor in
`sd_square_term()`, so the test stays exact. The minimum and parity tests
don't depend on the convention.

* `"either"` runs the test under both conventions and combines the
verdicts with `|`. The `reason` column names the convention that passed.

* `sd_type` is checked with `arg_match_in_export()`, whose fast path
costs a tenth of a bare `rlang::arg_match()` on every row.

* A population SD makes `n = 1` testable, so the explanation now reads
correctly for a single value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test GRIMMER against an exact oracle at two decimal places for n up to 12
recent_commits.body:
* The sums and sums of squares that `n` whole numbers can have are found
by dynamic programming, which reaches sample sizes that enumerating the
samples cannot. Reported pairs at two decimal places are far sparser than
at one, so this is a sharper check of the exact verdict for `n >= 5`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare numbers written out in full in the duplicate functions
recent_commits.body:
* `duplicate_count()`, `duplicate_tally()`, `duplicate_detect()`, and
`duplicate_count_colpair()` compared values via `as.character()`, which
writes a double in scientific notation when that is shorter but never an
integer. An integer column and a double column holding `100000` therefore
had no duplicate at that value, and `0.0001` did not duplicate `"0.0001"`.

* All four now spell values with `value_to_string()`, which writes numbers
out in full. `duplicate_count()` keeps its factor levels in the former
order, so values with the same frequency are listed as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write numbers out in full instead of in scientific notation
recent_commits.body:
* `number_to_string()` now writes a number that `as.character()` puts in
scientific notation, such as `1e+05` or `1e-04`, out in full, with the
fewest significant digits that convert back to the same number.

* `restore_zeros()` reads a numeric `x` through it rather than through
`as.character()`, so it counts decimal places as `decimal_places()` does.
`restore_zeros(1e-300, width = 300)` used to be an error, since the value
was read as `9.99999999999999e-301` with 315 decimal places, and
`c(1e-300, 1)` was padded to 315 places.

* Both help pages say that numbers with more than 15 significant digits
cannot be handled accurately, which only `decimal_places()` said before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep the grouping test from warning about an excluded column
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Suggest the basic mapper's arguments for an abbreviation in a sequence mapper
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_map_seq(round = "up")` got no suggestion, because the hint only searched
the mapper's own formals and `rounding` is one of `grim_map()`'s. An unnamed
argument after the key arguments, which the dots now take, is reported as such
instead of as an invalid argument with an empty name and a list of every formal.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test GRIMMER against a brute force under every rounding method and two items
recent_commits.body:
* The random brute force covered `"up_or_down"` with one item only. The same
reachable sums and sums of squares, rounded forward with `reround()`, now serve
as the oracle for every rounding method, with `"even"` taken to round a tie
either way, and for two items averaged, where the whole numbers are the
respondents' totals. The pairs are built by a shared helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the next attainable sum of squares for two numbers instead of scanning
recent_commits.body:
* `sum_squares_attainable()` allocated the whole range of sums of squares with
`seq()`, which runs into the hundreds of millions with many items averaged, and
scanned it for squares, which are too sparse to find that way. For one or two
numbers, the next attainable value is now computed directly; for three or four,
the scan runs step by step and ends soon, as most values are attainable.
`grimmer()` with `n = 3` and `items_averaged = 50000` took over a second and
takes a few milliseconds.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Put the mappers' dots right after the key arguments
recent_commits.body:
* Every argument after the dots must now be named in full. `items = 2` partially matched `items_averaged`, the argument renamed from `items` because the old name was misread as the number of scale points; it now reaches the dots and fails with a hint at the full name.
* The total-n mappers get an `n` key argument for the column of totals. `n = "total"` used to fail with base R's "argument matches multiple formal arguments", since `n` partially matched `n_min` and `n_max`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep total-n constant values with their groups in the back direction
recent_commits.body:
* The "back" direction swaps the groups, but `constant` was passed on unchanged, so a label for the group of `x1` stood next to `x2`. It is now swapped like the `digits_*` values.
* The total-n mappers document what `constant` means for them: values that belong to the groups of `x1` and `x2`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count decimal places of numbers near the ends of the double range as written
recent_commits.body: * `as.character()` wrote `1e-300` as "9.99999999999999e-301", so `decimal_places()` counted 315 decimal places. Scientific notation that uses all 15 significant digits is now replaced by the shortest string that converts back to the same number, in `decimal_places()` and `decimal_places_scalar()` alike.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the string "NA" as missing in is_numeric_like()
recent_commits.body: * `decimal_places()` and `restore_zeros()` take it as missing, but `is_numeric_like()` did not, so the `*_df()` functions skipped any column that contained it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Document that duplicate_tally() and duplicate_detect() compare strings
recent_commits.body: * Both coerce every value to a string, so a number and the string that it prints as are duplicates, and the output columns are strings. This was undocumented.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show the sequence mappers' real var default in their usage
recent_commits.body: * `var = Inf` was a sentinel for "all reported variables", resolved in the body, so the usage lines showed `Inf` where the docs said `c("x", "n")`. `function_map_seq()` now defaults `.var` to `.reported`, which the manufactured functions show as it is.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the one exported decimal-counting function in the devtools vignette
recent_commits.body: * It spoke of two such functions, but `decimal_places_scalar()` is internal.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject impossible input to the sd_binary_*() functions
recent_commits.body:
* A negative count, a count above `n`, or a mean outside of 0 and 1 gave `NaN` without a word. They are now errors.
* An `n` below 2 now gives `NA` by assignment rather than by multiplying `NaN` with `NA`, which R may resolve either way.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject factors where numbers are required
recent_commits.body:
* `check_type()` compared `typeof()`, which is "integer" for a factor, so a factor `n` column passed and failed in base R ("'round' not meaningful for factors"). Every numeric type check now rejects factors, naming the type.
* `is_seq_dispersed()` compared `x` to a factor `from`'s level code rather than its label.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Ignore grouping in the *_df() functions
recent_commits.body:
* `decimal_places_df()`, `restore_zeros_df()`, and `split_by_parens()` were never meant to take grouping into account. They now ungroup `data`, treat every column alike, and return ungrouped data.
* `regroup()` is gone. It put groups back after 65e61ec and, since b18b576, skipped grouping columns and kept `.drop` and row-wise grouping.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep testthat's failure record out of the build
recent_commits.body: * A failed run leaves `tests/testthat/testthat-problems.rds`, which `R CMD build` still packed; d7ecf96 only covered the `_problems` directory.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fixes for #506 and #523: output search limit, sandbox folders, writes beside the script, SPSS encoding (0.4.1.3)
recent_commits.body:
- reproducibility_check searches only the first 20,000 lines of a script's
  printed output for statistical results (option
  metacheck.repro_output_max_lines) and says so in the report (#523, item 2).
  On the SURF server sq8y6's script was stopped after 300 s as it should be,
  but the search through its printed output then kept the job busy until the
  60-minute job limit.
- Docker sandbox: R's cache, configuration and data folders are put in /tmp
  (the home folder is read-only, so renv::restore() stopped), and
  RSTUDIO_PANDOC points to the Pandoc Quarto has in the image (#523, items 4
  and 5).
- Package layout: a quoted relative path whose folder exists from the
  script's own or .Rproj folder, but not from the top, is rewritten to its
  path from the top, so writes beside the script work and later scripts find
  the file (#523, item 3).
- codebook_check: mapply(USE.NAMES = FALSE), so an NA variable name no longer
  stops it with "row names contain missing values" (#523, item 1).
- .sav files with Windows (CP1252) text are read again as CP1252 (#523,
  item 6).
- dryad_info(cache = TRUE) does not reuse listings stored before the paging
  fix of 0.3.3.1, or marked incomplete (#506).

recent_commits.message: Add functions for PsyArXiv's own API (psyarxiv_*)
recent_commits.body:
PsyArXiv now has its own read-only API (https://next.psyarxiv.org/api,
no key). New functions next to the OSF route, which is unchanged:
psyarxiv_search() (full-text search, filters, paging), psyarxiv_info()
(full records: data/prereg/materials statements, COI, supplements
project, file links), psyarxiv_versions(), psyarxiv_author(),
psyarxiv_download(), psyarxiv_dumps()/psyarxiv_dump() (yearly bulk
files), psyarxiv_subjects(), psyarxiv_licenses(). Ids are OSF guids;
links and PsyArXiv DOIs are accepted. The address is the option
metacheck.psyarxiv.api. Tests use recorded answers in
apis/next.psyarxiv.org; downloads are tested live (skipped on CRAN).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): guard the new running-head and furniture-number rules against real content
recent_commits.body:
Independent review of normalization 1.9.75 / table extraction 2.4.25 found inputs on which each rule
took content for furniture; each is now a test (tests/test_running_head_and_furniture_guards.py).

- Running heads: page numbers folded off a head must be distinct and rise with the page ("Study 1" /
  "Study 2" are headings); a line carrying a statistic or comparison is never taken; the alternating
  rule needs three pages after page 1 and reads parity from the pages present; nothing is stripped
  on page 1, where a line equal to the head is the title.
- Furniture numbers: only the grid's single bare ASCII page number in its first or last row; an axis
  column needs most ticks alone in their row, so years or a Likert key beside labels stay data.
- Public repo: cite consumer requests by date, not by correspondence message id; the hygiene test
  now detects that id shape.

Census on the final rules: 225 papers, 117 changed, every removed line a running head/footer or
download stamp; 125 papers, 66 uncaptioned candidates set aside in 11, all furniture.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize,tables): guard the new running-head and furniture-number rules against real content
recent_commits.body:
Independent review of normalization 1.9.75 / table extraction 2.4.25 found inputs on which each rule
took content for furniture; each is now a test (tests/test_running_head_and_furniture_guards.py).

- Running heads: page numbers folded off a head must be distinct and rise with the page ("Study 1" /
  "Study 2" are headings); a line carrying a statistic or comparison is never taken; the alternating
  rule needs three pages after page 1 and reads parity from the pages present; nothing is stripped
  on page 1, where a line equal to the head is the title.
- Furniture numbers: only the grid's single bare ASCII page number in its first or last row; an axis
  column needs most ticks alone in their row, so years or a Likert key beside labels stay data.
- Public repo: cite consumer requests by date, not by correspondence message id; the hygiene test
  now detects that id shape.

Census on the final rules: 225 papers, 117 changed, every removed line a running head/footer or
download stamp; 125 papers, 66 uncaptioned candidates set aside in 11, all furniture.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.

  but the search through its printed output then kept the job busy until the
  60-minute job limit.

  (the home folder is read-only, so renv::restore() stopped), and
  RSTUDIO_PANDOC points to the Pandoc Quarto has in the image (#523, items 4
  and 5).
- Package layout: a quoted relative path whose folder exists from the
  script's own or .Rproj folder, but not from the top, is rewritten to its
  path from the top, so writes beside the script work and later scripts find
  the file (#523, item 3).
- codebook_check: mapply(USE.NAMES = FALSE), so an NA variable name no longer
  stops it with "row names contain missing values" (#523, item 1).
- .sav files with Windows (CP1252) text are read again as CP1252 (#523,
  item 6).
- dryad_info(cache = TRUE) does not reuse listings stored before the paging
  fix of 0.3.3.1, or marked incomplete (#506).

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.

recent_commits.body:

64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.

recent_commits.message: Give sequence and total-n mappers a named `items_averaged` argument
recent_commits.body:
* Both factories now copy the helper arguments of `.fun`, as recorded in its `"scrutiny_args_helper"` attribute, with the defaults they have there. `items_averaged` was passed through the dots, where it was required but invisible to `formals()`, to tab-completion, and to the help pages. It now follows the key arguments, as in the basic mappers.

* The ones given are collected at the very start of the body, before any local variable could shadow one, and passed on to `fun()`. A missing one is left out, so that it reaches `fun()` as missing and the bespoke error still fires. The sequence mapper passes them to its initial `fun()` call only; the re-tests read them from the column that call returned.

* The rename hint in `check_factory_dots()` is gone again: `items` now partially matches the named argument in these mappers as well, so the dots never see it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say that `items` was renamed where the dots see it
recent_commits.body:
* The basic mappers and test functions match `items` to `items_averaged` by partial matching, but the sequence and total-n mappers take it through the dots, which only said that `items` is no valid argument. `check_factory_dots()` now adds that it was renamed.

* The `...` docs of these mappers say that `items_averaged` must be among the dots unless `data` has such a column, and test titles use the new name.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say which columns precede `consistency` in the mapper requirements
recent_commits.body: * The vignette said that `consistency` follows the key and helper columns, and that its index is their number plus one. The `digits_*` columns sit to its left as well, which the counting rule missed. Now that `items_averaged` is always returned, the count is off in every GRIM and GRIMMER mapper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Rename `items` to `items_averaged` without a default, close #94
recent_commits.body:
* `items` was mistaken for the number of scale points, and its default of 1 let multi-item scales be tested as single items without anyone noticing. Like `digits_x`, the renamed argument must now be stated in every GRIM and GRIMMER function, or given as an `items_averaged` column in the mappers. `grim_granularity()` keeps its default.

* A missing `items_averaged` calls `error_items_missing()`, which explains the argument and says that it replaces `items`. It fires after the `digits_*` checks.

* `manage_helper_col()` can be called without `default`, for helper arguments that have none. `function_map()` does that for such arguments and leaves required arguments out of the length check, so that a missing one reaches `fun()` as missing.

* Mapper output now always has an `items_averaged` column, which changes the expected shapes in many tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Cut GRIMMER's scale bounds, close #88
recent_commits.body:
* `min_val` and `max_val` are gone from `grimmer()`, `grimmer_map()`,
`grimmer_explain()`, and `grimmer_plot_values()`, along with the
`fail_scale` column of `audit()` and the comb's third tooth state. They
were never released, so no deprecation is needed.

* strait already covers this ground: `brimmer()` flags every case the
bounds flagged, and `brimmest()` decides exactly. strait imports
scrutiny and never passed the bounds on any branch. `?grimmer` and the
GRIMMER vignette now point there.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

Full suite on eccd3fa: 5 failed / 3796 passed. Two timing tests failed under machine load and pass

dehyphenated "WellBeing" that W0o now restores to the printed "Well-Being". The blank-header test

recent_commits.message: fix(diag): render_deletion_scan counts a table-text copy that yields to its grid separately
recent_commits.body:
QA 3c on v2.4.153 flagged 76 lines in 6 papers deleted by _suppress_orphan_table_cell_text; every
number of them is in an emitted <table>. The "survives near the same position" rule cannot see a grid
placed elsewhere. A step output carrying a table-text-duplicate marker folds out its removed lines
only when their combined numbers (the scan's own tokenizer, with multiplicity) are all in the
<table> blocks; they are printed as YIELDED TO GRID, never silently. A planted missing value and a
duplicated value still fail the fold.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.153 - W0o compound hyphens, table-text duplicate yields to its grid, flattened CI level is the table's own
recent_commits.body:
normalization 1.9.73, table extraction 2.4.23. Corpus (101 manifest PDFs): 313 hyphen restorations,
64 duplicate markers in 30 papers with 0 numbers lost, 69 of 10,713 flattened rows change level.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): W0o leaves a glued span two compounds claim; test that ranges tokenize as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 3 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on c55b34c: pooling sites per prefix let `re-sent`
and `res-ent` both rewrite one glued `resent`, giving `re-sentres-ent` (reproduced). A span with
two claims is ambiguous, so neither fires. Also pins that `2008–2013` and `2008-2013` tokenize as
2008 and 2013 in the table-text duplicate coverage test.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix: W0o never hyphenates a word the page prints glued; table-text duplicate compares every label and symbol
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult round 2 (Sonnet, 2026-10-13), each finding reproduced before the fix:
- W0o: the "printed glued" test compared whole layout words, so a glued word inside a
  space-less pdfplumber token was missed. 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.103977 p9 prints "nonmoral"
  and 10.1109/access.2024.3358206 p14 prints "multimodal" (rasterized); both rendered
  hyphenated. The test now searches every hyphen-free letter stretch (NFKC-folded) of every
  layout word.
- W0o: one line-end "A-" fragment licensed a site in every compound starting A (annals
  human-: 13 sites, 6 fragments). Sites are now pooled per prefix against the fragments.
- table-text duplicate: Greek letters, single-letter labels (p, F, d) and the symbols
  * x ~ != + are compared too; grid tokens come only from grids that survive the later
  phantom-table strip.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(render): table-text duplicate compares operators, needs specific values, reads ranges as ranges
recent_commits.body:
Tier-2 consult (Sonnet, 2026-10-13) on ad36764: coverage ignored < > = +- * daggers %, a run of small
integers could be covered by coincidence, and 12-15 tokenized as 12 and -15. Operators/markers are
now a multiset that must be covered, a run needs 3+ values with a decimal or 3+ digits, and a minus
after a word character or dot is a dash. Canary: ip_feldman Table 2 plain caption is italicized
in the duplicate arm as in the deletion arm.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.body:
Full suite on eccd3fa: 5 failed / 3796 passed. Two timing tests failed under machine load and pass
alone (5.8 s). CITATION.cff and README cited 2.4.152. The ip_feldman heading test asserted the
dehyphenated "WellBeing" that W0o now restores to the printed "Well-Being". The blank-header test
